sources.title: *Second National Communication under the UNFCCC* (UNFCCC1)
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical mainly 1951-2010; projections to 2100
sources.methodology: GSWP3 reanalysis; CORDEX regional models; seven-model ensembles; vulnerability/capacity assessment
sources.limitations: Older model generation; precipitation uncertainty high; institutional information predates August 2021.

sources.title: *Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Afghanistan* (NUPI3)
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly 2021-2026; climate series to 2024/projections to mid-century
sources.methodology: Literature/secondary-data synthesis and climate-security pathway framework
sources.limitations: Not a causal-identification study; several statistics derive from secondary sources; local examples cannot support national causal claims.

sources.title: *Afghanistan: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis, September 2025-September 2026* (IPCinfo7)
sources.temporal_coverage: Sep 2025-Sep 2026
sources.methodology: IPC consensus classification drawing on food security, livelihood, market, climate and humanitarian data
sources.limitations: Classification/projection, not causal evaluation; climate is one of several drivers.

sources.title: *Afghanistan Socioeconomic Review, 2024-2025* (UNDP2)
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly 2024-2025
sources.methodology: WoAA July-Aug 2025 plus administrative/UN sources; bespoke Subsistence Insecurity Index
sources.limitations: Cross-sectional survey evidence; some indices are UNDP constructs; some subgroup analysis restricted to common provinces.

sources.title: *Afghanistan Development Update* (The World Bank9)
sources.temporal_coverage: FY2025 and medium-term projections
sources.methodology: Macroeconomic estimation, administrative sources, World Bank datasets and 2025 Enterprise Survey
sources.limitations: Macro estimates and projections; cannot isolate climatic effects from returns, borders, policy, aid and other drivers.

sources.title: *World Bank & Afghanistan Resilience Trust Fund Support for the People of Afghanistan* (World Bank10)
sources.temporal_coverage: Since Aug 2021
sources.methodology: Administrative programme description, financing and monitoring arrangements
sources.limitations: World Bank fact sheet dated 26 September 2024; describes intended/current delivery and monitoring architecture, not independent evidence of outcomes or adaptation effectiveness.

sources.title: *Adapting Afghan Communities to Climate-Induced Disaster Risks - Terminal Evaluation* (Evaluation Resource Center6)
geographic_coverage: Project communities, mainly Nangarhar and Jawzjan plus institutional components
sources.temporal_coverage: Project 2017-Aug 2021; evaluation 2023
sources.methodology: Document review and stakeholder consultation by an external evaluator
sources.limitations: Activities suspended Aug 2021 and never resumed; nearly two-year gap; mainly remote evaluation; incomplete information for some cost-effectiveness questions.

sources.title: *Final Evaluation of UNDP GEF-LDCF2 Project Afghanistan: Strengthening the resilience of rural livelihood options...* (Evaluation Resource Center11)
sources.temporal_coverage: Apr 2014-Sep 2019
sources.methodology: Evaluation team review, fieldwork, stakeholder interviews and project monitoring evidence
sources.limitations: Security constrained field access; Uruzgan implementation/evaluation evidence was particularly constrained; weak indicators and M&E limit outcome attribution.

sources.title: *Crisis Compounded: Afghanistan’s Returnees Face an Escalating Water Emergency* (Mercy Corps4)
sources.temporal_coverage: Mid-Sep 2025
sources.methodology: Survey of 292 returnee households plus secondary research
sources.limitations: Local sample; many causal attributions are respondent perceptions or report synthesis; groundwater stress has climatic and non-climatic drivers.

sources.title: *No place to stay, no place to go: perspectives from climate-affected areas of Balkh province* (ACAPS12)
geographic_coverage: Dehdadi, Nahr Shahi, Sholgareh districts, Balkh
sources.temporal_coverage: Fieldwork Jun 2025
sources.methodology: Secondary review + experts + purposive qualitative study of 84 participants, interviews/FGDs/households, thematic analysis
sources.limitations: Purposive local study; translation and access limitations; unsuitable for estimating prevalence or national effects.

sources.title: *After return: Rebuilding livelihoods for Afghan women* (ecoi.net13)
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly late 2025-Apr 2026
sources.methodology: Telephone survey of 582 returnee women, 80 qualitative participants, participatory market work
sources.limitations: Cross-sectional/self-reported; phone frame may exclude women without phones or in highly restrictive households; small earnings subsample; no causal inference. The PDF states CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 IGO; reuse must comply with attribution, non-commercial and no-derivatives terms.

sources.title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Afghanistan
sources.organization: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) and Norwegian Institute of International Affairs (NUPI)
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate observations through 2024; displacement and socioeconomic conditions through 2025; selected projections to 2039-2050
sources.methodology: SIPRI/NUPI fact sheet synthesizes climate, conflict and security evidence.
sources.limitations: Secondary synthesis; climate rarely drives conflict.

sources.title: Favorable harvest temporarily improves food access despite lingering drought impacts
sources.temporal_coverage: July 2026-January 2027 food security outlook; 2026 harvest and late-July flooding
sources.methodology: FEWS NET update summarizes current food insecurity and geographic projections.
sources.limitations: High-level outlook page; projected food security outcomes are not a climate attribution analysis and are limited to the stated forecast period.

sources.title: Two in three Afghan households show resilience gains in last year
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
sources.temporal_coverage: Household resilience assessment results for 2023-2024; interventions since 2021
sources.methodology: FAO publisher summary reports E-RIMA resilience changes among supported households.
sources.limitations: Summary omits sampling and comparison details; findings are not nationally representative.

sources.title: Report of the Secretary-General on the activities of the United Nations Regional Office for Central Africa (S/2025/772)
sources.organization: United Nations Secretary-General / United Nations Office for Central Africa
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional climate conditions in June–August 2025 and a reported Namibe incident on 17 August 2025.
sources.methodology: UN Secretary-General's regional political and humanitarian reporting, including climate-service information.
sources.limitations: The report gives no independent causal assessment or names for the communities involved.

sources.title: Nationally Determined Contribution of Angola 2025 (NDC 3.0)
sources.organization: Republic of Angola, Ministry of Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate assessments and adaptation priorities, with historical examples and plans through 2035.
sources.methodology: NDC reviews national climate and sector plans.
sources.limitations: Commitments are not independently evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: Eastern and Southern Africa Region Humanitarian Situation Report No. 2, 1 January–31 December 2024
sources.organization: UNICEF Eastern and Southern Africa Regional Office
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional and Angola situation and response reporting for calendar year 2024, with some cited water-point data from 2022.
sources.methodology: Regional UNICEF situation report aggregates country-office needs and response reporting.
sources.limitations: Some water-point estimates are dated; the report gives limited local disaggregation.

sources.title: Angola Preparedness for Resilient Recovery Project: First Project Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Project progress and disaster-preparedness activities reported for September 2014–September 2015.
sources.methodology: UNDP project progress report records preparedness, training and recovery-assessment activities.
sources.limitations: It is a first-year report; many subsequent provincial and municipal plans were targets, not verified results.

sources.title: Angola Food Security Outlook, June 2026–January 2027: Likely El Niño-induced dryness to lead to outcomes aligned with Crisis in southern areas by November
sources.temporal_coverage: Current food-security conditions through June 2026 and outlook through January 2027.
sources.methodology: FEWS NET synthesizes weather, crop, market, livelihood and nutrition evidence.
sources.limitations: Not a census; some nutrition surveillance is not representative.

sources.title: Western Balkans 6: Albania Country Climate and Development Report Compendium
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate and socioeconomic data, historical hazards through 2023, municipal hazard rankings and policy review.
sources.methodology: World Bank compendium combines climate, infrastructure and socioeconomic data, scenario analysis and policy review.
sources.limitations: Municipal scores are aggregate and modeled; they are not household-level risk or conflict estimates.

sources.title: Albania's National Adaptation Plan 2026–2036
sources.organization: Government of Albania, Ministry of Environment, with UNDP and Green Climate Fund support
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate risks and an adaptation framework for 2026–2036; municipal plans developed during 2022–2024.
sources.methodology: National plan synthesizes sector and municipal climate-risk assessments and prioritizes adaptation measures.
sources.limitations: Municipal profiles summarize underlying plans; targets and risk ratings are not independent implementation evaluations.

sources.title: Local Climate Change Adaptation Plan for Shkoder Municipality: Project Summary
sources.temporal_coverage: Local adaptation planning project delivered June–October 2025.
sources.methodology: One-page summary from the implementing institute reports plan outputs and partners.
sources.limitations: The summary does not include the full hazard analysis or independently evaluated adaptation results.

sources.title: ALBAdapt: Climate-Resilient Urban Development Programme
sources.organization: Republic of Albania, Ministry of Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: Programme components and expected beneficiaries reported in July 2026.
sources.methodology: Ministry programme announcement describes planned components and expected reach; text translated from Albanian.
sources.limitations: Programme intentions and beneficiary targets are not measured results.

sources.title: Argentina's Second Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development, Argentine Republic
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate trends mainly cover 1960–2010; the Adaptation Communication also summarizes regional vulnerabilities and end-century RCP8.5 projections.
sources.methodology: Second NDC Adaptation Communication summarizes climate observations, projections and regional vulnerabilities.
sources.limitations: Regional impacts draw on earlier assessments; dates, scenarios and local population data vary.

sources.title: Tools for understanding the dynamics of the 7 March 2025 flood in Bahía Blanca
sources.organization: Instituto Nacional del Agua, Hydraulic Laboratory, Argentina
sources.temporal_coverage: Technical analysis of the 7 March 2025 flood, using event observations and a preliminary hydrodynamic model.
sources.methodology: INA combines public-video flood marks, hydrological data and a 2D hydrodynamic model for the four urban watersheds.
sources.limitations: First version; sparse public observations and simplified channel/terrain inputs limit precision.

sources.title: Resolution 532/2025: Supplement for Reconstruction rules, updated text
sources.organization: Ministry of National Security, Argentine Republic
sources.temporal_coverage: Rules for the one-time housing recovery subsidy after the 7 March 2025 Bahía Blanca flood, including July 2025 amendments.
sources.methodology: Official legal text defines eligibility, payment zones, verification and monitoring procedures for the SUR subsidy.
sources.limitations: The regulation establishes program rules, not the number of eligible applicants, payments made or resulting recovery.

sources.title: Storm impacts and resources sent to Bahía Blanca
sources.temporal_coverage: Provincial emergency update at 18:00 on 7 March 2025.
sources.methodology: Provincial government emergency communication lists reported rainfall and resources deployed during the response.
sources.limitations: This is an event-day government update, not an independent evaluation or a record of final outcomes.

sources.title: National Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction 2025–2029
sources.organization: National System for Integral Risk Management and Civil Protection, Argentina
sources.temporal_coverage: National disaster-risk priorities and targets for 2025–2029.
sources.methodology: Government summary describes the plan's objectives, participatory formulation and expected 2029 results.
sources.limitations: The webpage reports planned objectives and expected results; it does not establish implementation or achievement.

sources.title: Water situation and runoff forecast for Mendoza, 2026–2027 season
sources.organization: Department General of Irrigation, Government of Mendoza Province
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed 2025–2026 runoff and provincial flow forecasts for the 2026–2027 water season.
sources.methodology: Provincial water authority reports seasonal river-flow forecasts based on year-round monitoring and nine automated stations.
sources.limitations: The webpage summarizes seasonal volumes and does not state uncertainty ranges or climate-model scenarios.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Armenia
sources.temporal_coverage: Country climate and development assessment with observed risk mapping and modeled climate, flood and poverty outcomes through 2060.
sources.methodology: Opened the full 89-page CCDR; it combines spatial risk assessment, flood maps, household data and economic scenarios.
sources.limitations: Mapped losses and projections are model-based; the report notes asset valuation uncertainty for flood-loss estimates.

sources.title: Fourth National Communication on Climate Change under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Armenia, with UNDP support
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate observations and hazard impacts through 2017; crop-yield projections through 2070; adaptation measures mainly reported through 2020.
sources.methodology: Opened the full government communication and reviewed its climate, agriculture and adaptation sections.
sources.limitations: The yield tables do not identify an emissions pathway; reported programs are historical and not independently evaluated.

sources.title: National Action Program of Adaptation to Climate Change and the List of Measures for 2021–2025
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Armenia, Ministry of Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: Government-approved adaptation action program for 2021–2025, with national and marz-level planning measures.
sources.methodology: Opened the government decree and annex listing adaptation measures, responsible agencies, timelines and indicative financing.
sources.limitations: The program states planned actions, not verified implementation or achieved outcomes; its 2021–2025 period has ended.

sources.title: United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework 2026–2030
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Armenia and United Nations Country Team
sources.temporal_coverage: Joint Government–UN strategy for 2026–2030, signed in Yerevan on 19 December 2025.
sources.methodology: Opened the signed framework and reviewed its national rationale and planned green-transition and disaster-risk measures.
sources.limitations: This is a planning framework, not an evaluation; it does not name pilot municipalities or estimate climate-related displacement.

sources.title: Armenia Floods: May 2024 Post-Disaster Needs Assessment
sources.organization: Government of Armenia, United Nations and European Union
sources.temporal_coverage: Multi-sector assessment of the May 25–26, 2024 floods, their impacts and recovery needs in Lori and Tavush.
sources.methodology: Opened the full Government–UN–EU assessment, including human impacts, gender, housing and disaster-risk sections.
sources.limitations: Event assessment; no attribution to anthropogenic climate change or evaluation of long-term recovery.

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda Drought Hazard Assessment and Mapping: Summary Report
sources.organization: Organization of American States / USAID Caribbean Disaster Mitigation Project
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical drought impacts and watershed conditions assessed in a 2001 technical summary.
sources.methodology: OAS hazard-mapping summary draws on secondary records, maps, consultations and limited field observations.
sources.limitations: The report is dated; rainfall and watershed data were limited, and it does not attribute drought impacts to anthropogenic climate change.

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda Inland Flood Hazard Mapping: Summary Report
sources.organization: Organization of American States / USAID Caribbean Disaster Mitigation Project
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical flood susceptibility and settlement conditions summarized in 2001.
sources.methodology: OAS technical summary maps inland flood hazards and describes watershed, soil, drainage and settlement factors.
sources.limitations: The maps were preliminary because rainfall, watershed and drainage data were limited; findings are not a current risk assessment.

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda: Rapid Needs Assessment following Hurricane Irma
sources.organization: Government of Antigua and Barbuda, with World Bank/GFDRR, United Nations and European Union
sources.temporal_coverage: Post-disaster damage, loss and recovery needs after Hurricanes Irma and Maria in September 2017.
sources.methodology: Joint government-partner recovery needs assessment; this source is its executive summary.
sources.limitations: Assessment records disaster impacts and recommended needs, not subsequent completion of recovery measures.

sources.title: Concluding observations on the combined fourth to seventh periodic reports of Antigua and Barbuda
sources.organization: United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women
sources.temporal_coverage: Committee observations following its 20 February 2019 review; includes consequences of Hurricane Irma and recovery concerns.
sources.methodology: Treaty-body concluding observations based on the State review and information considered by the Committee.
sources.limitations: The observations identify concerns and recommendations; they are not a quantitative assessment of all affected women or recovery outcomes.

sources.title: Capacity Building for Improved Transparency of Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation in Antigua and Barbuda: Terminal Review
sources.organization: United Nations Environment Programme / Global Environment Facility
sources.temporal_coverage: Terminal evaluation of the 2019–2024 CBIT project, with primary review work in October–November 2025.
sources.methodology: Full terminal review assesses project outputs, outcomes, performance and sustainability using document review and stakeholder evidence.
sources.limitations: This evaluates climate-data and reporting institutions, not household adaptation outcomes; sustainability ratings are evaluative judgments.

sources.title: National Adaptation Plan: Sectoral Adaptation Plans and Local Area Adaptation Plans
sources.organization: Department of Environment, Government of Antigua and Barbuda
sources.temporal_coverage: Government announcement on 8 July 2026 of national, sectoral and local adaptation plans.
sources.methodology: Department of Environment webpage summarizes the NAP, sectoral plans and named local planning areas.
sources.limitations: The announcement describes plans and participation, not implementation, financing or measured resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Azerbaijan’s Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Azerbaijan
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate trends, current adaptation measures and a regional vulnerability index for 2041–2069; mitigation target year 2035.
sources.methodology: Opened the 96-page NDC; reviewed regional-risk, climate, adaptation and reintegration sections.
sources.limitations: Government synthesis; index method and scenarios unspecified. Its occupation-era damage account is not independently verified.

sources.title: The Great Return
sources.organization: President of the Republic of Azerbaijan
sources.temporal_coverage: Dynamic government page on post-conflict return and reconstruction; includes return to Aghdam beginning in March 2025.
sources.methodology: Opened the government page and reviewed its coordination and Aghdam reconstruction sections.
sources.limitations: Government-reported plans and progress; dynamic page has no single publication date and does not independently evaluate outcomes.

sources.title: UNDP and ANAMA held a Side Event on Mine Action and Environmental Sustainability within COP29
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme in Azerbaijan
sources.temporal_coverage: Report of a COP29 side event held in Baku on 18 November 2024.
sources.methodology: Opened the full UNDP event report, including statements by ANAMA and UNDP representatives.
sources.limitations: Event statements; the report gives no independent soil sampling or evaluation of demining outcomes.

sources.title: Closing Ceremony Marks Completion of Project on Promoting Kahriz Rehabilitation for Climate Adaptation in Azerbaijan
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration, through United Nations in Azerbaijan
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports kahriz rehabilitation since 2000 and a project completed in March 2026.
sources.methodology: Opened the full IOM project-completion story and reviewed the reported outputs and capacity-development details.
sources.limitations: Reported project outputs are not an impact evaluation; the 20 districts are not identified and household outcomes are not disaggregated.

sources.title: 4th International Mine Action Conference: Humanitarian Demining for Urban Recovery
sources.organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator’s Office in Azerbaijan
sources.temporal_coverage: UN Resident Coordinator representative’s speech at a Baku conference on 2 September 2026; includes reported mine-action support during 2020–2025.
sources.methodology: Opened the complete speech and reviewed its return, land-release and national-capacity passages.
sources.limitations: The speech attributes figures to ANAMA and provides no calculation method or independent audit.

sources.title: Tackling Climate Change, Land Degradation and Fragility: Diagnosing Drivers of Climate and Environmental Fragility in Burundi’s Colline Landscapes: Towards a Multi-Sector Investment Plan to Scale up Climate Resilience
sources.organization: World Bank and Government of Burundi
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate series, mid-century projections, and spatial multi-risk assessment reported in 2022
sources.methodology: Combines climate projections, land-degradation modeling and spatial multi-risk analysis of 2,616 collines.
sources.limitations: Risk scores combine hazards, exposure, vulnerability, coping capacity and past conflict; they are not causal estimates. Rainfall projections vary.

sources.title: Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (INDC) / Burundi
sources.temporal_coverage: National vulnerability assessment and climate projections through 2050, as reported in 2015
sources.methodology: Summarizes prior national communications, an ACCES soil-and-water vulnerability analysis, and general circulation model projections.
sources.limitations: 2015 assessment using earlier studies; the cited projection passage does not name a scenario. Adaptation measures describe plans, not evaluated results.

sources.title: Burundi Colline Climate Resilience Project (P180864): Appraisal Environmental and Social Review Summary
sources.temporal_coverage: Appraisal-stage project context and proposed activities, 2024
sources.methodology: World Bank appraisal summarizes cited colline climate-risk mapping, targeting and proposed activities.
sources.limitations: Activities are proposed; cited risk analyses are summarized, not replicated.

sources.title: Climate Change, Internal Mobility, and Conflict Dynamics: Country Brief - Burundi
sources.temporal_coverage: Survey interviews May-July 2025; displacement experiences within the previous five years
sources.methodology: Original country brief analyzing 1,027 in-person 4Mi surveys with internally displaced people, collected in Bujumbura city, Cibitoke and Makamba city.
sources.limitations: Purposive sample focused on recent climate-linked movement and active mobility; results are illustrative, not representative. Cover date is April 2026, while the suggested citation inside the report says 2025.

sources.title: Burundi country strategic plan (2024-2027)
sources.temporal_coverage: Country strategic plan period 2024-2027; revision approved June 2026
sources.methodology: WFP country strategic plan page describing climate and food-security context, planned outcomes and government capacity support.
sources.limitations: The page states commitments and intended outcomes; it does not evaluate whether planned support has been delivered or caused results.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Benin
sources.temporal_coverage: EHCVM household survey 2018/19; climate projections including 2070
sources.methodology: CCDR analysis with EHCVM 2018/19 household shock estimates.
sources.limitations: EHCVM shocks are self-reported retrospectively; fragility passage gives no causal estimate.

sources.title: Benin Economic Update 2024: Adapting to climate change for sustainable, resilient economic growth
sources.temporal_coverage: Economic-loss projection through 2050; adaptation priorities for coming decades
sources.methodology: World Bank publisher summary of the 2024 Economic Update; projected losses are reported as estimates.
sources.limitations: The inspected summary does not state the model assumptions or climate scenario behind the GDP estimate.

sources.title: Troisième Contribution Déterminée au niveau National du Bénin (CDN 3.0)
geographic_coverage: Coastal zone and five seafront communes
sources.temporal_coverage: Agricultural statistics through 2025; climate risks and planned adaptation measures in NDC 3.0
sources.methodology: Government NDC submission describing sectoral climate vulnerabilities, exposure and planned projects.
sources.limitations: Project listings are commitments, not evidence of implementation or effectiveness; coastal erosion rates apply to critical locations.

sources.title: Benin Context Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Country context and food-security conditions through 2025; report published June 2026
sources.methodology: FEWS NET synthesizes Benin's hazard, livelihood and security context.
sources.limitations: High-level synthesis; conflict details and climate attribution are limited.

sources.title: Gulf of Guinea Northern Regions Social Cohesion Project (P175043), Additional Financing Request 2: Project Information Document
sources.temporal_coverage: Context data current to December 2024; appraisal-stage project design in February 2025
sources.methodology: World Bank appraisal for northern Benin social-cohesion financing, context and proposed actions.
sources.limitations: Context is not outcome evaluation; measures are proposals.

sources.title: Updated National Adaptation Plan - Burkina Faso
sources.organization: Government of Burkina Faso and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
sources.temporal_coverage: Updated national adaptation planning framework current at March 2025.
sources.methodology: The government planning document consolidates national climate risks, sector priorities, institutions, and proposed adaptation actions.
sources.limitations: A policy plan records priorities and intended actions rather than independently evaluated implementation results.

sources.title: Climate Change and Violent Conflict in West Africa: Assessing the Evidence
sources.temporal_coverage: Academic literature available for the systematic review published in February 2022.
sources.methodology: A systematic literature review assesses four mediated climate-insecurity pathways and the strength of the regional evidence base.
sources.limitations: The review finds a limited research base and does not support deterministic or uniformly national causal claims for Burkina Faso. The prior candidate marked this source open, but the 2026-10-26 review did not verify explicit licence terms at a stable locator.

sources.title: Countering climate-related security risks in the Sahel
sources.temporal_coverage: Research and stakeholder consultation supporting climate-security strategy development through 2024.
sources.methodology: CGIAR researchers investigated risk pathways and consulted national and regional stakeholders to validate findings and identify policy options.
sources.limitations: This results page summarizes research and consultation rather than publishing the full underlying evidence or evaluation design.

sources.title: Climate change and conflict pursue displaced Burkinabes
sources.organization: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
sources.temporal_coverage: Displacement, drought, livelihood, and 2020 flood conditions reported through January 2021.
sources.methodology: A UNHCR field story combines interviews, site observation, government displacement data, and cautious expert interpretation.
sources.limitations: Selected households and sites are not nationally representative; the source explicitly cautions against a direct climate-conflict attribution.

sources.title: Burkina Faso country overview
sources.temporal_coverage: Living country overview with current humanitarian and food-security indicators.
sources.methodology: WFP synthesizes operational monitoring, food-security analysis, displacement context, and program activities.
sources.limitations: A living operational page can change and mixes indicators with different reference dates; program descriptions are not independent evaluations.

sources.title: Evaluation of Burkina Faso WFP Country Strategic Plan 2019-2023
sources.organization: World Food Programme Office of Evaluation
sources.temporal_coverage: WFP activities from January 2018 through July 2022; evaluation conducted April 2022 to January 2023.
sources.methodology: The independent evaluation assessed relevance, strategic positioning, outcome contributions, efficiency, and explanatory factors across the country portfolio.
sources.limitations: The evaluation predates later conflict and climate developments and assesses WFP's portfolio rather than all national response systems. The prior candidate marked this source open, but the 2026-10-26 review did not verify explicit licence terms at a stable locator.

sources.title: Supporting Local Governments and Building Resilience in Burkina Faso
geographic_coverage: All 13 regions and 349 municipalities of Burkina Faso
sources.temporal_coverage: Local governance program results, with crisis-response results concentrated in August 2020 to September 2021.
sources.methodology: A World Bank results brief reports program monitoring data on decentralization, municipal capacity, service continuity, and assistance to displaced households.
sources.limitations: The implementing institution's results brief is not an independent impact evaluation and some outcomes coincide with COVID-19 response rather than climate action.

sources.title: Promoting peaceful transhumance in the Liptako-Gourma region
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
geographic_coverage: Liptako-Gourma areas of Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger
sources.temporal_coverage: Lessons from a joint FAO-IOM Peacebuilding Fund initiative implemented from 2020 to 2024.
sources.methodology: The good-practice product synthesizes implementation lessons from work with farmer organizations and national authorities on transhumance, governance, and cohesion.
sources.limitations: Regional lessons do not isolate Burkina Faso effects or establish independent causal impact. The prior candidate marked this source open, but the 2026-10-26 review did not verify explicit licence terms at a stable locator.

sources.title: Farming communities in Burkina Faso are improving their agricultural practices with innovative weather tools
sources.temporal_coverage: Hydromet implementation and farmer rain-gauge distribution since 2023.
sources.methodology: A project feature reports administrative monitoring, training coverage, institutional roles, and selected participant accounts.
sources.limitations: The page reports outputs and testimonials rather than independent effectiveness or distributional evaluation.

sources.title: Burkina Faso Key Message Update September 2026–January 2027: Agropastoral production prospects negatively affected by El Niño conditions
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed 2026 rainy-season conditions and food-security projections through January 2027.
sources.methodology: FEWS NET key-message monitoring and food-security projections.
sources.limitations: High-level regional summary; it does not attribute violence to climate.

sources.title: Burkina Faso: Fourth Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement, Financing Assurances Review, and Request for an Arrangement Under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed context through late 2025; reform program runs through September 2027.
sources.methodology: IMF staff review of the ECF arrangement and RSF request, including macroeconomic analysis and policy discussions.
sources.limitations: The farmer-herder/conflict statement is a national-level narrative, not a localized causal estimate; reform measures are commitments, not evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: Humanitarian Action for Children 2026: Burkina Faso
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 displacement and service data, 2026 humanitarian needs and planned response.
sources.methodology: Appeal aligns with the 2026 HNRP and participatory JIAF 2.0 analysis.
sources.limitations: Reports needs estimates and planned activities, not outcomes; names unchanged.

sources.title: National bulletins vs the ASAP trigger — September 2026
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, Centre for Humanitarian Data
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 rainy season, with comparison to the JRC ASAP trigger record since 2001.
sources.methodology: OCHA compares JRC ASAP alerts with summaries of ANAM bulletins and a July 2026 SAP-GTP field mission.
sources.limitations: Underlying bulletins and mission findings are summarized, not republished; station and historical coverage are weak in the action area.

sources.title: Quatre Plans d’Action Anticipatoire pour agir avant la sécheresse au Burkina Faso [Four Anticipatory Action Plans to act before drought in Burkina Faso]
sources.temporal_coverage: Summary of four anticipatory-action plans covering 2025–2027.
sources.methodology: Oxfam summarizes four community-developed anticipatory-action plans and links their detailed PDFs.
sources.limitations: Only the summary page was accessible; it documents planned actions, not implementation or results.

sources.title: Environmental and Social Management Framework: Resilient Urban and Territorial Development Project (RUTDP), Volume 1: Main Report
sources.organization: Local Government Engineering Department, Government of Bangladesh
sources.temporal_coverage: Project context in 2024; first project phase planned for 2024-2030.
sources.methodology: Government project ESMF based primarily on the feasibility study and available secondary data.
sources.limitations: Subproject locations and designs were not finalized at preparation; the framework does not report completed outcomes.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Bangladesh Background Note, Environment, Natural Resources and Blue Economy
geographic_coverage: Chittagong Hill Forests in the east
sources.temporal_coverage: Bangladesh CCDR 2022 background note drawing on studies published in different years.
sources.methodology: CCDR background note synthesizing cited studies on ecosystems, coastal hazards, forests, and livelihoods.
sources.limitations: Evidence combines referenced studies with different dates and methods; this note is not a new field survey.

sources.title: Water and Health: Impact of Climate Change in Bangladesh
sources.organization: World Bank Group, Health, Nutrition, and Population Global Practice
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical studies summarized in a September 2022 discussion paper.
sources.methodology: Summarizes water and health studies by the six ecological zones used in the government Delta Plan 2100.
sources.limitations: The paper describes findings from prior studies and identifies zone-level differences; it is not a new epidemiological survey.

sources.title: Strengthening Disaster Risk Management and Community Resilience in Cox's Bazar
sources.temporal_coverage: Programme reported as implemented since October 2022 and completed in November 2025; page undated.
sources.methodology: UNDP page summarizes risk context, activities and reported results.
sources.limitations: Not an impact evaluation; some targets may not be completed activities.

sources.title: Safe Access to Fuel and Energy Plus, Phase 2 (SAFE+2): Annual Programme Narrative Progress Report, Reporting Period 1 January-31 December 2024
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization, International Organization for Migration, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and World Food Programme
geographic_coverage: Sadar, Ramu, Ukhiya and Teknaf upazilas
sources.temporal_coverage: Programme progress reported for 1 January-31 December 2024.
sources.methodology: 2024 resilience programme report.
sources.limitations: Outcomes unevaluated; no climate-tension attribution.

sources.title: Gender Alert: Bangladesh Monsoon Flood, Flash Flood and Landslide Risks (12 July 2026)
sources.organization: Gender in Humanitarian Action Bangladesh and UN Women
sources.temporal_coverage: Situation and risk update dated 12 July 2026; portal publication date 14 July 2026.
sources.methodology: Alert draws on local GiHA reports and inter-sector flash-flood updates.
sources.limitations: Acute snapshot, not a long-term model; some risks are anticipated.

sources.title: 2025-26 Joint Response Plan: Rohingya Humanitarian Crisis, Bangladesh
sources.organization: Government of Bangladesh, United Nations and humanitarian partners
sources.temporal_coverage: Two-year humanitarian response plan for January 2025-December 2026; needs and context include 2024 events.
sources.methodology: Inter-agency plan synthesizes needs, context and activities for refugees and hosts.
sources.limitations: Context and plans are not evaluated outcomes; tensions are not attributed to climate.

sources.title: Bulgaria's Biennial Transparency Report 2024 under the Paris Agreement
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate and hydrology across source-stated historical periods; future climate-health vulnerabilities; adaptation institutions through 2024.
sources.methodology: Government BTR compiles national climate, hydrological and sector evidence.
sources.limitations: Periods vary; future projections are uncertain.

sources.title: Overlooked: Examining the Impact of Disasters and Climate Shocks on Poverty in the Europe and Central Asia Region
sources.temporal_coverage: Bulgaria case study of the June 2014 flood, published in a 2021 regional report.
sources.methodology: World Bank regional poverty and disaster report; Bulgaria's case box synthesizes cited event sources.
sources.limitations: The Bulgaria box cites secondary references and does not reproduce an underlying local assessment.

sources.title: Disasters, Accidents, Incidents and Crises in 2024: Final Data
sources.temporal_coverage: Final event and expenditure statistics for 2024, with selected comparisons to 2023.
sources.methodology: Official NSI release presenting final annual counts of crisis events, declared disasters, geographic coverage and public expenditure.
sources.limitations: Categories include non-climate crises and accidents; the release does not attribute events to climate change or disaggregate household impacts.

sources.title: The Water Crises of Bulgaria: Analysis and Solutions (Summary)
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate observations include 1991–2020; water-sector indicators are reported as current in the March 2026 summary; irrigation figures include 2024.
sources.methodology: MOEW minister/deputy-minister report summary drawing on climate observations and water-sector/operator statistics.
sources.limitations: Summary-level government analysis; figures use varied periods and some operator records are not externally verifiable.

sources.title: Country Report Bulgaria 2026 (Staff Working Document and Annexes)
sources.organization: European Commission, Directorate-General for Economic and Financial Affairs
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 country analysis; mixed indicators from 2013–2025 and adaptation programming for 2021–2027.
sources.methodology: European Commission country staff working document synthesizing Bulgarian and EU indicators, policy documents and implementation evidence; Annex 10 addresses adaptation and preparedness.
sources.limitations: Indicators use different reference periods; reported plans and coverage are not household-level outcome measurements.

sources.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina National Adaptation Plan – NAP with proposed measures
sources.organization: Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations of Bosnia and Herzegovina, with UNDP and entity ministries
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate analysis through 2018, historical hazards, and projections through the end of the 21st century.
sources.methodology: Synthesizes climate records, sector studies and climate-model projections.
sources.limitations: The plan notes pending national analyses; proposed measures are not implementation evidence.

sources.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina Floods, 2014: Recovery Needs Assessment
sources.organization: Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina with the European Union, United Nations and World Bank
sources.temporal_coverage: Assesses the 14–19 May 2014 floods and recovery needs identified by June 2014.
sources.methodology: Authorities, EU, UN and World Bank combined records, visits and rapid surveys.
sources.limitations: Findings use information available by June 2014.

sources.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina Disaster Resilience Scorecard Assessment and Public Health Scorecard Addendum Analysis: Gaps, Challenges and Recommendations
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports local scorecards and DRR activities during 2021–2022.
sources.methodology: UNDRR analyzed municipal self-assessments and public-health scorecards.
sources.limitations: Selected local self-assessments, not an independent implementation evaluation.

sources.title: INFORM Subnational Risk Index for Bosnia and Herzegovina: Findings on natural hazard exposure, vulnerability and coping capacities, and recommendations for disaster risk management
sources.organization: United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security, guided by the European Commission Joint Research Centre INFORM methodology
sources.temporal_coverage: Municipal index published June 2026; includes historical disaster and war-legacy indicators.
sources.methodology: Aggregates 43 public-data indicators across 143 municipalities.
sources.limitations: DRR capability and humanitarian coping indicators were excluded for insufficient data.

sources.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina Floods Response – Multi-Cluster Initial Rapid Assessment
sources.organization: United Nations in Bosnia and Herzegovina, coordinated by the International Organization for Migration
sources.temporal_coverage: Rapid assessment of the 4 October 2024 storm, based on interviews conducted 2–6 November 2024.
sources.methodology: Light assessment based on 87 local key-informant interviews.
sources.limitations: Indicative sample; figures not independently verified.

sources.title: Report on the technical review of the eighth national communication and the fifth biennial report of Belarus
sources.organization: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change expert review team
sources.temporal_coverage: Reviews Belarus's NC8 and BR5 submissions for 2022; expert review held in October 2023.
sources.methodology: Full 37-page UNFCCC expert technical review; cited claims are what Belarus reported in NC8/BR5, not new independent monitoring.
sources.limitations: NC8 reporting summarized by the expert review team; plans described in 2022–2023 are not verified after publication.

sources.title: Towards Water Security in Belarus: A Synthesis Report
sources.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical river records through 2015; local water-system data mainly from 2018–2019; selected projections through 2035.
sources.methodology: Opened the English report; reviewed hydrology, regional cases and Kopyl.
sources.limitations: Synthesis uses older local datasets; the cited 2035 projection has no emissions pathway.

sources.title: Climate Change and Security in Eastern Europe: Regional Assessment
sources.organization: Environment and Security Initiative (OSCE, UNDP, UN Environment, UNECE and REC)
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional assessment based on desk review and consultations in 2014 and 2016; published 2017.
sources.methodology: Opened the full 51-page regional assessment; it combines desk studies, national consultations and joint analyst review.
sources.limitations: Published 2017; evidence mixes desk studies and expert consultation and does not establish a violent event caused by climate.

sources.title: Peatland rehabilitation as a response to drought and sand storms in Belarus: Experience of UN Convention to Combat Desertification
sources.organization: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports local climate and land conditions and peatland activities from 2017–2020, with later project targets as announced in 2020.
sources.methodology: Read the full UNCCD library article by Jamal Annagylyjova, including reported local cases and project status.
sources.limitations: Partner article, not an independent evaluation; completed work and second-phase targets are status as reported in 2020.

sources.title: Adapting to the Unpredictable: Belarusian Farmers Navigate the Consequences of Climate Change
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme in Belarus
sources.temporal_coverage: Country climate context and a Brahin district farm case, published in 2024.
sources.methodology: Read the full UNDP Belarus story and project description; used only the Brahin farm case.
sources.limitations: One human-interest farm story, not a representative sample or an impact evaluation.

sources.title: Belize prepares for current and future emergencies
sources.temporal_coverage: Reported 2014-2021 project activities and 2019 drought.
sources.methodology: Implementer's results brief.
sources.limitations: Self-reported activities; pandemic support is not proof of climate-adaptation impact.

sources.title: Belize's wildfires: Indigenous leadership for climate resilience
sources.temporal_coverage: May 2024 wildfires and subsequent community response.
sources.methodology: Staff account with Maya community-leader testimony.
sources.limitations: Qualitative local reporting; no independent event-attribution or causal evaluation.

sources.title: Resilience and conservation in a changing climate: The case of Belize
sources.temporal_coverage: Marine conservation and adaptation activities reported in 2021.
sources.methodology: Implementer feature describing ecosystem and livelihood interventions.
sources.limitations: Reported outputs and testimony are not independent long-term livelihood or peace outcomes.

sources.title: Climate Risk Profile: Belize
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 profile; mixed historical observations, projections and community assessment findings.
sources.methodology: Desk research and community participation across selected protected-area landscapes.
sources.limitations: Selected CAPA sites; qualitative conflict pathways are unquantified.

sources.title: CORVI: Measuring Multidimensional Climate Risks in Belize City, Belize
sources.temporal_coverage: Assessment published January 2025; includes expert views and data collected through December 2024.
sources.methodology: CORVI combines desk research, 93 expert surveys and 20 interviews.
sources.limitations: Expert-scored Belize City case study; not national or causal.

sources.title: United Nations Belize Common Country Analysis 2021
sources.organization: United Nations Belize, Office of the Resident Coordinator
sources.temporal_coverage: 2021 country analysis; underlying indicators and events span multiple source periods.
sources.methodology: Joint UN analysis; thematic groups scored risks by probability and development impact and consulted stakeholders.
sources.limitations: Dated 2021 analysis; risk ratings and program statements are not measured outcomes.

sources.title: Belize Second National Communication to the Conference of the Parties of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
sources.organization: Government of Belize, Ministry of Natural Resources and the Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: Prepared 2009 and edited through May 2012; includes projections for 2028, 2050 and 2100 and regional water assessments.
sources.methodology: Government sector assessments using climate models and sector studies.
sources.limitations: Old projections and observations; not current measurements.

sources.title: Bolivia: Rural Community Flood and Drought Resilience in the Bolivian Highlands
sources.temporal_coverage: EVAs project implementation in 2011–2017; terminal evaluation in 2017; post-completion assessment in 2023; regional climate modeling through 2070.
sources.methodology: Five-page case study synthesizes project-close and 2023 post-completion evaluations.
sources.limitations: Regional evaluation synthesis, not a representative climate-impact survey.

sources.title: Impacts of Wildfires on Economic, Social, Cultural and Environmental Rights and Biodiversity: Report of REDESCA's Working Visit to Bolivia
sources.organization: Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, Office of the Special Rapporteur on Economic, Social, Cultural and Environmental Rights (REDESCA)
sources.temporal_coverage: Examines the 2024 wildfire emergency; REDESCA mission conducted 9–11 December 2024; report approved 30 May 2025.
sources.methodology: Mission to La Paz, Santa Cruz and San Ignacio; reviewed official information and community testimony.
sources.limitations: Field mission, not a representative survey or fire-attribution study.

sources.title: De la emergencia a la gestión de riesgos por sequía: el caso de las ciudades de La Paz y El Alto en Bolivia y sus lecciones aprendidas
sources.organization: Inter-American Development Bank, Water and Sanitation Division
sources.temporal_coverage: Reviews the 2016–2017 and 2022–2023 drought episodes, the EPSAS drought-management protocol introduced in 2018, and system operation through 2024.
sources.methodology: Full 114-page Spanish note using EPSAS operational data.
sources.limitations: Provider case study; household impacts unmeasured.

sources.title: Adaptation Planning in Bolivia
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Accelerator Lab Bolivia
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports on a UNDP Accelerator Lab adaptation-planning prototype; page does not state implementation dates.
sources.methodology: Read the full case study describing deliberative workshops, a community survey and co-designed planning map.
sources.limitations: The case is explicitly a prototype/pilot, not an evaluation of institutionalized or scaled adaptation outcomes.

sources.title: Bolivia, Country Strategic Outcome 2: Decentralized Evaluation (2023–2025)
sources.organization: World Food Programme, Office of Evaluation
sources.temporal_coverage: Evaluation covers WFP Bolivia Country Strategic Plan outcome implementation from January 2023 through December 2024.
sources.methodology: Read the complete official evaluation synopsis page; its linked evaluation PDF required JavaScript bot verification and was not read.
sources.limitations: Claims are limited to the posted synopsis; detailed evaluation methods and findings were not verified in the PDF.

sources.title: Brazil Country Climate and Development Report: Executive Summary
sources.temporal_coverage: Current climate-risk diagnostic, historical loss estimates and modeled poverty impacts through 2030.
sources.methodology: Executive summary distills modeled national climate risks, poverty pathways and sector and institutional options.
sources.limitations: Only the 14-page executive summary was used; projections do not establish local incidence.

sources.title: Severe droughts reduce river navigability and isolate communities in the Brazilian Amazon
sources.organization: Communications Earth & Environment; authors from Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais and partner research institutions
sources.temporal_coverage: Settlement datasets dated 2020-2021; reported drought impacts from 2000-2020; hydrological series assessed through 2021.
sources.methodology: Maps settlement proximity to rivers and roads, codes reported drought impacts and analyzes 90 river-gauge time series.
sources.limitations: Media-reported impacts are incomplete; distance screening indicates isolation risk, not observed isolation for each settlement.

sources.title: Climate-related Crisis in the Amazon Region: Flash Update No. 1, Reporting Period August-September 2024
sources.organization: UNICEF Latin America and Caribbean Regional Office
sources.temporal_coverage: Situation and response snapshot for August-September 2024, with near-term risks and planned UNICEF actions.
sources.methodology: Flash update combines state, Indigenous-organization and humanitarian coordination data with UNICEF response monitoring.
sources.limitations: Dated situation snapshot; some population and service figures are relayed from third parties, not a prevalence study.

sources.title: Impact of drought in the Brazilian Amazon and 2025 outlook
sources.temporal_coverage: Secondary review of the 2023-2024 drought and humanitarian access conditions, with outlook for 2025.
sources.methodology: Seven-page thematic report based on review of public secondary sources.
sources.limitations: Remote-area needs and access data are explicitly scarce; armed-group information is synthesized from cited sources.

sources.title: Impacts of the Floods in Rio Grande do Sul: Observations and Recommendations for the Guarantee of Economic, Social, Cultural, and Environmental Rights
sources.organization: Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, Special Rapporteurship on Economic, Social, Cultural and Environmental Rights (REDESCA)
sources.temporal_coverage: Mission conducted December 2-6, 2024, documenting impacts and response to the April-May 2024 floods.
sources.methodology: December 2024 mission, meetings with authorities, civil society, scientists and affected communities, plus document review.
sources.limitations: State-specific mission; reported figures draw partly on administrative and secondary sources, not a representative survey.

sources.title: National Disaster Preparedness Baseline Assessment: Barbados
sources.temporal_coverage: 2024 national disaster-preparedness risk and vulnerability assessment with parish-level exposure, vulnerability and capacity composites.
sources.methodology: Opened the complete 124-page assessment, reviewing hazard exposure, parish vulnerability, island capacity and disaster-management findings.
sources.limitations: The maps and composite scores are multi-hazard assessments, not climate-specific causal estimates or records of observed losses.

sources.title: The Barbados Integrated Coastal Zone Management Plan, Volume 2, Segment 2
sources.organization: Coastal Zone Management Unit, Government of Barbados
sources.temporal_coverage: Volume 2 Part B and Part C of the coastal management plan dated October 2020; includes coastal risk assessment summaries and guidance for future management.
sources.methodology: Opened full 127-page Part B/C segment, including risk summaries, SWOT and national guidance.
sources.limitations: Part D sub-area maps were not reviewed; damage estimates use dated asset data and the plan is not an implementation evaluation.

sources.title: Barbados Voluntary National Review 2023
sources.organization: Government of Barbados, Office of the Prime Minister
geographic_coverage: southern and western coastal urban corridor
sources.temporal_coverage: Government SDG progress review submitted in 2023; includes 2021 Hurricane Elsa impacts and summaries of coastal-risk and resilience initiatives.
sources.methodology: Opened the full 246-page national review and read its climate, disaster-impact, coastal-risk and adaptation-program passages.
sources.limitations: The review summarizes other assessments and administrative reports; older figures and stated initiatives are not independently evaluated here.

sources.title: Barbados – Beryl Emergency Response and Recovery Project: Project Information Document
sources.temporal_coverage: Appraisal-stage project document covering Hurricane Beryl impacts in 2024, immediate recovery actions and the proposed emergency-response project.
sources.methodology: Opened the 16-page appraisal PID on Beryl impacts, sector context, response and project objectives.
sources.limitations: Appraisal PID, not completion evaluation; it cites Fisheries Division damage figures and does not attribute Beryl to climate change.

sources.title: Participatory Recovery Planning Workshop
sources.temporal_coverage: Fisherfolk survey findings and a community-recovery planning workshop held on 22 January 2026 after Hurricane Beryl.
sources.methodology: Opened the full agency post summarizing PACIFICO survey findings and the January 2026 workshop with landing-site representatives.
sources.limitations: The post does not provide the survey sample size, instrument, site-level results or sex-disaggregated findings.

sources.title: Barbados Coastal Fisheries Resilience
sources.temporal_coverage: Japan-funded UNDP coastal-fisheries recovery initiative following Hurricane Beryl; the project page reports a March 2025 start, December 2027 end and ongoing status.
sources.methodology: Opened the UNDP project page and reviewed its background, objectives, expected results, dates and status.
sources.limitations: The page describes intended outputs and reports ongoing status, not evaluated outcomes; its estimate of vessel damage differs from the World Bank PID.

sources.title: Bhutan Second Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.temporal_coverage: Second NDC covering 2021-2030.
sources.methodology: Government NDC describing national climate context, institutions, and planned mitigation and adaptation actions.
sources.limitations: Policy submission; planned actions are not evaluated outcomes, and the inspected passages do not quantify local hazard exposure.

sources.title: Assessment of Climate-Induced Loss and Damage in Bhutan
sources.temporal_coverage: Assessment published in 2026; includes a documented October 2025 extreme-weather event.
sources.methodology: Review of secondary documents, key-informant group interviews, stakeholder workshop, and field visits.
sources.limitations: The report notes limited primary datasets and dispersed institutional knowledge; the inspected 2025 event passage reports impacts but does not attribute the event to climate change.

sources.title: Adaptation, Climate Resilience, and Diversification Key to Creating Jobs, Accelerating Growth in Bhutan
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank publication page dated 2025; reports modeled risks through 2050.
sources.methodology: Official World Bank release summarizing findings and recommendations from its Bhutan Country Climate and Development Report.
sources.limitations: The press-release summary does not provide underlying model specifications; the qualitative hotter-and-drier scenario is not assigned a named pathway.

sources.title: Climate Change Vulnerability Analyses and Mapping for National Adaptation Plan Formulation Process in Bhutan
sources.organization: Royal Government of Bhutan and United Nations Development Programme Bhutan
sources.temporal_coverage: Dzongkhag indicators mainly from 2005-2017 and hazard records from 2010-2018; future risk modeled at five-year intervals to 2050.
sources.methodology: Dzongkhag indices combine government hazard/socioeconomic indicators and stakeholder input.
sources.limitations: Older sparse local data limit temporal/causal precision; projections exclude wildcard events.

sources.title: Kingdom of Bhutan, First National Adaptation Plan 2023
sources.organization: Department of Environment and Climate Change, Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources, Royal Government of Bhutan
sources.temporal_coverage: National adaptation priorities and implementation needs for the medium and long term; document published in 2023.
sources.methodology: The NAP synthesizes four sectoral risk assessments and national and regional stakeholder consultations.
sources.limitations: Adaptation priorities are policy commitments, not verified nationwide service outcomes.

sources.title: Mid Term Review of Advancing Climate Resilience of the Water Sector in Bhutan (ACREWAS)
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme and Royal Government of Bhutan, Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport
sources.temporal_coverage: Midterm review submitted in February 2026 for a project running from September 2023 to September 2028.
sources.methodology: Non-experimental review used documents, interviews, focus groups and observations.
sources.limitations: Midterm project evidence; some water-access and watershed outcomes were not yet delivered.

sources.title: Republic of Botswana: World Bank Group Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Country climate-development diagnostic published in 2025; combines historical observations and referenced studies with current-risk overlays and scenarios extending to 2050.
sources.methodology: Climate/poverty analysis with mapped overlays.
sources.limitations: Mixed vintages; noncausal overlays.

sources.title: National Drought Plan: Republic of Botswana
sources.organization: Republic of Botswana, prepared by Nnyaladzi Batisani under the UNCCD Drought Initiative
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical droughts through the 2020 plan; includes a 2015 vulnerability assessment, RCP4.5/8.5 projections and proposed 2020-2023 actions.
sources.methodology: National drought-risk synthesis and proposed sectoral governance actions.
sources.limitations: Uses a 2015 risk assessment; recommendations are not evaluated implementation or current status.

sources.title: Makgadikgadi Framework Management Plan 2010, Volume 2, Chapter 5: Wildlife Resources and Human Wildlife Conflict
sources.organization: Department of Environmental Affairs, Government of Botswana, with the Centre for Applied Research
sources.temporal_coverage: Assesses historical and current-at-the-time wildlife and human-wildlife conflict patterns, with focus groups in April-May 2010.
sources.methodology: Combines DWNP Problem Animal Control records, multi-year aerial counts, spatial mapping and 18-22-person focus groups in four villages.
sources.limitations: The report warns aerial counts vary in coverage and may substantially undercount; focus-group findings are historical and site-specific.

sources.title: Human-wildlife conflict a growing challenge
sources.organization: Botswana Daily News / Botswana Press Agency, reporting an Acting Director of the Department of Wildlife and National Parks briefing
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports a February 2025 briefing, including national wildlife-conflict figures for 2022-2024.
sources.methodology: Government newspaper account of an Acting DWNP Director's Ntlo ya Dikgosi briefing; incident figures are attributed to the speaker.
sources.limitations: Not an independent incident dataset; the account provides national statements without named hotspots.

sources.title: Gender and Equity Considerations for Building Climate Resilience: Lessons from Rural and Periurban Botswana
sources.organization: Kutlwano Makwatse, Leatile Modie, Morati Mpalo and Caitlin Blaser Mapitsa; Sustainability (MDPI)
sources.temporal_coverage: Household baseline research in Xhumaga and Ramotswa, reported in 2022; exact fieldwork dates are not stated.
sources.methodology: Participant-coded household narratives and survey with 141 residents in Xhumaga and Ramotswa, followed by community feedback meetings.
sources.limitations: Quasi-random qualitative sample, not statistically representative; fieldwork dates are unstated and participant data are restricted on ethical grounds.

sources.title: Central African Republic - Climate Fact Sheet 2024
sources.organization: Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical observations; projections to mid-century and beyond
sources.methodology: Desk synthesis drawing substantially on World Bank/IPCC-type climate evidence
sources.limitations: Not an original modelling study; some projections are regional rather than CAR-specific; rainfall/drought uncertainty is substantial.

sources.title: Plan national initial d’adaptation aux changements climatiques de la République centrafricaine
sources.temporal_coverage: Current planning horizon at publication and future adaptation planning
sources.methodology: Government policy process, sector reviews, consultations and adaptation planning
sources.limitations: Policy intentions do not demonstrate implementation or outcomes; several planned enabling activities lacked finalized budgets.

sources.title: Contribution déterminée au niveau national 3.0 - République centrafricaine (UNFCCC)
sources.temporal_coverage: Baselines generally 2025; targets through 2030/2035
sources.methodology: Government inventory, planning, targets, indicators and financing framework
sources.limitations: Self-reported baselines and targets; climate-peace-security language is policy framing, not causal evaluation.

sources.title: First Biennial Transparency Report of the Central African Republic (UNFCCC)
sources.temporal_coverage: Primarily through 2024, with retrospective reporting
sources.methodology: Government technical reporting, inventories, adaptation assessment and self-evaluation
sources.limitations: Government self-report; adaptation-risk analysis itself is described as largely qualitative and constrained by weak data.

sources.title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Central African Republic (NUPI)
geographic_coverage: CAR, with regional Sahel/Great Lakes mechanisms
sources.temporal_coverage: Contemporary, with historical context
sources.methodology: Literature synthesis and expert/interview inputs organized around climate-security pathways
sources.limitations: Explicitly acknowledges limited CAR-specific climate/security monitoring and evidence; some pathway evidence derives from comparable or regional settings.

sources.title: Climate change in the Central African Republic: what threats? (ICRC)
sources.organization: International Committee of the Red Cross
geographic_coverage: CAR, especially pastoral and rural contexts
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical context through 2020-2021
sources.methodology: Practitioner observations of climate, pastoralism, conflict and humanitarian programming
sources.limitations: Qualitative practitioner source, not representative research; programme activities are not evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: Central African Republic IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis / April-August 2026 update (IPCinfo)
sources.temporal_coverage: Apr-Aug 2026, with comparison to Sep 2025-Mar 2026
sources.methodology: Multi-partner IPC analytical framework integrating food consumption, livelihoods and contributing factors
sources.limitations: IPC classification is analytical, not a causal attribution study; exact publication day was not visible on the opened page.

sources.title: Central African Republic Emergency Food Crisis Response Project (P176754): Implementation Status & Results Report (World Bank)
sources.temporal_coverage: Through May 2025
sources.methodology: Project monitoring indicators and Bank implementation supervision
sources.limitations: Not independent evaluation; several indicators measure reach/output rather than durable resilience.

sources.title: Central African Republic Country Climate and Development Report: Resilient and Inclusive Growth—Sustainable Solutions for CAR's Future
sources.temporal_coverage: 2020 baseline; urban flood projections to 2050 and 2100 across SSP-RCP pathways; broader CCDR uses historical indicators.
sources.methodology: CCDR combines diagnostics, spatial exposure analysis and climate/economic scenarios.
sources.limitations: Scenario-dependent model; French OCR imperfect; no causal violence estimate.

sources.title: Central African Republic Humanitarian Situation Report No. 2 (End-of-Year), reporting period 1 January to 31 December 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Operational results and humanitarian events during 2025; reporting period 1 January-31 December 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF annual operational monitoring and partner-reported humanitarian results.
sources.limitations: Operational reporting, not causal evaluation; flood locations and climate-attributable shares are not disaggregated.

sources.title: Estudio de vulnerabilidad y riesgo de pueblos indígenas de Chile ante el cambio climático
sources.temporal_coverage: Consultancy report dated 10 April 2024; combines literature and participant workshops on Indigenous climate vulnerability, adaptation and risk.
sources.methodology: Consultancy report combining literature and Mapuche workshops.
sources.limitations: Proposed input, not official policy; Indigenous-specific indicators lack public disaggregated data.

sources.title: Emergency: Wildfires in Chile. Humanitarian Flash Note No. 2
sources.temporal_coverage: Humanitarian situation and response during central and southern Chile wildfires, February–7 March 2024.
sources.methodology: UNICEF flash report using official event data and a 44-interview rapid assessment in Viña del Mar.
sources.limitations: Emergency snapshot; report does not attribute fires to climate change.

sources.title: Chile ya cuenta con su primer Plan de Adaptación al Cambio Climático para los Recursos Hídricos
sources.organization: Dirección General de Aguas, Ministry of Public Works (Chile)
sources.temporal_coverage: DGA account published 28 September 2026 on the formal water-sector adaptation plan and implementation tools.
sources.methodology: Agency page summarizing formal plan status, measures, pilot indicators and local capacity-building.
sources.limitations: Describes plan inputs and implementation activities, not evaluated hydrological or household outcomes.

sources.title: Resolución Exenta N° 244: Procedimiento de consulta previa y convocatoria a instituciones representativas del pueblo Mapuche
sources.organization: Ministry of Social Development and Family, Subsecretariat of Social Services; Diario Oficial de Chile
sources.temporal_coverage: Resolution published 3 July 2025; recitals summarize the Peace and Understanding Commission mandate and land-fund information through 2024.
sources.methodology: Official resolution and recitals presenting the government's territorial-conflict framing, commission mandate and administrative land-fund data.
sources.limitations: Official administrative framing, not an independent violence dataset or evaluation of conflict-resolution outcomes.

sources.title: The People's Republic of China Third National Communication on Climate Change
sources.organization: People's Republic of China; submitted to the UNFCCC
sources.temporal_coverage: Government-approved communication dated December 2018; observed climate and sector trends and future scenarios, generally updated through 2015.
sources.methodology: Government-approved UNFCCC report combining observed trends and modeled risks.
sources.limitations: Unofficial translation; underlying studies are dated and projections are not measurements.

sources.title: Progress Report on China's Climate Change Adaptation (2024) / 中国适应气候变化进展报告（2024）
sources.organization: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China
sources.temporal_coverage: Official 33-page review of climate conditions and adaptation activities in 2024; includes implementation status through February 2025.
sources.methodology: Ministry report reviewing national climate observations, sector actions and regional adaptation measures.
sources.limitations: Government progress account; program coverage and reported outputs are not independent outcome evaluations.

sources.title: 2024 national situation of natural disasters
sources.organization: National Commission for Disaster Prevention, Reduction and Relief Office and Ministry of Emergency Management of China
sources.temporal_coverage: Calendar-year 2024 disaster impacts reported by local emergency-management departments and reviewed by national agencies.
sources.methodology: Annual bulletin compiled from local emergency reports and inter-agency review; includes hazard-specific and regional totals.
sources.limitations: Administrative impact estimates; the bulletin does not attribute individual disasters to climate change.

sources.title: MEM publishes typical cases of successful disaster avoidance in 2024 / 应急管理部公布2024年度全国成功避险避灾典型案例
sources.organization: Ministry of Emergency Management of China
sources.temporal_coverage: National ministry's selected 2024 disaster-avoidance cases, published 6 June 2025.
sources.methodology: Ministry-selected case reports drawn from local submissions and expert review of 437 reported cases.
sources.limitations: Selected successful cases illustrate response processes, not representative rates or independently evaluated impact.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Côte d’Ivoire
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical 2018 flood example; cocoa and climate projections for the 2050s
sources.methodology: World Bank CCDR using sector analysis, climate projections and cited crop-suitability modelling.
sources.limitations: Cocoa table cites an external model without a stated scenario.

sources.title: Contribution Déterminée au niveau National 3.0 de la Côte d’Ivoire
sources.temporal_coverage: Current vulnerability assessment and adaptation planning in NDC 3.0
sources.methodology: Government NDC describing health, social and geographic climate vulnerabilities and planned adaptation measures.
sources.limitations: The cited passages summarize diagnosis and plans; implementation outcomes are not assessed there.

sources.title: The Climate Change and Conflict Nexus in West Africa: A New Approach for Operationally Relevant Vulnerability Assessments
sources.temporal_coverage: Qualitative case study drawing on country literature and interviews; no single projection horizon
sources.methodology: Qualitative Côte d’Ivoire case study triangulating literature, local and organizational reports, and semi-structured interviews.
sources.limitations: Identifies potential risks, not causal attribution; findings are context-specific and some evidence is qualitative.

sources.title: Quatrième Communication Nationale de la Côte d’Ivoire au titre de la CCNUCC
sources.organization: Ministère de l’Environnement, du Développement Durable et de la Transition Écologique, Côte d’Ivoire
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical water event in 2018; country and sector observations; RCP projections through 2050 and 2099.
sources.methodology: National assessment using sector vulnerability matrices, historical cases and RCP climate projections.
sources.limitations: Water and conflict examples partly cite earlier sources; conflict risk is analytical, not causal.

sources.title: Project to Strengthen the Resilience of Local Communities in the Bafing Region Made Vulnerable due to Farmer-Breeder Conflicts Exacerbated by Climate Change: Fully Developed Proposal
sources.organization: Interprofessional Fund for Agricultural Research and Advice (FIRCA) and Bafing Regional Council; submitted to the Adaptation Fund
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional climate and livelihood context; four-year locally led adaptation project approved in 2025.
sources.methodology: FIRCA's Adaptation Fund proposal with local context diagnostics and community consultations.
sources.limitations: Historical local inputs are cited; proposed outputs are not evaluations.

sources.title: Northern Côte d’Ivoire Crisis Response Plan 2024
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Côte d’Ivoire
sources.temporal_coverage: 2024 response-plan context and proposed activities; funding page updated 2026-02-05.
sources.methodology: IOM response plan combines regional context analysis, planned interventions, target estimates and funding requirements.
sources.limitations: Contextual pathways cite earlier studies; planned activities are not evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: Cameroon NDC 3.0 / *Contribution Déterminée au Niveau National Actualisée*
sources.temporal_coverage: Current policy; projections to 2100
sources.methodology: Government policy synthesizing prior vulnerability/projection evidence
sources.limitations: Climate projections in adaptation section partly reproduce earlier NDC/vulnerability evidence and do not identify model/scenario there. (UNFCCC)

sources.title: *Request for an Arrangement under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility*, Country Report 24/53
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly 2023-24; prospective reform programme
sources.methodology: IMF staff assessment, government discussions, World Bank assessment input
sources.limitations: Climate-FCV effects are expert synthesis/prospective risks rather than causal estimates. (IMF)

sources.title: Cameroon data portal
geographic_coverage: National with separate Far North and NW/SW categories
sources.temporal_coverage: Current
sources.methodology: Government, UNHCR, IOM and OCHA compiled displacement estimates
sources.limitations: Composite sources and methodologies; IDP values are estimates and differ by source. (UNHCR Data Portal)

sources.title: *Japan boosts life-saving food assistance as funding crisis threatens 600,000 people in Cameroon*
