sources.methodology: WFP food-security and operational planning evidence
sources.limitations: Agency operational source; food insecurity is explicitly multi-causal; announced assistance is not evidence of effectiveness. (World Food Programme)

sources.title: *Climate-fueled Violence and Displacement in the Lake Chad Basin: Focus on Chad and Cameroon*
geographic_coverage: Far North/Logone Birni; Lake Chad Basin
sources.temporal_coverage: Fieldwork Jul-Aug 2022; events from 2021
sources.methodology: Interviews with Cameroonian refugees, authorities, UN/donors/NGOs plus Cameroon-focused phone interviews
sources.limitations: Advocacy source; interview/perception evidence; fieldwork mainly conducted in Chad; no causal counterfactual. (Refugees International)

sources.title: *Implications of Climatic Stressors on Agro-Pastoral Resources Among Mbororo Communities Along the Slopes of Kilum-Ijim Mountain, North West Region, Cameroon*
sources.temporal_coverage: Field data mainly 2020; livestock series 2013-17
sources.methodology: 350 randomly administered household questionnaires, interviews and quantitative/qualitative analysis
sources.limitations: Very local; “environmental stressors” combine climatic and non-climatic factors; observational design. (Frontiers)

sources.title: *Youth Agropastoral Entrepreneurship Promotion Programme (AEP-Youth): Impact Assessment Report*
sources.temporal_coverage: Programme 2015-23; household survey Nov-Dec 2023
sources.methodology: Non-experimental counterfactual; propensity-score/multistage matching; quantitative surveys + KIIs
sources.limitations: Programme applicants formed sampling frame; no clean treated/control village designation; only four regions. (IFAD)

sources.title: *Project Completion Report Validation - Commodity Value Chain Support Project (PADFA)*
sources.temporal_coverage: Project 2010-17; validation 2019
sources.methodology: Independent validation of PCR and supporting evidence
sources.limitations: M&E system itself was weak/non-operational, materially restricting attribution. (IOE)

sources.title: *Country programme document for Cameroon (2027-2031)*
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 baseline; programme 2027-31
sources.methodology: National statistics, UN evidence and prior Independent Country Programme Evaluation
sources.limitations: Some programme achievements are summarized from the underlying ICPE rather than independently re-evaluated in the CPD. (UNDP)

sources.title: *Joint Monitoring Mission Report: CSO-Led Peacebuilding Project in the Lake Chad Basin Sub-Region - Cameroon and Niger*
sources.methodology: Joint visits/interviews with implementers, beneficiaries, authorities and CSOs
sources.limitations: Not independent; beneficiaries and implementers are part of monitoring process; no counterfactual. (MPTF Gateway)

sources.title: *Implementation Completion and Results Report: Cameroon Inclusive and Resilient Cities Development Project (P156210)*
geographic_coverage: Douala, Yaoundé, Kumba, Ngaoundéré, Batouri, Maroua, Kousséri
sources.temporal_coverage: Project 2017-25
sources.methodology: Project M&E, reports, databases, field missions and beneficiary/stakeholder evidence
sources.limitations: Formal satisfaction survey absent; some ex-post analysis used ex-ante benefit assumptions; NBS component incomplete. (World Bank)

sources.title: Cameroon Humanitarian Situation Report No. 4 (End of Year), 31 December 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Humanitarian events and UNICEF/partner response during 1 January-31 December 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF annual situation monitoring and partner-reported humanitarian results.
sources.limitations: Operational report, not an independent causal evaluation or representative coverage estimate.

sources.title: The situation in Central Africa and the activities of the United Nations Regional Office for Central Africa: Report of the Secretary-General (S/2026/445)
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional conditions and events from December 2025 through 15 March 2026; report dated 29 May 2026.
sources.methodology: Secretary-General regional reporting drawing on UN and cited partner sources, including ACLED and the regional climate centre.
sources.limitations: Climate conditions are described at subregional scale; the report does not attribute the Cameroon clash to climate.

sources.title: *National Adaptation Plan to Climate Change (2022-2026)*
sources.organization: DRC Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development / UNDP support
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical baseline plus projections to 2100
sources.methodology: Existing vulnerability assessments; CRU and model-ensemble climate information; RCP4.5/RCP8.5; policy consultations
sources.limitations: NAP explicitly notes reliance on older TNC/CRU information and need for updated, targeted studies.

sources.title: *Contribution Déterminée à l'échelle Nationale révisée*
sources.organization: DRC Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development
sources.methodology: National mitigation/adaptation planning, sector analysis, stakeholder revision process
sources.limitations: Policy commitments and financing needs are not evidence of implementation or outcomes.

sources.title: *Independent Country Programme Evaluation: Democratic Republic of Congo*
geographic_coverage: National plus fieldwork in five provinces
sources.temporal_coverage: Programme 2020-2024; some earlier projects
sources.methodology: OECD/DAC-oriented evaluation; document and portfolio review; 362 stakeholders; field visits; qualitative/quantitative triangulation
sources.limitations: Security/access constraints limited fieldwork; North Kivu fieldwork was limited to Goma; women were about one-third of interviewees.

sources.title: *Climate, Peace and Security in Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo* (SIPRI2)
sources.temporal_coverage: Literature to early 2025; workshop May 2024; KIIs Oct. 2024
sources.methodology: Literature synthesis; workshop with 50+ local stakeholders; five key-informant interviews; climate-security pathway framework
sources.limitations: Qualitative and geographically restricted; cannot establish national causal effects.

sources.title: *Climate Related Security Risks in Eastern DRC: Local Perspectives from North and South Kivu Provinces*
sources.organization: Folke Bernadotte Academy, Réseau CREF, Strong Roots Congo
geographic_coverage: North and South Kivu; Ruzizi evidence
sources.temporal_coverage: Workshop Mar. 2023 plus cited local studies
sources.methodology: Two-day multidisciplinary exploratory workshop and local research presentations
sources.limitations: Explicitly non-exhaustive; several pathway findings reflect participant expertise and presented research rather than a causal study by the report itself.

sources.title: *Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Democratic Republic of the Congo* (NUPI3)
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly evidence available to 2023
sources.methodology: Research synthesis of climate-security mechanisms and recommendations
sources.limitations: Broad synthesis; some claims are based on secondary evidence and should not override more recent humanitarian data.

sources.title: *Joint News Release - WFP/FAO: Millions Trapped in Deepening Hunger Crisis in the DRC...* (World Food Programme1)
geographic_coverage: National with focus on North/South Kivu, Ituri, Tanganyika
sources.methodology: Latest IPC update plus agency operational evidence
sources.limitations: Humanitarian situation data, not a causal climate attribution study.

sources.title: *DRC Urban Flood Resilience Project (P508410), Appraisal PID* (World Bank5)
sources.temporal_coverage: 2023-2030 context/design
sources.methodology: Project appraisal, DRM assessment and proposed results framework
sources.limitations: Mostly intended mechanisms and targets; not evidence that resilience outcomes were achieved.

sources.title: *DRC Urban Flood Resilience Project - Implementation Status & Results Report* (World Bank6)
sources.temporal_coverage: May-Sep. 2025
sources.methodology: First ISR; indicator and disbursement monitoring
sources.limitations: Very early implementation stage; “satisfactory” rating does not establish final effectiveness.

sources.title: *IMF Executive Board Completes Third ECF Review and Second RSF Review for DRC* (IMF8)
sources.methodology: Programme review and macroeconomic assessment
sources.limitations: Not an independent evaluation of climate-adaptation outcomes; programme performance is broader than climate policy.

sources.title: Democratic Republic of Congo Level 3 Emergency - Upsurge in Conflict, Humanitarian Situation Report No. 5, 1-15 May 2025
sources.organization: UNICEF Democratic Republic of the Congo
sources.temporal_coverage: Humanitarian events and response reported for 1-15 May 2025, with selected response totals since the crisis began.
sources.methodology: UNICEF situation monitoring and partner-reported humanitarian response results.
sources.limitations: Operational reporting; some response figures are cumulative and are not independent evaluations.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief: Democratic Republic of the Congo (reference date 24 June 2026)
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, Global Information and Early Warning System
sources.temporal_coverage: Seasonal crop assessments and food-security data through June 2026; rainfall outlook for June-October 2026.
sources.methodology: FAO GIEWS synthesis of crop, forecast, IPC and supply data.
sources.limitations: Country brief; forecast resolution and intervention impact evaluation are not provided.

sources.title: The Republic of Congo can turn the climate crisis into an opportunity to end poverty and boost shared prosperity
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank CCDR summary includes projections through 2050 and policy priorities
sources.methodology: World Bank press-release summary of the Republic of Congo CCDR and its headline estimates and recommendations.
sources.limitations: Summary page does not present the modeling assumptions behind economic-loss projections; recommendations are not outcomes.

sources.title: Contribution Déterminée au niveau National de la République du Congo
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Congo
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC vulnerability assessment and adaptation priorities; historical hydrological observations described in the document
sources.methodology: Government NDC describing sectoral vulnerability, observed impacts and planned adaptation actions.
sources.limitations: The cited assessment is dated 2021; it is not a current flood-impact inventory.

sources.title: Republic of Congo: Selected Issues; IMF Country Report No. 24/252
sources.temporal_coverage: EM-DAT data from 2000; flood events and government estimates for 2023–2024
sources.methodology: IMF selected-issues chapter uses EM-DAT, WFP and initial government estimates for recent flood events.
sources.limitations: Some 2023 impact figures are preliminary government estimates; reported averages depend on the underlying event database.

sources.title: Urban Flood and Gully Erosion Risk Management in the Congo Basin: Republic of the Congo, Technical Report
sources.organization: Global Center on Adaptation and World Bank
sources.temporal_coverage: Urban hazard and pre-feasibility assessments; workshops and community demonstrations in October-November 2025.
sources.methodology: Technical report draws on an urban NbSWLM inventory, three site assessments and 2025 workshops.
sources.limitations: Proposed measures and workshop findings; not an impact evaluation or proof of implementation.

sources.title: Armed Group Responses to Climate Shocks: A Study of FARC-EP Dissident Activities in the Colombian Amazon During an El Niño Year
sources.organization: United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR), Managing Exits from Armed Conflict project
sources.temporal_coverage: Qualitative focus groups conducted in San José del Guaviare in November 2023 and September 2024, around the 2023–2024 El Niño cycle.
sources.methodology: Two qualitative focus-group rounds in San José del Guaviare with Indigenous people, leaders, youth, authorities, military and police.
sources.limitations: One subregion; El Niño is a proxy, and concurrent political/economic changes confound attribution.

sources.title: Multiple shocks drive Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes in La Guajira and Chocó
sources.temporal_coverage: Food Security Outlook covering June 2026–January 2027; information available through 25 June 2026.
sources.methodology: FEWS NET IPC-compatible food-security outlook using national and local reports.
sources.limitations: Projection through January 2027; local conditions vary.

sources.title: MinVivienda identifica 558 municipios en riesgo y orienta acciones de preparación ante el Fenómeno El Niño
sources.organization: Ministry of Housing, City and Territory of Colombia
sources.temporal_coverage: Territorial water and sanitation risk analysis and El Niño preparedness guidance published 12 September 2026.
sources.methodology: Ministry territorial screening of potential El Niño impacts on drinking water and sanitation systems.
sources.limitations: Risk categories and recommended actions; no household-level estimates or measured service outcomes.

sources.title: Gobierno nacional alerta por altas temperaturas y aumento en probabilidad de El Niño
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development, IDEAM and National Unit for Disaster Risk Management
sources.temporal_coverage: Joint national alert on May 2026 heat and rainfall conditions, fire alerts, and El Niño probability.
sources.methodology: Government alert combining IDEAM monitoring, recent observations and climate forecasts.
sources.limitations: Short-term alert and forecast; it does not confirm El Niño or attribute individual hazards to climate change.

sources.title: Troisième contribution déterminée au niveau national (CDN 3.0)
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate and disaster context, including 2018–2023 events and adaptation priorities
sources.methodology: Nationally determined contribution describing climate context, vulnerability, reported disaster impacts and planned adaptation priorities.
sources.limitations: French-language national plan; adaptation priorities and risk tables are not independent impact evaluations. Historical event figures are reported by the NDC.

sources.title: Initial National Communication on Climate Change: Executive Summary
sources.organization: Government of the Union of the Comoros, Ministry of Development, Infrastructures, Post and Telecommunications and International Transports, General Directorate of Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: Initial national communication and projections through 2050, published in 2002; some farming-system data date to 1987
sources.methodology: Executive summary drawing on vulnerability studies for agriculture, coastal infrastructure and resources, health and water, with IPCC-based island projections.
sources.limitations: Historical assessment with old demographic and land-use inputs; projections reflect the science and assumptions available in 2002.

sources.title: Comoros country overview
sources.temporal_coverage: Current World Bank country-page overview; publication date not stated
sources.methodology: World Bank country overview page; no underlying analysis method is stated on the inspected passage.
sources.limitations: Undated, mutable summary page; the inspected passage gives no detailed measurement method for infrastructure vulnerability.

sources.title: Analyse du paysage climatique pour les enfants aux Comores
geographic_coverage: coastal and riverine areas across the islands
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed island-level water access; modeled rainfall and sea-level risks to 2090; May 2024 flood impacts.
sources.methodology: UNICEF climate-landscape assessment using secondary evidence and youth consultations.
sources.limitations: National assessment with limited local exposure and displacement estimates.

sources.title: Comoros National Water Resilience Project (P504691) – Additional Financing Request 1
sources.temporal_coverage: Project appraisal context and water-sector conditions documented in April 2025.
sources.methodology: Public-disclosure appraisal-stage project information document with country and water-sector context.
sources.limitations: Project document summarizing sector estimates; it is not an independent national water-sector evaluation.

sources.title: Inondation en mai- juin 2024 : Une main forte extraordinaire dans les zones sinistrées
sources.temporal_coverage: May 2024 floods and response measures reported through September 2024.
sources.methodology: UNDP article reporting official flood response, affected localities and follow-up works.
sources.limitations: News report, not a comprehensive damage assessment or independent response evaluation.

sources.title: Increased Access to Water Supply for Resilience in Comoros (IAWASuR)
sources.temporal_coverage: Project status milestones through August 2025 and planned cross-island water-resilience activities.
sources.methodology: Official project summary, intended beneficiaries, expected outcomes and approval milestones.
sources.limitations: The page describes aims and expected outcomes, not verified implementation results.

sources.title: Ambitious climate action will reap large dividends for Cabo Verde
sources.temporal_coverage: Current vulnerabilities and GDP/tourism projections through 2050
sources.methodology: World Bank official CCDR summary page describing sectoral exposure and headline projections.
sources.limitations: Summary page omits assumptions behind 2050 estimates.

sources.title: Cabo Verde Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0 (NDC)
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate trends over approximately 50 years; current vulnerability assessment
sources.methodology: Government NDC summarizing historical climate analysis and differentiated vulnerability assessments.
sources.limitations: The cited vulnerability passages are national diagnostics; station-level and group-level methods are not detailed there.

sources.title: Cabo Verde: Increasing Resilience to Disasters and Climate-Related Shocks
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank-supported disaster-risk reforms reported for 2018–2022
sources.methodology: World Bank results brief describing a policy-financing operation and reported outputs.
sources.limitations: Institutional achievements are publisher-reported results; the page does not provide an independent counterfactual evaluation.

sources.title: Cabo Verde Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Current and historical exposure; climate scenarios through 2050 and 2100; cited social data years vary by indicator.
sources.methodology: CCDR uses geospatial exposure analysis and climate scenarios.
sources.limitations: Modeled estimates depend on stated thresholds and cited data years.

sources.title: Cape Verde Floods: Operation Update #1 (MDRCV005)
sources.organization: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
sources.temporal_coverage: August 2025 floods and IFRC/Cabo Verde Red Cross response reported through 30 September 2025.
sources.methodology: IFRC operation update reports crisis effects, local needs and response outputs for August–September 2025.
sources.limitations: Operational figures and response outputs are not an independent post-disaster evaluation.

sources.title: Cabo Verde launches national roll-out of Early Warnings for All
sources.temporal_coverage: National Early Warnings for All rollout and draft roadmap announced in December 2025.
sources.methodology: WMO update summarizing a national rollout and multi-stakeholder workshop.
sources.limitations: The roadmap was still awaiting validation; no warning-system performance results are reported.

sources.title: Building Adaptive Capacity and Resilience to Climate Change in the Water Sector in Cabo Verde
sources.temporal_coverage: Completed UNDP/GEF water-sector adaptation project; page gives no project completion date.
sources.methodology: UNDP project page describes intervention design, pilot locations and reported completion status.
sources.limitations: Page does not name all municipalities or independently quantify adaptation outcomes.

sources.title: Governo anuncia plano de emergência para mitigação da seca e mau ano agrícola
sources.temporal_coverage: Government announcement of the 2017–2018 drought and poor agricultural-year emergency program.
sources.methodology: Government announcement describing program scope, intended beneficiaries and implementation arrangements.
sources.limitations: The announcement records approved measures, not delivery or effectiveness results.

sources.title: Grass-roots of Adaptation: Strengthening community climate resilience through locally led adaptation in Costa Rica
sources.organization: Fundecooperación para el Desarrollo Sostenible; submitted to the Adaptation Fund
sources.temporal_coverage: Proposal contextualizes historical meteorological records from 1980–2017 and regional adaptation risks; proposal version July 2025.
sources.methodology: Proposal summarizes IMN hazard records and regional risks.
sources.limitations: Applicant proposal; regional summaries rely on prior government analyses and do not attribute events.

sources.title: United Nations organizations’ support to community-driven recovery, risk knowledge and governance enhances disaster and climate resilience in Costa Rica
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR)
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports 2017 Storm Nate recovery and United Nations-supported risk and resilience work through 2023.
sources.methodology: UNDRR summarizes program activities and risk findings.
sources.limitations: Program account; no independent impact evaluation.

sources.title: Informe de progreso del Plan Nacional de Adaptación al Cambio Climático de Costa Rica 2022-2026
sources.organization: Dirección de Cambio Climático, Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía; GIZ and IISD
sources.temporal_coverage: Implementation progress of the 2022–2026 National Adaptation Plan, assessed through June 2026.
sources.methodology: Questionnaires, consultation and document review assessed NAP products through June 2026.
sources.limitations: Progress covered 179 of 232 products; institutional self-report is not impact evaluation.

sources.title: Proyectos Climáticos
sources.organization: Dirección de Cambio Climático, Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía (MINAE)
sources.temporal_coverage: MINAE project-register entries with stated project durations; the page does not provide publication or project-status dates for every entry.
sources.methodology: Official registry lists project aims, locations and durations.
sources.limitations: Entries describe design; status and outcomes are unreported.

sources.title: Contribution déterminée au niveau national de Djibouti (CDN de Djibouti), version révisée
sources.organization: Republic of Djibouti, Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development; UNFCCC repository
sources.temporal_coverage: Revised NDC implementation period 2024–2030; climate projections to 2050 and longer-term risks.
sources.methodology: Revised government NDC reports climate-risk analysis and adaptation commitments.
sources.limitations: French-language policy estimates; some scenarios are unspecified.

sources.title: Djibouti Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: CCDR summary presents projections to 2050 and mid-century.
sources.methodology: World Bank Group CCDR country page with substantive report summary, risk estimates, and priority recommendations.
sources.limitations: The linked full report was not inspected; claims are confined to the opened CCDR summary page.

sources.title: Djibouti: Climate Action Can Protect Growth and Build Resilience
sources.temporal_coverage: CCDR press release summarizes long-term climate risk through 2050 and current coastal-city exposure.
sources.methodology: World Bank Group press release summarizing the first Djibouti CCDR and its priority risks.
sources.limitations: Press-release summary, not the full CCDR; model assumptions are not included in the release.

sources.title: Analyse de l’insécurité alimentaire aiguë et de la malnutrition aiguë, mai–décembre 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Current acute food insecurity May–June 2025; projection July–December 2025; response coverage January–May 2025.
sources.methodology: IPC survey and monitoring synthesis.
sources.limitations: Dated multi-driver analysis; forecasts depend on assumptions.

sources.title: The Republic of Djibouti: Country Brief
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, Global Information and Early Warning System
sources.temporal_coverage: Rainfall and pastoral conditions March–May 2025; food-security projection July–December 2025.
sources.methodology: GIEWS country brief summarizes weather, rangeland and food-security monitoring for the reference date.
sources.limitations: A dated situation snapshot; seasonal forecasts and projected food-security outcomes are not observed results.

sources.title: Integrated Community Resilience Project (P506969), Project Appraisal Document
sources.temporal_coverage: Country context and refugee figures as of January 2025; appraisal and proposed project activities in 2025.
sources.methodology: Project appraisal and design synthesis.
sources.limitations: Appraisal context and planned investments, not evaluated impact.

sources.title: Sustainable Management of Water and Rangeland Resources for Enhanced Climate Resilience of Rural Communities in Djibouti
sources.temporal_coverage: Six-year adaptation project listed as under implementation; page states intended results and target population.
sources.methodology: UNDP project page describes locations, climate risks, institutional needs and planned activities.
sources.limitations: Planned outcomes and targets are not evidence of completed delivery or independently measured impact.

sources.title: Dominica
sources.temporal_coverage: Hurricane Maria recovery and resilience programmes described on an undated page.
sources.methodology: Country programme account.
sources.limitations: Historical programme descriptions; current institutional status and independent outcomes not verified.

sources.title: Strengthening community resilience within Kalinago Territory
sources.temporal_coverage: Programme described for 2025-2026.
sources.methodology: Project rationale and expected results.
sources.limitations: Project intentions and reported updates are not evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: Strengthening community resilience in the Kalinago Territory in Dominica
sources.organization: Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture
sources.temporal_coverage: Project dates17August2026-17February2027.
sources.methodology: Implementer project description and objectives.
sources.limitations: No publication date stated; proposed training and food-security gains are not completed outcomes.

sources.title: Post-Disaster Needs Assessment: Hurricane Maria, September 18, 2017
sources.organization: Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica, with technical support from GFDRR, UNDP, EU, UN, OECS and World Bank Group
sources.temporal_coverage: Hurricane Maria effects and recovery needs; figures reported through November 2017.
sources.methodology: Government-led multisector post-disaster assessment of physical, economic, social and sector effects and recovery needs.
sources.limitations: Immediate 2017 recovery estimates; reported damage and projections are not a later recovery evaluation.

sources.title: Dominica: Disaster Resilience Strategy
sources.organization: Government of Dominica; published by the International Monetary Fund
geographic_coverage: towns and communities affected by Hurricane Maria
sources.temporal_coverage: Government disaster-resilience strategy, August 2021; includes the post-Maria emergency and recovery period.
sources.methodology: Government strategy prepared with stakeholder and development-partner consultation and hosted by IMF.
sources.limitations: The strategy summarizes reported post-disaster conditions; it is not a causal study of violence or insecurity.

sources.title: Dominica’s Journey to Become the World’s First Climate Resilient Country
sources.temporal_coverage: Disaster Vulnerability Reduction Project outputs and infrastructure works reported in 2023, including the 2022 trough event.
sources.methodology: World Bank project feature summarizing reported disaster-risk-reduction outputs and infrastructure works.
sources.limitations: The feature reports project outputs and works in progress, not an independent outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Strengthening Community Resilience within Kalinago Territory, Project Document
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme and Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica
sources.temporal_coverage: Signed project design for July 2025–December 2026, including cited poverty context and planned activities.
sources.methodology: UNDP project document sets out a local situation analysis, implementation risks, theory of change and planned activities.
sources.limitations: Some poverty and livelihood context cites older sources; intended outputs and social-cohesion outcomes are not measured results.

sources.title: Kalinago Families Receive Tools and Training to Strengthen Food Security and Resilience
sources.temporal_coverage: UNDP community distribution and training reported in August 2026.
sources.methodology: UNDP press release describes project activities, delivered inputs and participating households.
sources.limitations: Implementer reporting of early project outputs; no independent assessment of sustained food-security or resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Update: Government of Dominica Response to Trough System – April 30
sources.organization: Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica, Office of the Prime Minister
sources.temporal_coverage: Flood and landslide impacts from the 26 April 2026 trough and immediate response update published 1 May 2026.
sources.methodology: Government response update based on field visits, rapid household assessments and reports from responsible agencies.
sources.limitations: An early operational update; damage, assistance and restoration figures were provisional and evolving.

sources.title: Climate migrants: Dominican Republic: Country Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate-migration projections for 2050 and 2100; qualitative case-study interviews in Restauración reported in the 2024 country report.
sources.methodology: Quantitative climate-migration modeling plus qualitative interviews in Restauración.
sources.limitations: Projections are uncertain; interviews reflect one agricultural-border locality, not population prevalence.

sources.title: Dominican Republic Poverty Assessment 2023: Background Note on Poverty and Climate Change
sources.temporal_coverage: Uses a 2021 flood-risk household survey for reported impacts and coping in April 2019–April 2021, plus historical household and hazard data.
sources.methodology: Uses a 2,057-household 2021 flood survey and risk maps.
sources.limitations: Survey reports April 2019–April 2021 experiences.

sources.title: Dominican Republic: 2025 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 Article IV report; reports recent policy and disaster conditions, including Hurricane Fiona in 2022 and climate projections to 2050.
sources.methodology: Article IV report covers climate and disaster-risk policy.
sources.limitations: WB source for some impacts; policy tools not evaluated.

sources.title: National Climate Resilience Assessment for Algeria
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate and infrastructure evidence through 2024; projections to 2081–2100.
sources.methodology: IEA assessment combines climate observations, IPCC projections, INFORM hazard indicators and energy-system exposure analysis.
sources.limitations: Most infrastructure examples concern energy assets; household vulnerability is not comprehensively mapped.

sources.title: Inclusive insurance and risk financing in Algeria: Snapshot and way forward 2023
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Insurance and Risk Finance Facility and UNDP Algeria
sources.temporal_coverage: Hazard records range from historical periods through 2020; insurance and disaster-finance snapshot mainly covers 2019–2021.
sources.methodology: The 23-page summary presents an inclusive-insurance and disaster-risk-finance country diagnostic and key hazard impacts.
sources.limitations: Historical hazard and insurance data are dated, not a current local assessment.

sources.title: Algeria: Selected Issues, Fiscal Reforms to Support Addressing Climate Change Challenges
sources.temporal_coverage: IMF staff climate-risk and fiscal analysis completed in March 2024; includes projections through 2100 and policy simulations.
sources.methodology: IMF staff assesses physical and fiscal climate risks and models policy options using the IMF-World Bank Climate Policy Assessment Tool.
sources.limitations: Impact pathways and policy results are projections or model outputs; they do not establish observed displacement or violence.

sources.title: Urban Natural Hazard Vulnerability Reduction Project: Technical Annex to the Memorandum of the President
sources.temporal_coverage: Technical annex and proposed project design following the November 2001 Algiers flood.
sources.methodology: Technical annex documents local vulnerability diagnoses, project components, institutional arrangements and intended emergency works.
sources.limitations: This is a 2002 design-stage annex; proposed surveys, training and protections are not evidence of completed results.

sources.title: Law No. 24-04 of 26 February 2024 on prevention, intervention and reduction of disaster risks
sources.organization: Official Gazette of the People's Democratic Republic of Algeria
sources.temporal_coverage: Statutory disaster-risk governance provisions published March 2024.
sources.methodology: Official Gazette publishes the French translation of Law 24-04 and its disaster-risk governance requirements.
sources.limitations: Statutory mandates do not establish whether local plans, training or warning systems operate effectively.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Ecuador
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports historical flood and shoreline impacts, recent policy processes, and modeled climate, poverty and adaptation outcomes to 2050.
sources.methodology: Climate scenarios, hazard models, sector analysis and poverty microsimulation.
sources.limitations: Some impact estimates are cited; model results depend on scenarios.

sources.title: Análisis de choques en Ecuador - 2026
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
sources.temporal_coverage: Intersectoral shock analysis published May 2026; describes security-related operational constraints during 2025 and current humanitarian needs.
sources.methodology: OCHA intersectoral analysis summarizes 2026 shock needs and access conditions.
sources.limitations: Only the official publication-page text was accessible; the linked PDF was not opened.

sources.title: Food security impacts of organized criminal violence in Ecuador
sources.organization: Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET)
sources.temporal_coverage: Special report published 29 May 2026; describes recent violence and projects food-security and weather conditions for June–December 2026.
sources.methodology: FEWS NET combines food-security and weather analysis.
sources.limitations: Forecast reflects May 2026 information; local outcomes may vary.

sources.title: Egypt's First Biennial Transparency Report
sources.organization: Government of Egypt, Ministry of Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical hazards and 2024 baseline, with adaptation plans and projections to 2100.
sources.methodology: Government submission synthesizing climate vulnerability, hazard history and adaptation reporting.
sources.limitations: Some measures and beneficiaries are reported plans or targets, not independently evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: Egypt Country Climate and Development Report: Executive Summary
sources.temporal_coverage: Country climate-development analysis published in 2022; includes scenarios through 2030 and 2037.
sources.methodology: Country climate-development analysis combining sector evidence, cited studies and modeled risks.
sources.limitations: Executive-summary projections rely on stated assumptions and referenced background studies.

sources.title: Egypt's Updated Nationally Determined Contributions
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC update covering 2015–2030, with national water context through 2050.
sources.methodology: Government NDC reporting national circumstances and adaptation commitments.
sources.limitations: National-level strategy; stated commitments are not evidence of delivered results.

sources.title: Project to Enhance Climate Change Adaptation in the Nile Delta and North Coast
sources.organization: Egyptian Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation
sources.temporal_coverage: Project description accessed in 2026; coastal planning scenarios extend to 2100.
sources.methodology: Official project summary of a GCF-funded coastal adaptation initiative.
sources.limitations: Describes project scope and objectives, not an independent outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Eritrea NDC 3.0
sources.organization: Government of the State of Eritrea; submitted to the UNFCCC
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate observations through 2018, recent drought context and climate projections to 2100
sources.methodology: NDC summarizes national studies, consultations, field visits and IPCC AR5-based projections.
sources.limitations: Observed data and group rankings are cited; projections are model-dependent (RCP2.6/RCP8.5).

sources.title: Inclusive and Sustainable Development
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Eritrea Country Office
sources.temporal_coverage: Undated page; land and agriculture figures attributed on-page to Ministry of Agriculture 2022
sources.methodology: UNDP country-page description of its development portfolio and cited national agricultural context; no separate method is stated.
sources.limitations: Undated, mutable webpage; the cited agricultural figures are attributed to the Ministry of Agriculture 2022.

sources.title: Climate Change Adaptation Programme in Water and Agriculture in Anseba Region, Eritrea: Request for Project/Programme Funding
sources.organization: Adaptation Fund; implementing entity UNDP; executing entity Ministry of Agriculture, Anseba Region
sources.temporal_coverage: Project proposal with undated receipt field; includes historical baselines and long-range climate projections
sources.methodology: Project-funding proposal combining local water and agriculture context, national adaptation projections and proposed interventions for Anseba.
sources.limitations: Proposal is not an evaluation; its explicit water-land conflict statement is a prospective risk hypothesis and the cited passage gives no empirical conflict estimate.

sources.title: Ex Post Evaluation #6: Climate Change Adaptation Programme in Water and Agriculture in Anseba Region, Eritrea
sources.organization: Adaptation Fund Technical Evaluation Reference Group; evaluation conducted by Universalia Management Group
sources.temporal_coverage: AF-supported project outcomes seven years after its 2018 closure; fieldwork in August 2025.
sources.methodology: Independent AF-TERG ex-post evaluation using document review, interviews, focus groups, transect walks, observation and site visits.
sources.limitations: Eight of 16 project sites were visited; findings are not a region-wide census.

sources.title: Returning Thirsty: Water Supply, Livelihoods and Returnees in the Gash-Barka Region, Eritrea
sources.organization: Overseas Development Institute, South Bank University and Eritrean research collaborators
sources.temporal_coverage: Post-border-war return and resettlement period; field research around 2001 and report published in 2002.
sources.methodology: Field research in nine Gash-Barka communities using rapid appraisal, interviews and a structured 156-household survey.
sources.limitations: Historical post-conflict study; reports localized resource tensions, not climate-caused or widespread armed violence.

sources.title: Climate Change Adaptation Programme in Water and Agriculture in Anseba Region, Eritrea: Eritrea Case Study
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Adaptation Learning Mechanism
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate and livelihood conditions reported for a 2012 project case study, including 2002–2004 rainfall impacts.
sources.methodology: UNDP case study presents local climate, livelihood and water context for an adaptation programme and its design.
sources.limitations: Project-preparation context, not a current reassessment or outcome evaluation; projections and conditions are dated.

sources.title: Climate Risks and Adaptation Guidelines for Power Transmission and Solar Generation Systems in the Sahel Region: Country Chapter – Eritrea
sources.temporal_coverage: Reference climatology 1961–1990, historical climate 1990–2020 and projections for 2030–2060.
sources.methodology: Country chapter summarizes modelled hazards and risks to solar technologies, drawing on GCA's 2022 Sahel hazard assessment.
sources.limitations: High-level, energy-asset assessment; the report calls for site-specific studies and notes climate-model uncertainty.

sources.title: Updated Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.temporal_coverage: Baselines mainly historical/2018; targets to 2030
sources.methodology: Government review, modelling and stakeholder process; 40 adaptation interventions
sources.limitations: Government policy/source; several underlying vulnerability statistics are older.

sources.title: Stocktake of Climate Change Adaptation Interventions in Ethiopia
sources.temporal_coverage: Primarily implementation since 2021
sources.methodology: Focus groups, structured questionnaires to line ministries, desk review and secondary statistics
sources.limitations: Primarily qualitative and government-led; many adaptation indicators themselves lack data.

sources.title: Ethiopia Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical to 2023; modeled futures to 2100
sources.methodology: CMIP6 ensemble, economic/sector modelling, surveys, administrative and literature synthesis
sources.limitations: Explicitly does not model future climate-fragility interaction; some conflict evidence comes from underlying/forthcoming analyses. (World Bank2)

sources.title: Is climate a risk multiplier in Ethiopia?
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical observational data
sources.methodology: Empirical study of climate, food-security and conflict relationships
sources.limitations: Detailed downloadable study could not be fully fetched here; numerical results retained only where reproduced with locator in the CCDR. (World Food Programme1)

sources.title: The World Food Programme’s Contribution to Improving the Prospects for Peace in Ethiopia
sources.temporal_coverage: Interviews chiefly 2021
sources.methodology: Literature review; remote KIIs; in-person beneficiary/non-beneficiary interviews and focus groups
sources.limitations: Local case; mixed evidence; cannot be generalized nationally. (SIPRI7)

sources.title: Ethiopia emergency
sources.methodology: WFP operational/humanitarian monitoring
sources.limitations: Agency operational reporting; needs and planned reach are not evaluation results. (World Food Programme8) Publisher passage access failed during the 26 October 2026 review; no snippet was used as verification.

sources.title: WFP supports Ethiopia to build resilient food systems in Somali Region with solar-powered irrigation scheme
sources.temporal_coverage: Through Apr. 2026
sources.methodology: Programme administrative/output reporting
sources.limitations: WFP self-report; production/output figures are not independently evaluated impact estimates. (World Food Programme12)

sources.title: Children displaced in a changing climate: Preventing and minimizing risk of displacement and preparing for climate mobility in Eastern and Southern Africa
sources.organization: UNICEF, in partnership with the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical displacement estimates for 2017–2023 and Ethiopia protection-system analysis published in September 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF–IDMC combine recorded 2017–2023 disaster displacements with georeferenced child-population proxies.
sources.limitations: Counts are conservative displacement events, not unique children; Ethiopia-specific climate-conflict and long-term outcome research is limited.

sources.title: Nothing to put in your mouth: Seeking durable solutions to drought displacement in Ethiopia
sources.temporal_coverage: Fieldwork in Somali Region in July 2019; includes displacement associated with the 2015–2017 drought and 2019 conditions.
sources.methodology: 219 purposive interviews and qualitative fieldwork in Doolo camps in July 2019.
sources.limitations: Camp sample is not representative; forced displacement is hard to distinguish from adaptive migration, and estimates omit some people remaining in place.

sources.title: The Dynamics of (Agro) Pastoral Conflicts in Eastern Ethiopia
sources.organization: Ethiopian Journal of the Social Sciences and Humanities, Addis Ababa University
geographic_coverage: Meiso-Mullu district, Shinile Zone, Somali Region
Meiso district, West Hararghe Zone, Oromia Region
sources.temporal_coverage: Fieldwork from February 2013 to November 2014; published in Volume 11, Number 1, June 2015.
sources.methodology: Mixed qualitative and quantitative study with a 128-household survey, interviews, focus groups and observations in three selected districts.
sources.limitations: Kebeles were selected for drought and conflict severity; findings reflect a small, purposively located study and respondents’ perceptions, not causal estimates.

sources.title: Ethiopia, Endline Evaluation of Satellite Index Insurance for Pastoralists (SIIPE)
sources.organization: World Food Programme Ethiopia Country Office
geographic_coverage: 11 woredas (names not given on the accessible page)
sources.temporal_coverage: SIIPE programme period 2019–2022; programme reach and evaluation findings summarized by WFP in November 2024.
sources.methodology: WFP describes a decentralized mixed-method evaluation combining quasi-experimental quantitative analysis with qualitative interviews and data.
sources.limitations: Only WFP’s evaluation landing-page summary was accessible; it gives limited estimation detail and reports missing gender-disaggregated data.

sources.title: Fiji Country Climate and Development Report: Investing in Resilience, Growth and Jobs
sources.temporal_coverage: Long-term development and climate risks; publication date not stated
sources.methodology: Substantive CCDR publisher synthesis.
sources.limitations: Publisher summary, not the complete underlying study or an independent causal evaluation.

sources.title: Fiji launches initiative to strengthen early warning systems for all
sources.temporal_coverage: May 2026 launch and design
sources.methodology: Programme launch and institutional diagnosis.
sources.limitations: Project design and intended benefits; implementation and outcomes are not established.

sources.title: Climate Change and Peacebuilding in Fiji
sources.organization: Conciliation Resources, with Transcend Oceania and the Pacific Centre for Peacebuilding
geographic_coverage: Qauia, Nanuku and Maravu near Suva
sources.temporal_coverage: Fiji programme ran January 2020–June 2024; practice paper cover dated June 2024.
sources.methodology: 2020–24 partner-programme practice report.
sources.limitations: Purposive implementer account, not representative or experimental.

sources.title: Perspectives on climate change and adaptation in Fijian villages contemplating relocation
sources.organization: Frontiers in Climate; Yuki Yoshida, Giles B. Sioen, Gauna Metuisela and Richard Crichton
geographic_coverage: Vanua Levu: Macuata and Cakaudrove provinces

sources.methodology: March 2024 qualitative field visits, interviews and talanoa across seven purposively selected iTaukei villages.
sources.limitations: Brief scoping sample centered on village leaders; not representative or causal; field notes summarize local accounts.

sources.title: Climate Change and Sea Level Rise, Fiji
geographic_coverage: Votua, Nawaqarua and Etatoko villages, lower Ba River Catchment, Viti Levu
sources.temporal_coverage: IMF paper completed 30 May 2025 and published June 2025; includes modeled sea-level-rise scenarios and earlier relocation cases.
sources.methodology: IMF staff estimates sea-level-rise costs and adaptation with CIAM; Box 1 summarizes prior village relocation research.
sources.limitations: Local cases are explicitly partial and anecdotal; CIAM requires finer topographic, population and asset data.

sources.title: Climate change and the planned relocation of people: A longitudinal analysis of Vunidogoloa, Fiji
sources.organization: Ambio; Celia McMichael, Teresia Powell, Annah E. Piggott-McKellar and Merewalesi Yee
sources.temporal_coverage: Seven qualitative research waves in Vunidogoloa from 2015 to 2023; journal issue June 2025.
sources.methodology: Longitudinal qualitative study with 41 interviews and 11 talanoa discussions over seven visits from 2015–2023.
sources.limitations: Online publication 8 January 2025, June issue. Qualitative longitudinal village study, not causal attribution or a current national assessment.

sources.title: Roads across Federated States of Micronesia set for climate-resilient upgrade
sources.temporal_coverage: 2022 project approval and road exposure
sources.methodology: Country project announcement.
sources.limitations: Project design and intended benefits; implementation and outcomes are not established.

sources.title: Understanding risk is key to growth and jobs in Pacific cities
sources.temporal_coverage: Undated city-risk assessment synopsis
sources.methodology: Staff synthesis of urban risk assessments.
sources.limitations: Qualitative city examples; not exhaustive hazard mapping or causal attribution.

sources.title: The Federated States of Micronesia Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0
sources.organization: Government of the Federated States of Micronesia
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate and adaptation assessment published September 2025; includes 2024 population and water-service information.
sources.methodology: National government submission to UNFCCC; policy report.
sources.limitations: Commitments and needs are not independently evaluated.

sources.title: Climate Change in the Federated States of Micronesia: Food and Water Security, Climate Risk Management, and Adaptive Strategies—Report of Findings 2010
sources.organization: University of Hawaiʻi Sea Grant College Program, Center for Island Climate Adaptation and Policy, with the U.S. Geological Survey
sources.temporal_coverage: Three-week field assessment in April 2009, including retrospective accounts of 2002 and 2007–2008 hazards.

sources.limitations: Short field period and older hazard conditions; not a representative survey or updated risk model.

sources.title: Federated States of Micronesia: 2026 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Federated States of Micronesia
sources.organization: International Monetary Fund, Asia and Pacific Department
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 Article IV consultation; climate-risk assessment, governance and fragility analysis, and adaptation discussion.
sources.methodology: IMF Article IV staff assessment and risk matrix; coordinator inspected public full-report passages.
sources.limitations: Staff institutional/risk synthesis, not local causal estimates.

sources.title: Gabon Country Climate and Development Report: Annexes
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 CCDR annex with 2021 urban exposure data and forward-looking climate-risk analysis.
sources.methodology: CCDR annex combining urban exposure estimates and social-inclusion analysis.
sources.limitations: French report; selected city estimates and projected risks are not national incident rates.

sources.title: Troisième Contribution Déterminée au niveau National (CDN3.0) du Gabon
sources.organization: Government of Gabon, National Climate Council
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC 3.0 dated November 2025, covering 2025–2035 and longer-term climate strategy.
sources.methodology: Government NDC drawing on national vulnerability analysis, sector plans and stakeholder consultation.
sources.limitations: Risks and 2025–2035 measures are national policy claims; planned actions are not completed outcomes.

sources.title: Lancement des missions de sensibilisation pour la préparation du Plan National d’Adaptation (NAP-II)
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports NAP-II sensitization missions scheduled for 3–12 December 2025.
sources.methodology: UNDP announcement describing government-led local consultations for NAP-II preparation.
sources.limitations: Reports a planning process and intended roadmap, not completed implementation or impact.

sources.title: L’ANPN et la CDC en première ligne pour la mise en œuvre du Plan national d’adaptation côtière
sources.organization: Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations du Gabon
sources.temporal_coverage: Page describes a coastal adaptation project; publication date is not stated.
sources.methodology: Institutional news page describing a co-managed coastal adaptation project.
sources.limitations: Project description does not establish completion or measured resilience benefits.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Georgia
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical hazard impacts and current exposure; scenario-based climate and poverty projections to 2030 and 2050.
sources.methodology: Country assessment combines climate, infrastructure and poverty analysis using household and hazard data.
sources.limitations: Modeled regional estimates may mask within-region variation.

sources.title: A People-Centered Approach to Inclusive Growth, Sustainability and Human Development in Georgia: Country Analysis Summary Report 2025
sources.organization: United Nations Country Team in Georgia
sources.temporal_coverage: Country analysis published in 2025; summarizes current development, climate and conflict vulnerabilities and institutional status.
sources.methodology: Synthesis of official data, UN research and stakeholder workshops in May-June 2025.
sources.limitations: Intersectional framing, not a measured causal pathway.

sources.title: South Caucasus Climate Impact Profile
sources.organization: adelphi research; authored by Sam Geldin (Climatepedia)
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed regional climate and displacement context; near-term 2020-2039 and medium-term 2040-2059 scenarios.
sources.methodology: Regional synthesis of observed climate, projections and sectoral impacts across three countries.
sources.limitations: Not all cross-country findings are Georgia-specific; IDPs are localized broadly.

sources.title: Reducing the Risk of Climate-Driven Disasters in Georgia
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme and Government of Georgia
sources.temporal_coverage: Ongoing programme listed for December 2018-January 2028; page reports implementation outputs and status as accessed on 2026-10-27.
sources.methodology: UNDP page reports programme implementation outputs and status.
sources.limitations: Self-reported; update date unstated, no independent outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Impacts of Climate Change on Georgia’s Coastal Zone: Vulnerability Assessment and Adaptation Options
sources.temporal_coverage: 2020 coastal vulnerability study; includes observed 2017 degradation estimates and projections based mainly on 2015 climate models.
sources.methodology: Reviews climate projections, coastal risks and sector impacts with expert input, consultations and cost-of-environmental-degradation analysis.
sources.limitations: Regional projections use simplified assumptions; 2017 degradation estimates are not disaggregated by municipality.

sources.title: Ghana Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical flood impacts; modelled poverty impacts to 2050
sources.methodology: World Bank CCDR with climate-risk, economic, and poverty analysis.
sources.limitations: The cited poverty effects are modelled; the coastal and annual flood figures are national-level estimates.

sources.title: Climate-Proofing Northern Ghana’s Future: Investing in Resilient Livelihoods and Infrastructure
sources.organization: National Development Planning Commission (Ghana), prepared for the SOCO project
geographic_coverage: 48 districts across five northern regions and Oti Region
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical droughts 1981–2019; 2024 drought and flood reporting; projection to 2080
sources.methodology: Policy brief reports a mixed-method study with geospatial analysis and interviews involving 210 participants.
sources.limitations: Reported district and event findings are not a national causal estimate; the cited 2080 risk passage does not identify its projection scenario.

sources.title: Ghana’s Updated Nationally Determined Contribution under the Paris Agreement (2020–2030)
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC policy and implementation period 2020–2030
sources.methodology: Government NDC setting out mitigation and adaptation actions, institutional responsibilities, and intended coverage.
sources.limitations: The beneficiary figure is a planned reach, not an independently verified result.

sources.title: Ghana’s first biennial transparency report to the UNFCCC under Article 13 of the Paris Agreement
sources.organization: Environmental Protection Agency, Ghana; Ministry of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate impacts, adaptation progress and institutional gaps reported through 2024
sources.methodology: EPA’s first UNFCCC BTR used an 18-month interagency reporting process with technical and stakeholder review.
sources.limitations: The local vulnerability ranking summarizes a cited 2024 assessment; the BTR also reports local data, funding and capacity gaps.

sources.title: Climate Change Vulnerability Assessment for the Kintampo Municipal Assembly
sources.organization: Government of Ghana, Environmental Protection Agency; authored by Yaw Agyeman Boafo for Foresight Planners and Research Africa Limited
sources.temporal_coverage: Household and qualitative assessment in 2022; historical climate review 1980–2020; projections through 2100
sources.methodology: Mixed qualitative and quantitative municipal assessment, including a 153-household survey in nine purposively selected communities, interviews and participatory mapping.
sources.limitations: Community rankings are based on a purposive, small-area sample and the report’s composite indices; they are not municipality-wide probability estimates.

sources.title: Farmer-herder conflicts in northern Ghana amid climate change: causes and policy responses
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate and conflict mechanisms and local responses reported through 2022
sources.methodology: Case-based policy brief draws on police and chiefs’ records, interviews, cited research and northern climate trends; it is not a national causal estimate.
sources.limitations: The author identifies political, tenure and identity drivers alongside climate and warns local cases may be under-reported.

sources.title: Ghana Disaster Management and Risk Finance Strategy Framework and Implementation Plan (2025–2030)
sources.organization: Government of Ghana, National Disaster Management Organisation, with technical support from UNDP’s Insurance and Risk Finance Facility
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional disaster risk and coping-capacity baseline based on 2021 assessment; framework and implementation plan for 2025–2030
sources.methodology: Regional profile builds on the 2021 PDC-NADMO Risk and Vulnerability Assessment and Disaster Management Analysis.
sources.limitations: Indices are region-level summaries, not district estimates; an approved strategy does not establish implementation or outcomes.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Guinea
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate projections through the 2060s and 2090s; macroeconomic modelling to 2050
sources.methodology: CCDR combines climate-risk analysis with CC-MFMod macroeconomic and fiscal modelling.
sources.limitations: Rainfall projections are uncertain; scenario results are model estimates, not observed impacts.

sources.title: CDN 3.0 de la République de Guinée
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Guinea
geographic_coverage: Conakry, Forécariah, Boffa, and Kamsar coastal areas
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate events reported for 2024–2025; proposed NDC implementation period 2026–2035
sources.methodology: Government NDC 3.0 summarizes sectoral climate risks, vulnerabilities, and proposed adaptation actions.
sources.limitations: Government-reported impacts and proposed actions; independent validation absent.

sources.title: 2025-2026 IFRC network country plan: Guinea
sources.organization: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, in support of the Red Cross Society of Guinea
sources.temporal_coverage: Reported 2024 flood events and response; 2025–2026 network plan
sources.methodology: Plan combines situational analysis and Red Cross operational reporting.
sources.limitations: No probability survey or independent outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Guinea: Selected Issues, IMF Country Report No. 24/131
sources.temporal_coverage: Hazard and coping-capacity context; macroeconomic adaptation simulations for 2024 onward
sources.methodology: IMF staff analysis of climate-risk indicators and DIGNAD macroeconomic scenario simulations.
sources.limitations: Comparative and modeled results are national macroeconomic analysis, not local household evidence.

sources.title: The Gambia Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate and agricultural trends; modelled poverty effects to 2050; climate scenarios through the second half of the century
sources.methodology: CCDR combines climate projections with economic, poverty, and development analysis.
sources.limitations: Rainfall projections are indicative; poverty modelling omits some non-labour and disaster-asset effects.

sources.title: The Gambia Floods Rapid Needs Assessment Report
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), with UNDAC and national counterparts
sources.temporal_coverage: Floods of July–August 2022; assessment published January 2023
sources.methodology: Rapid needs assessment drawing on national disaster-management data, a perception survey, and secondary-source review.
sources.limitations: Affected and displaced counts are assessment estimates; the inspected report does not attribute the floods to climate change.

sources.title: The Gambia Second Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate vulnerability and policy document; dated 2021
sources.methodology: Government NDC describing national climate vulnerabilities and commitments.
sources.limitations: The cited passage is a qualitative national assessment and does not quantify the exposed population or attribute specific impacts.

sources.title: National Disaster Risk Management Policy 2024–2033
sources.organization: National Disaster Management Agency, The Gambia
sources.temporal_coverage: Disaster impacts and implementation review through 2022; policy period 2024–2033
sources.methodology: Review of prior implementation, agency interviews and regional consultations.
sources.limitations: No outcome evaluation or household measures.

sources.title: The Gambia National Climate Hazard Assessment: Technical Report
sources.organization: Global Center on Adaptation, with World Bank and Government of The Gambia collaboration
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed reference conditions and modeled climate/flood hazards through 2100, with focus on 2050
sources.methodology: Combines observational data, climate projections and mapped flood scenarios.
sources.limitations: Hazard models do not measure household impacts or conflict outcomes.

sources.title: The Gambia: Climate Policy Diagnostic, High-Level Summary Technical Assistance Report
sources.organization: International Monetary Fund, Fiscal Affairs Department
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate-policy and institutional diagnostic, 2024
sources.methodology: High-level summary of IMF technical assistance requested by the Gambian authorities.
sources.limitations: National diagnostic; not a subnational or event-level causal study.

sources.title: Guinea-Bissau’s NDC 3.0
sources.organization: Government of Guinea-Bissau; submitted to the UNFCCC
sources.temporal_coverage: Mangrove change 2001–2021; adaptation targets through 2035
sources.methodology: Government NDC summarizes coastal and marine vulnerability and adaptation targets.
sources.limitations: The PDF labels itself draft, although the UNFCCC registry records the submission as active.

sources.title: Fourth National Communication Report (NC4) to the UNFCCC
sources.organization: Government of Guinea-Bissau, Ministry of Environment, Biodiversity and Climate Action; UNEP and GEF provided technical and financial support
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed impacts and climate vulnerabilities reported in the 2025 national communication
sources.methodology: Government national communication with participatory preparation and sectoral vulnerability assessment.
sources.limitations: The report reserves all rights and requires prior authorization for reproduction; reported impacts are not independently validated here.

sources.title: Guinea-Bissau: 2020 Updated NDC
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate projections for 2016–2045 and 2046–2075
sources.methodology: Government NDC reports national and regional climate projections and vulnerability assessments.
sources.limitations: Projection uncertainty is noted; the cited passages do not quantify resulting damages.

sources.title: Guinea-Bissau Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Current diagnostics and modeled climate, mobility and development effects through 2050 and 2100
sources.methodology: Country climate-development diagnostic with modeled impacts and fragility review.
sources.limitations: National analysis; some local and farmer-herder links are conditional.

sources.title: The Sea Swallowed our Houses and Rice Fields: The Vulnerability to Climate Change of Coastal People in Guinea-Bissau, West Africa
sources.organization: Marina Padrão Temudo and Ana I. R. Cabral, University of Lisbon; Pedro Reis, National Institute of Agricultural and Veterinary Research
sources.temporal_coverage: Djobel household survey in 2017; Diola livelihoods research 2017–2019 and follow-up fieldwork through 2022
sources.methodology: All-household Djobel survey, interviews across five villages, repeated fieldwork and land-cover mapping.
sources.limitations: Single island-village case; conflict history includes qualitative accounts and cited earlier records.

sources.title: Guinea-Bissau country strategic plan (2023–2027)
sources.temporal_coverage: Country analysis and prior flood impacts; planned WFP programming for 2023–2027
sources.methodology: WFP country plan informed by country analysis and partner consultations in May 2022.
sources.limitations: Plan commitments are not implementation or impact evidence; cited flood totals are not locally disaggregated.

sources.title: Country Hydromet Diagnostics: Guinea-Bissau Peer Review Report
sources.organization: Systematic Observations Financing Facility and World Meteorological Organization, with Guinea-Bissau National Meteorological Institute
sources.temporal_coverage: Hydrometeorological-service capacity and observation network, assessed in 2024
sources.methodology: Standardized WMO Country Hydromet Diagnostics using national-service information and peer review.
sources.limitations: National service diagnostic; it does not measure community receipt of forecasts or warnings.

sources.title: First National Communication to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
sources.organization: Republic of Equatorial Guinea, Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Forests and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate and institutional assessment published in 2019; some baselines cite the 2013 adaptation plan.
sources.methodology: National climate communication with sector analyses and proposed adaptation priorities.
sources.limitations: Institutional conditions and proposals are historical; manager-level water conflict is not armed conflict.

sources.title: Contribuciones Determinadas a Nivel Nacional (CDN), actualización 2022

sources.temporal_coverage: IPC acute food-insecurity analysis valid April 2026–February 2027, released August 2026.
sources.methodology: Directly opened IPC country-analysis page reporting phase classifications, population estimates and recommendations.

sources.title: Resilience in action: Strengthening local capacity in Guyana
sources.temporal_coverage: Local resilience engagement initiated in 2025 and described inMay 2026.
sources.methodology: Account of local risk assessments and stakeholder engagement.
sources.limitations: Reported engagement and planning, not an independent impact evaluation.

sources.temporal_coverage: Structural coastal exposure and adaptation priorities assessed in 2026.
sources.methodology: Publisher summary drawing on research, government documents and stakeholder engagement.

sources.title: Guyana to strengthen coastal resilience and adaptation
sources.temporal_coverage: Coastal drainage constraints and project design described inJune 2024.

sources.temporal_coverage: Historical and institutional evidence; retain dates stated in individual claims.
sources.methodology: Desk review, stakeholder consultations and semi-quantitative institutional-capacity scoring.

sources.temporal_coverage: Historical and institutional evidence; retain dates stated in individual claims.

sources.temporal_coverage: Historical and institutional evidence; retain dates stated in individual claims.

sources.limitations: Full linked PDF failed to open; community reports are historical.

sources.title: Accelerating climate action will help Honduras achieve inclusive and resilient growth
sources.temporal_coverage: CCDR findings summarized inMay 2023; long-term development risks.
sources.methodology: Publisher's substantive CCDR summary.
sources.limitations: Summary inspected, not full CCDR; qualitative risk statements are not measured causal effects. Body publication date differs from URL date.

sources.title: Honduras country overview
sources.temporal_coverage: Undated country page describing 2024-2025 conditions, accessed26October 2026.

sources.title: Honduras overview
sources.temporal_coverage: Overview updated6October 2026.
sources.methodology: World Bank country diagnostic summary.
sources.limitations: Broad national context does not establish site-level conditions or climate causation.

sources.temporal_coverage: Retain the dated scope of individual claims; no extrapolation to present conditions.

sources.title: La paradoja del sur de Honduras: riqueza geoestratégica y deuda social en Choluteca y Valle
sources.temporal_coverage: Retain the dated scope of individual claims; no extrapolation to present conditions.
