sources.methodology: Interviews, questionnaire, workshops and cognitive mapping; 12 stakeholder representatives in key workshops
sources.limitations: Small qualitative sample; important political actors excluded/unavailable; very old relative to 2026 conditions; no causal identification. Author-uploaded published full text was inspected on ResearchGate. LSE institutional metadata confirms the 2011 publication; its accepted-version PDF could not be fetched. Author upload is not redistribution permission.

sources.title: *Compounding Vulnerability: Impacts of Climate Change on Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank*
sources.organization: Mason, Zeitoun & Mimi; *Journal of Palestine Studies*
geographic_coverage: Gaza and selected West Bank localities
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly evidence assembled around 2008-2011
sources.methodology: Analysis of UNDP consultations and supporting literature/case evidence
sources.limitations: Qualitative and interpretive; locality-specific; pre-2023 and not a national causal study. Published full article inspected at Columbia's journal archive. The opening notice reserves all rights and directs reproduction-permission requests to the publisher.

sources.title: *The political economy of water and sanitation in Palestine’s Gaza Strip: A scoping review*
sources.temporal_coverage: Literature spanning roughly two decades
sources.methodology: Scoping review of 17 peer-reviewed and 37 grey-literature sources
sources.limitations: Heterogeneous literature, much of it low-to-moderate direct relevance; political-economy synthesis rather than causal impact evaluation. Article copyright notice explicitly grants Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

sources.title: *ICR Review: Water Supply & Sewage System Improvement (P101289)*
sources.temporal_coverage: Project period through 2017, including 2014 conflict
sources.methodology: Independent desk review of implementation completion evidence and results framework
sources.limitations: Pre-2023; some outcome data weak; focused on one WASH project, not climate adaptation as a whole.

sources.title: *Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment - Gaza Strip, April 2026*
sources.organization: World Bank, United Nations and European Union
sources.temporal_coverage: Conflict impacts Oct 2023-Oct 2025
sources.methodology: Remote sensing, ground-verified information and standard RDNA damage/loss/needs methodology across 17 sectors
sources.limitations: Access constraints required substantial remote assessment; authors call for later on-the-ground sector assessments; conflict damage is not climate damage. The World Bank metadata page and continuous official UN executive-summary extract were inspected; direct UN PDF fetch returned 403 and UNmissions fetch was unavailable. No claim of full-PDF inspection; the WASH-needs table figure was removed.

sources.title: *Economic Update on the West Bank and Gaza*
geographic_coverage: West Bank and Gaza, separately where data permit
sources.temporal_coverage: Information through end-Apr 2026; principal economic data through 2025/Q1 2026
sources.methodology: Macro-fiscal, labour, financial, energy and social-sector monitoring drawing on official and partner data
sources.limitations: Rapidly changing conflict/access context; economic monitoring, not a climate or impact evaluation.

sources.title: *Humanitarian Situation Report - 23 July 2026*
geographic_coverage: Gaza and West Bank; detailed West Bank localities
sources.temporal_coverage: West Bank reporting primarily 14-20 Jul 2026; cumulative indicators
sources.methodology: OCHA/cluster operational reporting, incident monitoring and partner data
sources.limitations: Humanitarian monitoring rather than causal research; data can be revised; politically sensitive claims require attribution. Report title/reference date is 23 July 2026; webpage display date is 25 July 2026.

sources.title: *Humanitarian Situation Update - Analysis of the Response to the Needs of Children at Mid-year 2026*
sources.temporal_coverage: Through 17 Jul 2026
sources.methodology: UNICEF operational monitoring and partner/sector estimates
sources.limitations: Humanitarian operational estimates; no climate attribution or counterfactual evaluation.

sources.title: *Gaza Strip: Acute Food Insecurity Situation for 16 April-30 June 2026 and Projection for 1 July-31 December 2026*
sources.temporal_coverage: 16 Apr-31 Dec 2026
sources.methodology: IPC evidence-convergence classification and projection
sources.limitations: Projection depends on scenario assumptions; improvement attributed by IPC to assistance is synthesis, not randomized causal evaluation.

sources.title: *UNICEF in the State of Palestine Humanitarian Situation Update - The West Bank*
geographic_coverage: West Bank including East Jerusalem; Area C/Jordan Valley emphasis
sources.temporal_coverage: Through 30 Apr 2026
sources.methodology: UNICEF operational and partner monitoring
sources.limitations: Webpage publication metadata and stated reporting period are inconsistent; humanitarian estimates rather than climate-specific research. Reporting period 30 April 2026 governs use of its figures; no publication-day inference was made.

sources.title: Crop Mapping in Palestine for Winter and Spring Seasons 2023–24
sources.organization: Applied Research Institute–Jerusalem, Food and Agriculture Organization, Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, and Palestinian Water Authority
sources.temporal_coverage: Jericho winter 2023–2024 and spring 2024 crop mapping and field surveys.
sources.methodology: ARIJ, FAO, the agriculture ministry and water authority used Sentinel-2 imagery, field surveys and 366 ground-truth points.
sources.limitations: The page intro refers to 2025 mapping, unlike its title and detailed 2023–2024 survey dates; findings are Jericho-specific.

sources.title: Humanitarian Situation Update #314: West Bank
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, occupied Palestinian territory
sources.temporal_coverage: Humanitarian and water-access conditions reported through 14 August 2025, with some water analysis from early 2025.
sources.methodology: OCHA situation update drawing on WASH Cluster analysis, partner reporting and documented incidents.
sources.limitations: Operational reporting is time-bounded; water-shortage drivers and access varied by community.

sources.title: Enhancing Adaptation Planning and Adoption of Climate Resilient Agriculture in Palestine
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: Project page lists a period from 25 August 2020 through 24 August 2025.
sources.methodology: FAO project summary describing the proposal's objective, partners, budget and stated dates.
sources.limitations: Page states planned objectives but does not document implementation or outcomes.

sources.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Romania 2026, Enhancing resilience to climate risks
sources.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sources.temporal_coverage: National heat-stress data through 2024; disaster records 1980–2023; flood-plan implementation status and adaptation discussion in the 2026 survey.
sources.methodology: OECD survey synthesizes climate indicators, national records and cited sectoral studies.
sources.limitations: Loss and exposure estimates are national or basin-scale; the report does not evaluate each local project.

sources.title: Assessment of progress on climate adaptation in the individual Member States according to the European Climate Law
sources.temporal_coverage: Assessment of Romania's adaptation reports for 2021 and 2023; covers reported projections, institutions and municipal initiatives.
sources.methodology: Commission assessed Romania's 2021 and 2023 EU Climate Law adaptation submissions.
sources.limitations: Implementation and impact detail are often unavailable.

sources.title: UCPM Peer Review Report: Romania 2023
sources.organization: European Commission, Union Civil Protection Mechanism Peer Review Programme
sources.temporal_coverage: Disaster-risk-management peer review conducted in 2023; country-profile annex includes indicators based on 2015–2022 data and mid-century scenarios.
sources.methodology: EU civil-protection peer review drew on Romanian authorities and stakeholder consultations and includes a country-profile annex.
sources.limitations: The annex compiles external risk indices; its conflict projection does not identify a mechanism or model details.

sources.title: România și-ar putea îmbunătăți substanțial nivelul de trai concomitent cu decarbonizarea economiei până în 2050: raportul Grupului Banca Mondială
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank summary of its October 2023 Romania Country Climate and Development Report and selected recommendations.
sources.methodology: World Bank press release summarizes findings and recommendations from its 2023 Romania CCDR.
sources.limitations: Press release is a summary; the detailed report PDF was not accessible.

sources.title: Romania, EU Mission on Adaptation to Climate Change portal
sources.organization: European Commission, Directorate-General for Climate Action
sources.temporal_coverage: Portal counts and funding displayed in June 2026; localized mountain-meadow adaptation example in Râu Sadului and Cristian.
sources.methodology: EU Mission portal lists Romanian adaptation participants, funding and example projects.
sources.limitations: Portal stories are selected examples, not impact evaluations.

sources.title: Доклад об особенностях климата на территории Российской Федерации за 2024 год
sources.organization: Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring (Roshydromet)
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate monitoring for 2024; permafrost active-layer trends for 2005–2024; crop precipitation anomalies relative to 1991–2020.
sources.methodology: Official national climate-monitoring report using station observations, regional aggregates, and permafrost monitoring sites.
sources.limitations: The report does not attribute individual weather events to climate change; permafrost monitoring covers few sites and uneven time series.

sources.title: State Report on the Protection of the Population and Territories of the Russian Federation from Natural and Technogenic Emergencies in 2024
sources.organization: Ministry of the Russian Federation for Civil Defence, Emergencies and Elimination of Consequences of Natural Disasters (EMERCOM)
sources.temporal_coverage: Emergency preparedness, disaster response and impacts recorded in 2024.
sources.methodology: Annual national government report compiling regional emergency preparedness, incident records and response operations.
sources.limitations: Administrative and operational reporting; the cited wildfire and flood-preparedness passages do not assess climate attribution.

sources.title: Second Nationally Determined Contribution of the Russian Federation as part of the implementation of the Paris Agreement
sources.temporal_coverage: Government submission in 2025; includes warming observations since the mid-1970s and adaptation arrangements through 2025.
sources.methodology: Government submission summarizing observed trends, adaptation plans and selected practices.
sources.limitations: Self-reported policies; second-stage plan ended in 2025 and later status was not checked.

sources.title: Heuristic relative assessment of climate risks in Russian regions
sources.organization: Higher School of Economics; article published in Science of the Total Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: Current exposure and vulnerability indicators with climate-hazard projections to mid-century under multiple SSP scenarios.
sources.methodology: Publisher abstract describes heuristic regional risk ranking using hazard, exposure and vulnerability indicators.
sources.limitations: Full article was not inspected; the abstract notes incomplete spatial economic data and no quantified damage functions.

sources.title: Adapting to what? Regional climate policy in Russia
sources.organization: Fridtjof Nansen Institute; article published in Energy Policy
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional adaptation policies analyzed in an article published online 17 April 2026.
sources.methodology: Publisher abstract summarizes regional climate adaptation policies, including Yamal-Nenets.
sources.limitations: Only the publisher abstract was inspected; no independent outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Climate risks
sources.temporal_coverage: Bank of Russia climate-risk analysis, stress tests and financial-institution survey reported through 2024; one modeled horizon is 2030–2040.
sources.methodology: Official central-bank page summarizing climate-risk analysis, stress tests and a survey of financial institutions.
sources.limitations: Underlying stress-test and survey reports were not reviewed; the 2030–2040 transition-risk estimates are described as preliminary.

sources.title: Rwanda's 2035 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0)
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate/disaster information and projections through 2050 reported in 2025
sources.methodology: NDC compiles national climate records, cited studies and adaptation priorities.
sources.limitations: Cited disaster estimates do not establish climate effects on conflict.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Rwanda - Technical Appendix
sources.temporal_coverage: Modeled crop and macroeconomic impacts under climate scenarios through 2050 and 2100
sources.methodology: Technical appendix uses Rwanda-specific crop, labor, health and flood damage functions in a computable general-equilibrium model.
sources.limitations: Scenario-dependent model using CMIP5 projections and a 2017 social accounting matrix; results are not observed impacts.

sources.title: Assessing Community Vulnerability to Landslide and Flood in Northwestern Rwanda
sources.organization: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction; UCLouvain repository
sources.temporal_coverage: Household survey conducted May-July 2023; article published 2025.
sources.methodology: Repository abstract reports a 904-household survey across 50 cells and principal component analysis.
sources.limitations: Only the repository abstract was inspected; its linked full-text PDF returned HTTP 502, and the abstract does not name the higher-risk cells.

sources.title: Climate vulnerability in Rwanda
sources.temporal_coverage: District assessment published in 2026; the publisher page describes change over the previous five years without specifying those years.
sources.methodology: Publisher summary describes mixed quantitative and qualitative research on district climate vulnerability and grassroots policy implementation.
sources.limitations: The publisher page's detailed summary was inspected, but its linked full report download failed; the summary omits the sample design and index formula.

sources.title: Rwanda NDC Deep Dive: Advancing Financial Innovation to Scale up Climate Action (P172153), Implementation Completion and Results Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Implementation and results of the NDC Deep Dive project through 2024.
sources.methodology: World Bank completion report reviews the project's outputs, implementation, outcome indicators, and lessons.
sources.limitations: Project-specific results do not establish national adaptation effects; the report notes that the weather-information system's use and effectiveness could not be verified.

sources.title: Rwanda Emergency Connectivity Restoration Project (RECOR): Environmental and Social Management Framework (Draft)
sources.temporal_coverage: Draft project framework dated December 2024; includes May 2023 disaster impacts and planned reconstruction measures.
sources.methodology: Draft project environmental and social management framework with national and project-area baseline information and planned risk-management measures.
sources.limitations: Draft and project-specific; some subproject locations were not identified. Its border-conflict statement is contextual, not causal analysis.

sources.title: World Bank Steps Up Support to Increase Rwanda's Resilience to Natural Disasters
sources.temporal_coverage: Board approval announcement dated 2025-09-30.
sources.methodology: World Bank announcement of approved disaster-risk financing and its intended policy pillars.
sources.limitations: The announcement describes approved support and intended systems, not completed activities or measured household outcomes.

sources.title: *Sudan's National Adaptation Plan*
sources.organization: Government of Sudan / HCENR, hosted by UNFCCC
geographic_coverage: National; state components for all 18 states
sources.temporal_coverage: Observations 1961-2010; projections to 2100
sources.methodology: State consultation, vulnerability assessment, station data, CMIP5 GCMs and BCSD downscaling
sources.limitations: Pre-war; CMIP5; six-station baseline; not an evaluation. (UNFCCC1)

sources.title: *Sudan Updated First NDC*
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical assessment plus 2030-2060 sector modelling
sources.methodology: Government synthesis of vulnerability, adaptation priorities and implementation needs
sources.limitations: Predates current war; some national trend statements are not readily reconcilable with the NAP station record; programme/self-report evidence. (UNFCCC2)

sources.title: *Climate-Fragility Risk Brief: Sudan*
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly pre-2020 evidence
sources.methodology: Literature and expert synthesis
sources.limitations: Pre-war political/security setting; secondary synthesis rather than causal evaluation. (Climate-Diplomacy7)

sources.title: *Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Sudan*
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly pre-2022
sources.methodology: Research synthesis and policy analysis
sources.limitations: Predates April 2023 war; some institutional recommendations refer to arrangements that later changed. (NUPI8)

sources.title: *How does climate exacerbate root causes of conflict in Sudan? Climate Security Pathway Analysis*
geographic_coverage: Sudan; emphasis on Darfur, Kordofan, Blue Nile, Kassala
sources.temporal_coverage: Literature through early 2023; workshop Mar 2023
sources.methodology: Systematic literature interpretation plus stakeholder workshop
sources.limitations: Completed around onset of current war; mechanisms include workshop judgement and older studies; not causal impact evaluation. (CGSpace9)

sources.title: *Climate Change, Conflicts and Food Security in North Darfur State, Sudan: Risks and Implications*
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate/crop series 2000-2024; household survey 2025
sources.methodology: Al Fashir station data; RAI; crop-yield analysis; internet-based IDP household questionnaire
sources.limitations: Single-state study; only Al Fashir station used for drought analysis; internet survey during conflict/siege; no national inference warranted. (CMI - Chr. Michelsen Institute10)

sources.title: *Famine Review Committee: Sudan, October 2025 - Conclusions and Recommendations*
geographic_coverage: El Fasher, Kadugli, Dilling, Western Nuba Mountains and wider risk areas
sources.temporal_coverage: Sep 2025; projection Oct 2025-Jan 2026
sources.methodology: FRC review, multiple outcome datasets, extrapolation, key informants and expert judgement under access constraints
sources.limitations: Severe access/data constraints; FRC explicitly declined longer projection in some areas because conflict was too volatile. (IPCinfo5)

sources.title: *Three years on, war-weary Sudanese remain on the move*
sources.temporal_coverage: Apr 2023-Apr 2026
sources.methodology: UNHCR operational displacement monitoring / briefing
sources.limitations: Fast-changing operational figures; not a climate-attribution source. (UNHCR3)

sources.title: *Terminal Evaluation Report: Climate Risk Finance for Sustainable and Climate Resilient Rainfed Farming and Pastoral Systems, Sudan*
geographic_coverage: Six states: River Nile, North Kordofan, Gedarif, South Darfur, Kassala, White Nile
sources.temporal_coverage: Programme 2014-2020
sources.methodology: UNDP/GEF evaluation criteria; documents, interviews and limited field evidence
sources.limitations: Pre-war; commissioned within UNDP/GEF evaluation system; some respondents/financial records unavailable; COVID reduced field sample. (UNDP IEO Evaluation Resource Center11)

sources.title: *Environmental degradation and conflict in Darfur: implications for peace and recovery*
sources.organization: Humanitarian Practice Network / ODI; author Brendan Bromwich, UNEP
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly 2000s Darfur conflict
sources.methodology: Field-informed specialist synthesis
sources.limitations: Foundational but old; environmental scarcity is broader than anthropogenic climate change; Darfur-specific. (Humanitarian Practice Network12)

sources.title: *Sudan - Enhancing Community Resilience Project (P181490), Additional Financing 3 Project Paper*
geographic_coverage: Kassala, Northern, River Nile and other project locations
sources.temporal_coverage: 2024-2028; ISR through 20 Jan 2026
sources.methodology: Project monitoring, implementation ratings, risk analysis and results framework
sources.limitations: Full project paper inspected; marked Official Use Only/restricted distribution. Derived summaries only.

sources.title: *New FAO-WFP report warns worsening hunger puts 13 hotspots at significant risk*
geographic_coverage: National with North/South Darfur and South Kordofan hotspots
sources.temporal_coverage: Jun-Nov 2026; some Sudan projections to Jan 2027
sources.methodology: GNAFC consensus early warning using field/technical teams and conflict, economic and natural-hazard analysts
sources.limitations: Forward-looking; not designed to isolate climate effects from conflict; report PDF access was blocked by the browser, but publication/release content was accessible. (World Food Programme14)

sources.title: *Risk of Famine persists as nearly 19.5 million people face acute food insecurity in Sudan*
sources.temporal_coverage: Current to May 2026
sources.methodology: IPC and UN operational evidence
sources.limitations: Humanitarian operational source; rapidly changing; no climate attribution. (World Food Programme15)

sources.title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Sudan
sources.organization: Norwegian Institute of International Affairs; Stockholm International Peace Research Institute
sources.temporal_coverage: Fact sheet published May 2022; reports historical climate, displacement, and resource-conflict evidence.
sources.methodology: NUPI-SIPRI country fact sheet synthesizes cited climate, displacement, land-use, and conflict evidence.
sources.limitations: Secondary synthesis; it rejects a direct climate-conflict causal claim and identifies political, land-use, marginalization, and governance factors.

sources.title: Building resilience in the face of climate change within traditional rain-fed agricultural and pastoral systems in Sudan
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme; Higher Council for Environment and Natural Resources
sources.temporal_coverage: Green Climate Fund project listed as 2020-2027; page has no publication/update date.
sources.methodology: UNDP project page describes climate-risk context, planned activities, intended water-conflict mechanism, and expected results.
sources.limitations: The page lists three states in project details but nine states in expected results; it describes intentions and targets, not independently verified delivery or effects.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief on Sudan
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: Reference date September 24, 2026; includes 2025 harvest and 2026 rainy-season/lean-season assessments.
sources.methodology: FAO brief combines IPC, crop assessments, rainfall, and Agricultural Stress Index monitoring.
sources.limitations: No national lean-season projection was made owing to data gaps; famine-risk figures are scenario-based.

sources.title: Restoring Trade and Livelihoods: Sudan's Agri-food and Market Resilience Analysis (SAMRA)
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme; International Trade Centre
sources.temporal_coverage: Report published August 2026; combines conflict-era consultations and 2024-2026 agriculture, production, and market information.
sources.methodology: UNDP-ITC analyzes production, trade, prices, and over 80 in-person/remote stakeholder consultations.
sources.limitations: Access/data gaps remain; conflict-state consultations were remote and percentages are not representative household estimates.

sources.title: Senegal Country Climate and Development Report: Executive Summary
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed socioeconomic vulnerability and modeled climate impacts through 2050
sources.methodology: Executive summary reports CCDR climate and macroeconomic modeling results.
sources.limitations: Only summary opened; inherited West Bank/Gaza and Madagascar footer references raise source-quality concerns.

sources.title: Diagnostic sur le Financement des Risques Climatiques et de Catastrophes au Sénégal
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical hazard impacts and forward climate-risk analysis in the 2024 diagnostic
sources.methodology: World Bank disaster-risk financing diagnostic combines historical loss review and probabilistic risk analysis.
sources.limitations: Historical event and modeled risk estimates use different methods and periods; the report notes data-quality dependence for modeled results.

sources.title: Contribution Déterminée au Niveau National du Sénégal: Document approuvé – décembre 2020
sources.organization: Republic of Senegal; submitted to the UNFCCC
sources.temporal_coverage: Government NDC climate-risk projections and adaptation commitments through 2030
sources.methodology: Government NDC summarizes observed climate impacts and modeled regional climate risks.
sources.limitations: NDC projections are dated and should not be read as current observations or as evaluated results.

sources.title: Don't blame it on ethnicity: The role of group identities and climate risks in farmer-herder relations in Senegal
sources.organization: Journal of Peace Research; Wageningen University & Research
geographic_coverage: Ferlo Desert silvopastoral zone in Louga Region
sources.temporal_coverage: Field data collected October-November 2022; article published November 2025.
sources.methodology: Public-good experiment with 332 analyzed participants after five exclusions from 337;14 focus groups. Coordinator read the publisher DOI redirect.
sources.limitations: Artificial collective-risk treatment and game cooperation are not observed climate impacts or violence; study municipalities are unnamed.

sources.title: Senegal, Evaluation of Green Climate Fund Project: 2020-2024
sources.temporal_coverage: R4 project implementation 2020-01-14 to 2024-10-14; evaluation conducted July 2024-February 2025.
sources.methodology: WFP publisher summary of a decentralized, end-of-project evaluation; full evaluation methods were not accessible.
sources.limitations: The publisher summary omits design details, sample, subgroup estimates and effect sizes; the linked evaluation PDF required JavaScript verification.

sources.title: Strengthening adaptive and socio-economic capacities of women and youth in the village of Mbam through the Integrated Resilience Garden approach
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), SAGA 2
sources.temporal_coverage: Project page lists start date 2024-09-06 and end date 2026-05-31, while still displaying status as active.
sources.methodology: Official FAO project page describing local objectives, implementation partners and listed activities.
sources.limitations: The page's displayed active status conflicts with its May 2026 end date; listed activities are not independently verified as completed outcomes.

sources.title: Challenges to food security in a changing environment: a community-based participatory research study in Casamance, Senegal (West Africa)
sources.temporal_coverage: Study field period not stated in the article; published 2026-03-31.
sources.methodology: Mixed-method participatory study: 42 exploratory participants, then 234 agricultural interviewees across 13 communities.
sources.limitations: Purposive sample from selected communities; partly self-reported and cross-sectional, limiting generalization.

sources.title: Social Dimensions of Climate Change in Solomon Islands
sources.temporal_coverage: 2022 research summarized in 2023
sources.methodology: Publisher findings from mixed qualitative and quantitative community research.
sources.limitations: Publisher synthesis, not the complete report or a causal evaluation.

sources.title: Inclusive Governance of Natural Resources
sources.temporal_coverage: Undated programme design
sources.methodology: Institutional and customary-tenure diagnosis.
sources.limitations: Design commitments and intended benefits are not verified outcomes.

sources.title: Climate change, conflict and peacebuilding in Solomon Islands
sources.temporal_coverage: March 2019; day not stated
sources.methodology: Authors' publisher summary of a contextual peacebuilding paper.
sources.limitations: Month-only publication date; qualitative potential risks, not event attribution.

sources.title: Implementation Completion and Results Report: Community Resilience to Climate and Disaster Risk Project (P112613)
sources.temporal_coverage: CRISP implementation 2014-2020; report dated 2020-10-26.
sources.methodology: World Bank completion evaluation using project monitoring, beneficiary survey, site visits and economic analysis.
sources.limitations: M&E was rated modest; the 103-person survey was non-representative, and remote-site visits and COVID-19 limited field coverage.

sources.title: Community-based adaptation to climate change in villages of Western Province, Solomon Islands
sources.organization: Marine Pollution Bulletin; Britt Basel, Gillian Goby and Johanna Johnson; hosted by SPREP
sources.temporal_coverage: Community fieldwork and adaptation workshops in 2017; article published in 2020.
sources.methodology: Participatory workshops, interviews and semi-quantitative vulnerability assessment in two Rendova communities.
sources.limitations: Two purposively selected communities had existing leadership and conservation ties; not representative.

sources.title: Climate-related disasters and temperature extremes are not associated with conflict risk in Pacific Island countries
sources.organization: Environment and Security; Tobias Ide, Ore Koren and Luke Derrick
sources.temporal_coverage: Geocoded conflict and climate-event dataset for 2012-2020; article first published online 2026-01-22.
sources.methodology: Original geocoded social-conflict dataset and panel regressions at 0.5-degree cell-year scale across three Pacific countries, with contextual controls and robustness tests.
sources.limitations: Observational panel; Methods specify 2012-2020 but Discussion describes13years/936observations. No direct mechanism test or coverage of organized armed groups.

sources.title: Community-Led Climate Adaptation Projects Strengthen Resilience Across Solomon Islands
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Pacific Office
sources.temporal_coverage: Community-Based Adaptation Phase III investments 2022-2026; closing workshop in June 2026; page dated 2026-08-25.
sources.methodology: Official UNDP programme-completion announcement summarizing community project outputs and a June 2026 closing workshop.
sources.limitations: No evaluation design, baseline or disaggregated beneficiary counts are provided; reported benefits are UNDP's summary, not independent impact estimates.

sources.title: Solomon Islands Advances National Climate Adaptation Planning
sources.organization: Solomon Islands Government, My SIG Services Portal
sources.temporal_coverage: NAP formulation workshop held 2026-10-20; CRVA and SIIVA assessment processes reported as current in October 2026.
sources.methodology: Government announcement summarizing the NAP workshop, the national Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessment, and SIIVA work in two provinces.
sources.limitations: The announcement describes planning and assessment scope, not underlying CRVA or SIIVA findings or evaluated adaptation outcomes.

sources.title: Sierra Leone Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical baseline, 1995-2014 climate reference, school flood data through 2022, and climate/poverty projections to 2050
sources.methodology: CCDR combines climate scenarios and household-linked poverty modeling.
sources.limitations: Rainfall projections are uncertain; poverty results depend on growth and adaptation assumptions.

sources.title: NDC 3.0 of the Republic of Sierra Leone
sources.organization: Republic of Sierra Leone; submitted to the UNFCCC
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC 3.0 risk analysis and planned climate actions for 2025-2035
sources.methodology: Government NDC presents a qualitative conflict-sensitive climate-risk framework and adaptation measures.
sources.limitations: The conflict-risk discussion is a policy framing and illustrative mechanism, not a quantified causal or local empirical assessment.

sources.title: Climate and Health Vulnerability Assessment: Sierra Leone
sources.organization: World Bank Group and Climate Investment Funds, with Sierra Leone Ministry of Health and Sanitation
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate data through 2020; hazard and health-system inputs from varying years; CMIP5 projections for the 2030s and 2050s.
sources.methodology: Assessment combines CRU observations, CMIP5 projections, and health/climate data.
sources.limitations: PDF copyright 2023 differs from filename 2024; exact publication year unresolved. Dated health/admin inputs and limited drought surveillance constrain present-day interpretation.

sources.title: Disaster Risk Financing Strategy and Implementation Plan 2024-2029
sources.organization: Government of Sierra Leone, Ministry of Finance
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical disaster experience through 2022; strategy and implementation period 2024-2029.
sources.methodology: Government strategy compiles NDMA hazard calendars, prior risk assessments and historical disaster-loss data.
sources.limitations: Records are uneven; mapped hazards and losses are not climate-attribution estimates.

sources.title: Sierra Leone Common Country Analysis 2023
sources.organization: United Nations Country Team in Sierra Leone
geographic_coverage: Guinea and Liberia transboundary river basins
sources.temporal_coverage: Country conditions and climate-related sector risks summarized in the 2023 common country analysis; some historical conflict and migration context is included.
sources.methodology: UN Country Team multi-sector synthesis of country context, sector data, policy materials and climate-risk information.
sources.limitations: The analysis calls for better geographically and sex/age-disaggregated data; its climate annex is largely national and does not estimate local conflict effects.

sources.title: Multilateral peacebuilding in practice: addressing farmer-herder disputes along the border of Sierra Leone and Guinea
sources.organization: International Security and Development Center; Thissen et al.
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 research publication summarizing a UN Peacebuilding Fund-supported cross-border project and its evaluation.
sources.methodology: The accessible research summary reports satellite imagery, a household survey and qualitative interviews.
sources.limitations: Only the institute's article summary was accessible; detailed sample, effect sizes and subgroup results could not be checked in the full paper.

sources.title: Sierra Leone, Asset creation and livelihood: evaluation
sources.temporal_coverage: Asset creation and livelihood activities January 2020-December 2023; the page says evaluation fieldwork ran July 2023-July 2024.
sources.methodology: WFP publication page provides a summary of a decentralized evaluation of asset creation and livelihood activities.
sources.limitations: The page date predates its stated evaluation end date; only the online summary was accessible, with no district disaggregation or underlying sample details.

sources.title: Improving Lives and Livelihoods: Poverty and Equity Assessment for El Salvador 2024
sources.temporal_coverage: Poverty and climate analysis published in 2024; includes historical exposure and forward-looking risks.
sources.methodology: Country poverty assessment combining household and climate evidence.
sources.limitations: Conflict links are conditional risks, not measured outcomes.

sources.title: Contribuciones Nacionalmente Determinadas de El Salvador 2025
sources.organization: Government of El Salvador, Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 NDC; adaptation objectives and strategic targets mainly cover 2030–2035.
sources.methodology: Government NDC based on sector and territorial vulnerability analysis and interagency consultation.
sources.limitations: Commitments and planned systems are not evidence of completed results.

sources.title: The World Food Programme's Contribution to Improving the Prospects for Peace in El Salvador
sources.organization: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, with World Food Programme field research
sources.temporal_coverage: Field research conducted in March 2019; findings describe the then-current program and conflict context.
sources.methodology: Two-week country case study using interviews, focus groups, programme review and project-site visits.
sources.limitations: Qualitative, programme-specific and historical (2019).

sources.title: Evaluación de Vulnerabilidad y Adaptación al Cambio Climático en El Salvador
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources of El Salvador; ESSA Technologies Ltd. and associates
sources.temporal_coverage: Municipal vulnerability baseline and projections for 2021–2050 and 2071–2100, published February 2018.
sources.methodology: Indicator-based two-territory municipal assessment with participatory adaptation prioritization.
sources.limitations: Focuses on the AMSS and selected Eastern Dry Corridor municipalities, not all of El Salvador.

sources.title: *Climate Risk Profile Somalia*
sources.organization: Weathering Risk / Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK)
sources.temporal_coverage: Baseline to 2080
sources.methodology: AGRICA methodology; multi-model RCP2.6/RCP6.0 projections plus sector synthesis
sources.limitations: Socioeconomic change not included in climate models; precipitation, river flooding, crop and ecosystem projections have substantial uncertainty; not a current humanitarian assessment.

sources.title: *Somalia's Third Generation Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0)*
sources.organization: Somalia; reproduced by FAO/FAOLEX through InforMEA
sources.temporal_coverage: Strategy 2025-2035
sources.methodology: Policy commitments and planned measures
sources.limitations: Policy intent, not evaluated implementation; accessible page is a UN/FAOLEX reproduction rather than the official UNFCCC PDF. (InforMEA)

sources.title: *Climate-related security risks and peacebuilding in Somalia*
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly historical-2019
sources.methodology: Single-case plausibility probe; qualitative process tracing; literature plus 27 interviews and expert consultations
sources.limitations: Publisher PDF was read in full. Copyright page states all rights reserved; derived summaries only and reuse requires permission.

sources.title: *Environmental Peacemaking in Somalia: Integrated Climate and Conflict Analysis of the Newly Liberated Areas of Hirshabelle and Galmudug*
geographic_coverage: Newly Liberated Areas, Hirshabelle and Galmudug
sources.temporal_coverage: Field/consultation work Aug 2023-Mar 2024
sources.methodology: Literature/regulatory review, expert consultations and Mogadishu stakeholder workshop
sources.limitations: Educational/nonprofit reproduction permitted with acknowledgement; written permission required for resale or other commercial use. No unrestricted open licence asserted.

sources.title: *SWALIM Quarterly Newsletter: Jan-March 2026*
sources.organization: FAO Somalia Water and Land Information Management
sources.temporal_coverage: Jan-Mar 2026
sources.methodology: Combined Drought Index, hydrometeorological monitoring, satellite/DEM analysis, field observers and community feedback
sources.limitations: Operational quarterly monitoring, not climate attribution or long-term projection.

sources.title: *FAO GIEWS Country Brief: Somalia*
geographic_coverage: National with market and livelihood-zone examples
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly 2025-Mar 2026
sources.methodology: Cereal balance, food-price monitoring, Earth observation and IPC evidence
sources.limitations: The official historical 11 March 2026 edition was inspected through FAO's indexed country-brief service. The rolling country page had advanced to 15 September 2026 and was not treated as verification of the March figures. GIEWS service identifies content as CC BY 4.0.

sources.title: *Somalia IPC Acute Food Insecurity and Acute Malnutrition Analysis - Updated Projection April-June 2026*
sources.organization: Somalia IPC Technical Working Group / IPC partners
sources.temporal_coverage: Apr-Jun 2026; nutrition Jan-Dec 2026
sources.methodology: IPC protocols; government, FAO/FSNAU, WFP, UNICEF, WHO, FEWS NET, REACH and cluster inputs
sources.limitations: Projection conditional on evolving rainfall, prices, assistance and conflict; some areas have scarce evidence due to limited/no humanitarian access.

sources.title: *UNHCR Somalia PSMN 2026 Q2 Report*
sources.methodology: Recorded displacement monitoring
sources.limitations: Web publication page gives high-level result but limited methodology detail; percentage refers to recorded displacement, not population-wide causal attribution. (UNHCR Data Portal)

sources.title: *Support for Strengthening Climate Change Adaptation Planning for the Federal Republic of Somalia*
sources.temporal_coverage: 2020-2024 programme
sources.methodology: Programme diagnostics, institutional reviews and reported outputs
sources.limitations: Mostly programme theory/output reporting; page still says “Under Implementation” despite listed 2020-24 dates; effectiveness not independently evaluated here. (UNDP Climate Change Adaptation)

sources.title: *The World Bank Group in the Federal Republic of Somalia, Fiscal Years 2013-23: Country Program Evaluation*
sources.methodology: Project evidence, secondary datasets, literature review, 43 evaluative reports from 18 partners and interviews
sources.limitations: Evaluates World Bank Group engagement rather than the full Somali institutional/humanitarian system; some outcome evidence originates in project reporting.

sources.title: *Evaluation of Somalia WFP Country Strategic Plan 2022-2025*
sources.temporal_coverage: CSP 2022-25 plus ICSP 2019-21
sources.methodology: Independent evaluation conducted Jun 2024-Mar 2025
sources.limitations: WFP-specific; effectiveness attribution occurs in a highly dynamic multi-actor crisis; resilience and capacity-strengthening results constrained by funding/logistics. (World Food Programme)

sources.title: *Joint Communiqué - Activation of the National Preparedness Plan for Food and Nutrition Security Crises*
sources.organization: Federal Government of Somalia and partners / World Bank host
sources.temporal_coverage: Feb 2026
sources.methodology: Administrative record and response framework
sources.limitations: Evidence of activation, coordination and intended mechanisms - not evidence that the plan subsequently reduced losses. (World Bank)

sources.title: *UNDP Somalia Annual Report 2025*
sources.methodology: UNDP programme monitoring/reporting
sources.limitations: Self-reported outputs/results; no counterfactual; reported peacebuilding and resilience achievements should not be interpreted as independently demonstrated causal effects. (UNDP)

sources.title: Somalia Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), Somalia Humanitarian Country Team, and Somali Disaster Management Agency
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 shock and displacement observations; 2026 humanitarian needs, response planning and access conditions.
sources.methodology: Multi-agency plan synthesizes assessments, displacement tracking and access mapping.
sources.limitations: Operational snapshot; estimates are not climate attribution or independent causal evaluation.

sources.title: Endline Evaluation Report: Building Resilient Communities in Somalia (BRCiS) III
sources.organization: Causal Design, prepared for the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
sources.temporal_coverage: BRCiS III baseline 2024 and endline 2026; programme closed on 31 March 2026.
sources.methodology: Panel survey, focus groups and contribution analysis: 3,889 households across 21 districts.
sources.limitations: Non-counterfactual, self-reported programme results; early closure limits attribution and follow-up.

sources.title: Burning Ground: Tackling Climate Change and Conflict in South-central Somalia
sources.temporal_coverage: Deegan Bile project period and drought context 2021-2024; SIPRI surveys and focus groups in January 2024.
sources.methodology: Literature review, IOM partnership, over 700 survey respondents and six focus groups.
sources.limitations: Close partnership may affect objectivity; 18-month projects; Hirshabelle evaluation was pending.

sources.title: First Biennial Transparency Report of the Republic of Serbia
geographic_coverage: areas south of the Sava and Danube rivers
sources.temporal_coverage: Sectoral climate impacts and adaptation reporting through 2024; crop comparison baseline 2011–2020.
sources.methodology: Government BTR compiles sectoral climate-risk and adaptation reports; full English PDF read.
sources.limitations: National self-report; spatial detail varies. The 2014 flood is not attributed to climate change.

sources.title: Programme for Adaptation to Changed Climate Conditions for 2023–2030
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Serbia; Ministry of Environmental Protection
sources.temporal_coverage: Adaptation programme 2023–2030; first action plan 2024–2026; climate projections through 2081–2100.
sources.methodology: Serbian government programme read in full; English summaries are translated paraphrases.
sources.limitations: Cited studies underpin projections; area shares are not exposed-population estimates.

sources.title: Gender Analysis of the Impact of the 2014 Floods in Serbia
sources.organization: Višnja Baćanović; supported by the OSCE Mission to Serbia
sources.temporal_coverage: Interviews and flood-response observations from May–July 2014; report published 2015.
sources.methodology: Study combines interviews with 78 flood-exposed residents in four municipalities and focus-group input from evacuation-centre volunteers.
sources.limitations: Small event-specific sample; gender-disaggregated administrative records were incomplete. The report does not attribute the flood to climate change.

sources.title: EU for Civil Protection and Disaster Risk Resilience Strengthening in the Republic of Serbia
sources.temporal_coverage: Project ran March 2020–January 2026; page gives no INFORM score reference year.
sources.methodology: Directly read UNDP project-page narrative and impact/status fields.
sources.limitations: Page gives no score vintage or scale and reports project framing rather than evaluated outcomes; INFORM is not an FCV classification.

sources.title: Sustainable Urban and Regional Development Program (SURGE): Annual Report 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank FY2025 programme activities through June 2025; programme extension ended June 2026.
sources.methodology: World Bank report; read full Serbia chapter and FY2025 results.
sources.limitations: Self-reported FY2025 outputs, not resilience outcomes; programme ended June 2026.

sources.title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: South Sudan (2025)
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate, peace, and security conditions synthesized for the 2025 fact sheet.
sources.methodology: SIPRI and partner authors synthesize climate trends, conflict dynamics, institutional context, and policy implications into a country fact sheet with recommended actions.
sources.limitations: The official PDF cover is dated March 2025, while the SIPRI catalogue lists April 2025; publication_date follows the document version. The concise synthesis does not replace review of its underlying sources.

sources.title: Climate Security Risks in South Sudan: An Information Brief (2025)
sources.temporal_coverage: Current climate-security risks and response priorities as assessed in 2025.
sources.methodology: The information brief was jointly developed by UNDP, UNMISS, and the UN Resident Coordinator's Office to synthesize climate-related security risks and strategic interventions for South Sudan.
sources.limitations: This is a short strategic brief rather than a reproducible dataset; its country-level framing can obscure variation among states, livelihood systems, and conflict settings.

sources.title: Joining Forces for a Conflict-Sensitive Flood Response in South Sudan (2025)
geographic_coverage: South Sudan (national and selected flood-affected subnational locations)
sources.temporal_coverage: Lessons from the 2024 flood response and preparedness priorities for the 2025 flood season.
sources.methodology: The article distils a UN Community of Practice discussion and operational examples from UNMISS, OCHA, the UN Country Team, national authorities, and subnational flood taskforces.
sources.limitations: The source is a practice-oriented UN news account, not an independent evaluation; selected operational examples cannot establish how consistently conflict sensitivity was applied nationwide.

sources.title: First National Adaptation Plan for Climate Change Republic of South Sudan
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of South Sudan and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
sources.temporal_coverage: National adaptation priorities for 2021-2025.
sources.methodology: The national planning document organizes adaptation around three resilience pillars and nine priority sectors to guide policy and implementation from national to community level.
sources.limitations: The plan records government priorities and intended actions rather than evaluated adaptation outcomes; implementation progress after its 2021-2025 planning horizon requires separate evidence.

sources.title: South Sudan Second Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of South Sudan and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate commitments and priorities submitted in 2021, principally oriented to 2030.
sources.methodology: The government submission updates the national greenhouse-gas inventory and sets sectoral mitigation, adaptation, and implementation commitments under the Paris Agreement.
sources.limitations: The date recorded is the UNFCCC submission date, 2021-09-21, not the portal file-publication timestamp; an NDC states commitments and assumptions rather than demonstrating achieved results.

sources.title: South Sudan Flood Damage and Needs Assessment Study (2021)
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
geographic_coverage: Three flood-affected payams in South Sudan
sources.temporal_coverage: Impacts of the June-December 2020 floods, with fieldwork from 2021-08-31 to 2021-10-14.
sources.methodology: IOM field-validated the 2020 flood assessment using two quantitative tools, focus-group discussions, and key-informant interviews, consulting more than 1,131 people across three payams.
sources.limitations: The official page states publication year 2021 without an exact month or day, so publication_date preserves year precision; purposive coverage of three payams is not nationally representative.

sources.title: South Sudan UN Common Country Analysis (CCA)
sources.organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator's Office in South Sudan
sources.temporal_coverage: Multisector country context through late 2021, published on the UN portal in 2022.
sources.methodology: The UN country analysis synthesizes political, conflict, humanitarian, socioeconomic, environmental, and institutional evidence to identify constraints to sustainable development.
sources.limitations: The portal publication date, 2022-06-27, is used consistently, while the downloadable document is versioned 2021-12-24; underlying indicators have different reference periods and may have since changed.

sources.title: INFORM South Sudan Country Risk Profile (2021)
sources.temporal_coverage: INFORM 2021 risk profile, including trend displays for 2017-2021.
sources.methodology: INFORM combines standardized indicators of hazard and exposure, vulnerability, and lack of coping capacity into a composite country risk index with peer and trend comparisons.
sources.limitations: The profile identifies version 2021 rather than a dated publication, so publication_date records the stated version year; composite national scores compress indicator uncertainty and subnational disparities.

sources.title: Climate change deepens gender inequality and violence in South Sudan: UNFPA study highlights urgent need for action
sources.organization: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), Sudd Institute, and South Sudan National Bureau of Statistics
sources.temporal_coverage: Study findings released in 2025 on current climate-related gender and violence risks.
sources.methodology: The UN story summarizes a vulnerability study conducted by UNFPA with the Sudd Institute and National Bureau of Statistics in three high-exposure locations, with findings validated in a stakeholder workshop.
sources.limitations: This is a summary rather than the full study methodology; purposive selection of three highly exposed locations and condensed reporting limit national generalization.

sources.title: South Sudan Event Tracking Report 73: Flood Displacements (1-31 December 2024)
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
sources.temporal_coverage: Flood-related displacement events recorded from 2024-12-01 to 2024-12-31.
sources.methodology: IOM DTM enumerators used event tracking to document disaster-related displacement during December 2024 and record affected people's reported priority needs.
sources.limitations: Event tracking is a rapid, period-specific account rather than a complete displacement stock; the 2025-02-10 publication date follows the December 2024 observation period.

sources.title: South Sudan Climatology (ERA5)
sources.organization: World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal
sources.temporal_coverage: ERA5 climatology for 1991-2020 and historical daily data for 1950-2023.
sources.methodology: The World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal presents ERA5 reanalysis-derived South Sudan climatology for 1991-2020 and historical daily data for 1950-2023 at 0.25-degree resolution.
sources.limitations: ERA5 is model-based reanalysis rather than direct station observation, and national summaries can mask subnational variation. This living page can change and has no fixed publication date; publication_date remains null with basis not-stated.

sources.title: South Sudan - Trends & Variability (CMIP6)
sources.organization: World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal
geographic_coverage: South Sudan (national aggregation with mapped subnational detail)
sources.temporal_coverage: CMIP6 reference period 1995-2014 and scenario projections through 2100.
sources.methodology: CMIP6 multi-model ensemble trends, variability, and emergence from historical variability at 0.25-degree resolution across SSPs.
sources.limitations: The accessible page exposed direction, scenario, horizon, and uncertainty but not stable numeric p10, p50, and p90 exports; national aggregation masks local variation.

sources.title: Uplifting Vulnerable South Sudanese Households through Safety Net Assistance
geographic_coverage: Ten project counties in South Sudan
sources.temporal_coverage: South Sudan Safety Net Project implementation and reported results from 2020 to 2023.
sources.methodology: Official results brief using delivery records, monitoring indicators, and selected beneficiary outcome measures.
sources.limitations: Not an independent impact evaluation; selected beneficiaries in ten counties do not establish national or climate-attributable effects.

sources.title: Building community resilience from the ground up in South Sudan
geographic_coverage: Twenty selected counties in South Sudan
sources.temporal_coverage: ECRP implementation from 2020 to 2024 and functionality reporting as of 2024.
sources.methodology: Official feature summarizing project monitoring, infrastructure functionality, flood-protection reach, and community-institution outputs.
sources.limitations: Not an independent evaluation; selected counties, third-party implementation, and output indicators limit generalization and causal interpretation.

sources.title: Narrow Path to Recovery: Finding a Climate-Smart Pathway and Stabilizing South Sudan's Economy
sources.temporal_coverage: Current flood and development conditions summarized from the 2026 CCDR and Public Finance Review.
sources.methodology: Official press release summarizing selected CCDR and Public Finance Review findings.
sources.limitations: Does not expose underlying spatial analysis, model ranges, or source tables and supports only the stated national headline finding.

sources.title: South Sudan Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), on behalf of the Humanitarian Country Team and partners
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 humanitarian conditions and flood/drought observations; 2026 response and logistics planning.
sources.methodology: OCHA consolidated a multi-agency needs assessment and response plan for the Humanitarian Country Team.
sources.limitations: Operational planning synthesis, not a causal evaluation; many figures are regional or national aggregates.

sources.title: Special Report: 2025 FAO/WFP Crop and Food Security Assessment Mission (CFSAM) to the Republic of South Sudan
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and World Food Programme
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 crop season and food-security conditions; IPC outlooks through April-July 2026.
sources.methodology: Mission: 20 crop missions in 44 counties, with about 2,500 farmer interviews and 34 focus groups.
sources.limitations: In insecure areas, phone and committee reports substituted for field visits; food-security estimates combine multiple drivers.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief: South Sudan
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, Global Information and Early Warning System on Food and Agriculture
sources.temporal_coverage: GIEWS reference date 7 September 2026; 2026 crop performance and food-security conditions.
sources.methodology: GIEWS brief synthesizes cereal balances, earth observation, food prices and IPC analysis.
sources.limitations: Rolling dated snapshot; rainfall forecasts and food-security estimates can change as weather, security and markets evolve.

sources.title: Updated NDC 3.0 - Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe
sources.organization: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe; submitted to the UNFCCC
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical flood losses and fisheries impacts; flood-risk estimates to 2050 and 2080
sources.methodology: Government NDC summarizes sector risks, losses and climate projections using cited assessments.
sources.limitations: Several quantified flood and fishery estimates are attributed to external studies, not new NDC analysis.

sources.title: Prosperity for All Saotomeans: Priorities to End Poverty, Promote Growth, and Build Resilience in São Tomé and Príncipe - Systematic Country Diagnostic
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate observations from 1951 to 2010 and country diagnostic published in 2021
sources.methodology: World Bank diagnostic synthesizes country and sector evidence; trends draw on the Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal.
sources.limitations: Climate trends are historical and based on polynomial fits; they do not represent updated observations.

sources.title: West and Central Africa Region Humanitarian Situation Report No. 1: 1 January to 30 June 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional report dated 29 August 2025; São Tomé and Príncipe section covers recurring risks and events in December 2021, May 2024 and 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF operational situation report summarizing country needs, hazards and agency responses for January-June 2025.
sources.limitations: Self-reported operational synthesis; some country hazard details refer to 2021 and 2024 events.

sources.title: Rising Waters, Rising Hopes: Shaping Resilience in São Tomé and Príncipe Through Flood Risk Analysis
sources.organization: World Bank; authors include a Natural Resources Management Specialist and report contributors
sources.temporal_coverage: Summary of World Bank national flood-risk assessment using present-climate data and projections for 2050 and 2080; published 2 May 2024.
sources.methodology: Report-author summary of high-resolution riverine and coastal flood-risk modelling under SSP3-7.0, without additional climate policy.
sources.limitations: Accessible blog summary, not the full technical report; selected household interviews are illustrative, not representative.

sources.title: São Tomé’s Água Grande District advances local disaster resilience
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, Regional Office for Africa
sources.temporal_coverage: District resilience assessment conducted 7-9 September 2026; article dated 6 October 2026.
sources.methodology: UNDRR account of a district scorecard workshop involving public agencies, civil society and sector representatives.
sources.limitations: The account describes an assessment and draft strategy inputs, not an adopted plan or measured resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Enhance Adaptive Capacity to Floods and Water Security in São Tomé and Principe
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Climate Change Adaptation platform; Global Environment Facility project information
sources.temporal_coverage: Project concept/PIF approval shown as June 2024; webpage presents proposed outcomes and beneficiary estimates, not completed results.
sources.methodology: UNDP project-platform summary of the project concept, target population, design and expected outputs.
sources.limitations: The page labels the funding source as pipeline; stated outcomes and beneficiary reach are planned, not evaluated achievements.

sources.title: Suriname signs novel project to strengthen resilience against environmental shocks
sources.temporal_coverage: Flood vulnerabilities and proposed investments described inFebruary 2025.
sources.methodology: Project approval announcement and local drainage diagnosis.
sources.limitations: Expected benefits are plans, not evaluated results.

sources.title: El Niño in the Amazon: Building resilience to crises in Suriname
sources.temporal_coverage: Interior consultations and anticipatory-action planning reported inSeptember 2026.
sources.methodology: WFP field-mission account and community consultation.
sources.limitations: Qualitative operational account; no national causal estimate or evaluated effectiveness.

sources.title: Climate change adaptation investments for the resilience of Paramaribo
sources.temporal_coverage: Project period 2024-2026 shown on publisher page.
sources.methodology: Implementer's project objectives and expected results.
sources.limitations: Expected outcomes and project dates do not establish completion or publication date.

sources.title: The Republic of Suriname’s First National Adaptation Plan Progress Report
sources.organization: Ministry of Spatial Planning and Environment, Republic of Suriname
sources.temporal_coverage: Reviews national adaptation progress for 2020-2024; report published 1 April 2025.
sources.methodology: NAP implementation reviewed against indicators using questionnaires, focus groups, interviews and a validation workshop.
sources.limitations: Some indicator data were unavailable; the report is not an impact evaluation.

sources.title: Suriname Systematic Country Diagnostic
sources.temporal_coverage: Diagnostic drafted mainly in 2023; includes 2022 flood observations and a 2023 household phone survey.
sources.methodology: World Bank diagnostic based on two 2022 country visits, stakeholder interviews, literature review and a household phone survey.
sources.limitations: The report cautions that some conditions may have changed since drafting; flood and land-rights sections synthesize earlier sources.

sources.title: Climate Resilience for Food Security in Suriname
sources.organization: Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture (IICA), Water and Agriculture platform
sources.temporal_coverage: Project listing states implementation from 2023 to 2024 and finalized status.
sources.methodology: IICA implementer account of field assessments, farmer meetings, demonstration plots and project lessons.
sources.limitations: Project-page account is not an independent evaluation and provides no controlled outcome estimate.

sources.title: Building Indigenous Maroon Farmers’ Resilience to Climate Change Guaranteeing Food Security in Suriname
sources.organization: Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture (IICA)
sources.temporal_coverage: Project listing states dates 8 May 2025 to 30 June 2026; current implementation status is not stated.
sources.methodology: IICA project listing summarizing the problem statement, planned training and demonstration-site activities.
sources.limitations: The page states intended activities, not completed outcomes; it does not name participating villages.

sources.title: Eswatini Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate and disaster impacts, climate projections, and planned adaptation targets reported in 2025
sources.methodology: National communication summarizes climate trends, scenarios, sector impacts and adaptation priorities.
sources.limitations: Statistics cite other studies; NDC targets are plans, not evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: Drought Resilience Profiles: Eswatini
sources.organization: World Bank, CIWA, SADRI, IWMI and National Drought Mitigation Center
sources.temporal_coverage: Drought impacts and preparedness information summarized in an undated profile
sources.methodology: Brief profile applies an integrated drought-risk-management framework covering monitoring, vulnerability and impacts, and preparedness and response.
sources.limitations: The profile is a concise overview, carries a disclaimer that it may not represent partner organizations' views, and does not constitute an impact evaluation.

sources.title: The Kingdom of Eswatini's Initial Adaptation Communication to the UNFCCC
sources.organization: Government of Eswatini, Ministry of Tourism and Environmental Affairs
sources.temporal_coverage: Government assessment summarizing historic impacts and a 2021 risk profile, with adaptation actions reported through 2021 and some projections to 2050.
sources.methodology: Government UNFCCC submission synthesizing prior risk studies, a 2021 assessment and adaptation activities.
sources.limitations: Dated national self-report; project outcomes are not independently evaluated.

sources.title: Kingdom of Eswatini: Selected Issues
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate-impact chapter reports disaster and agricultural context through 2024 and provincial agricultural stress since 2020.
sources.methodology: IMF staff country analysis using EM-DAT, FAO data and staff calculations, with cited government and partner evidence.
sources.limitations: Short national analysis synthesizes secondary sources; provincial stress chart is relative and does not estimate household-level losses.

sources.title: Effectiveness of climate change adaptation strategies in strengthening food and water security resilience in Eswatini
sources.organization: Lindiwe Maphalala, Denver Naidoo, Unathi Kolanisi and Lelethu Mdoda; Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
sources.temporal_coverage: Mixed-methods household survey and open-ended responses collected in 2025 in six communities in Lubombo Region; article published 18 August 2026.
sources.methodology: Cross-sectional mixed-methods household survey in six selected Lubombo communities.
sources.limitations: Abstract gives 859 respondents; methods specify an 880 target. Selected cross-sectional sites are not national causal estimates.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief on Eswatini
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: GIEWS reference date 25 August 2026; reports completed 2026 harvest and food-security projections for October 2026 to March 2027.
sources.methodology: FAO GIEWS brief drawing on cereal balances, earth observation, price monitoring and the latest IPC analysis.
sources.limitations: National food-security assessment and outlook without regional or livelihood-zone breakdown.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Seychelles
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate risks, sector analyses and modeled development pathways through 2050; selected sea-level results to 2100.
sources.methodology: World Bank assessment combines climate-risk, sector and economy-wide modelling.
sources.limitations: Scenario and survey-based estimates, not observed outcomes.

sources.title: Seychelles’ Third National Communication under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
sources.organization: Republic of Seychelles, Ministry of Agriculture, Climate Change and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate communication; observed and projected sectoral risks, with precipitation simulations through 2100.
sources.methodology: Government communication compiled with ministries, local bodies and other contributors.
sources.limitations: Prior studies; spatial detail varies.

sources.title: UNDP Supports Stronger Early Warning Systems and Disaster Preparedness in Seychelles
sources.temporal_coverage: TIAEWS project inputs and planned disaster-information and early-warning functions reported in July 2026.
sources.methodology: Official UNDP announcement reports a project handover and stated objectives.
sources.limitations: Press release describes an input and planned functions, not evaluated results.

sources.title: About Us
sources.organization: Department of Risk and Disaster Management, Government of Seychelles
sources.temporal_coverage: Institutional history through the December 2025 transformation of DRMD into DRDM.
sources.methodology: Departmental page summarizes its statutory basis, institutional history and mandate.
sources.limitations: Institutional self-description does not evaluate operational effectiveness.

sources.title: UNDP Seychelles Country Programme Document 2024–2028
sources.temporal_coverage: UNDP country programme theory of change for 2024–2028.
sources.methodology: Official publication page provides the programme’s theory-of-change extract.
sources.limitations: The extract records programme intentions, not implementation or results.

sources.title: *Background analysis of climate risks to Syria's electricity and urban water sectors* (ODI: Think change1)
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical trends to reconstruction scenarios through 2045+
sources.methodology: New climate-trend analysis, population scenarios, water systems and electricity-demand analysis
sources.limitations: Reconstruction-oriented; population scenarios are planning tools rather than forecasts; substantial data gaps acknowledged.

sources.title: *Human-induced climate change compounded by socio-economic water stressors increased severity of drought in Syria, Iraq and Iran* (World Weather Attribution7)
geographic_coverage: Euphrates-Tigris basin including large parts of Syria and Iraq; Iran separately
sources.temporal_coverage: Jul 2020-Jun 2023; counterfactual climate comparison
sources.methodology: 36-month SPEI; observations and climate models using published peer-reviewed attribution methods
sources.limitations: Regional basin result cannot be generalized to every Syrian locality; rapid attribution study, not a conflict-causality study.

sources.title: *FAO GIEWS Country Brief - Syrian Arab Republic* (FAOHome2)
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 harvest; 2025/26 marketing year; 2026 planting
sources.methodology: Crop, rainfall, input, import and food-security monitoring
sources.limitations: Current operational synthesis rather than causal impact evaluation; subnational detail uneven.

sources.title: *UNHCR Syria Operational Update - March 2026* (UNHCR Data Portal3)
sources.temporal_coverage: Through Mar 2026
sources.methodology: Operational displacement, return and assistance data
sources.limitations: Rapidly changing population movements; estimates depend on operational data systems.

sources.title: *Syria at a turning point: A new chapter for children - Annual Report 2025* (UNICEF9)
geographic_coverage: All 14 governorates, with selected subnational examples
sources.methodology: Programme monitoring and sectoral operational statistics
sources.limitations: UNICEF self-report; beneficiary/reach numbers are outputs unless an evaluation establishes outcomes.

sources.title: *The Syrian Conflict: Physical Damage and Reconstruction Assessment (2011-2024)* (World Bank4)
sources.methodology: Predominantly remote data and asset/exposure modelling
sources.limitations: Does not measure full human/economic impacts or service-restoration needs; remote-data uncertainty; sectoral disaggregation limited.

sources.title: *Syria Common Country Analysis: 2024 Update* (UN Syria10)
sources.temporal_coverage: Primarily 2023-2024 with older source material
sources.methodology: Synthesis of UN, government and external evidence
sources.limitations: Some environmental material derives from older sources; broad synthesis claims need source-level checking before causal use.

sources.title: Kelley et al., *Climate change in the Fertile Crescent and implications of the recent Syrian drought* (Columbia OCP5)
sources.temporal_coverage: Pre-2011 drought and longer climatic record
sources.methodology: Observations, CMIP5 simulations and secondary social evidence
sources.limitations: Historical and heavily contested causal interpretation; migration/conflict evidence relies partly on secondary sources.

sources.title: Selby et al., *Climate change and the Syrian civil war revisited* (Cambridge Repository11)
sources.temporal_coverage: Pre-2011 drought and uprising onset
sources.methodology: Systematic interrogation of climate, migration and conflict evidence
sources.limitations: Historical critique rather than evidence about current Climate-FCV mechanisms; cannot prove a zero climate effect.

sources.title: Eklund et al., *Societal drought vulnerability and the Syrian climate-conflict nexus are better explained by agriculture than meteorology* (Nature12)
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly pre-conflict drought/land-use period
sources.methodology: Satellite-derived cropland and climate data
sources.limitations: Cropland is not equivalent to household livelihood, migration or political behaviour; historical focus.

sources.title: *Making Adaptation Work: Addressing the compounding impacts of climate change, environmental degradation and conflict in the Near and Middle East* (ICRC6)
geographic_coverage: Near/Middle East; examples from Syria, Iraq, Yemen
sources.temporal_coverage: Contemporary through 2022/23
sources.methodology: Desk review and country examples
sources.limitations: Many findings are regional rather than Syria-specific; not an impact evaluation.

sources.title: *Syrian Arab Republic Interim Country Strategic Plan Evaluation 2018-25* (World Food Programme13)
sources.temporal_coverage: Performance 2018-Jun 2023
sources.methodology: Theory-based mixed-methods evaluation
sources.limitations: Page publication date conflicts with stated evaluation period; downloaded evaluation PDF was not fetchable in this session; findings on publication page were verified. Not a climate-specific impact evaluation.

sources.title: *JP Syria 2.0 Annual Programme Narrative Progress Report 2025* (MPTF Gateway14)
sources.organization: UN Joint Programme: FAO, UNDP, UNFPA, UN-Habitat, UNICEF, WFP
sources.methodology: Implementing-agency monitoring, lessons and reported outputs
sources.limitations: Self-reported programme evidence, geographically narrow; lessons should not be treated as independently demonstrated outcomes.

sources.title: *Increasing the climate change resilience of communities in Eastern Ghouta...* (Adaptation Fund15)
sources.temporal_coverage: 2021-2025 implementation period
sources.methodology: Project design, administrative and performance documentation
sources.limitations: Project objectives and budgets are intended mechanisms, not proof of resilience outcomes; local evidence only.

sources.title: *Approval of request for no-cost extension of project completion date: UN-Habitat (Syria)* (Adaptation Fund16)
sources.methodology: Secretariat review of documented implementation delays
sources.limitations: Establishes implementation delay and reported causes, not the magnitude of resulting resilience loss.

sources.title: *Syria - Country Overview* (World Bank17)
sources.temporal_coverage: Through 2026
sources.methodology: World Bank synthesis and high-frequency indicators
sources.limitations: Page explicitly notes limited and unevenly reliable official data; current estimates remain uncertain.

sources.title: Historical assessment of agricultural drought impact in the Syrian Arab Republic (2021–2025)
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO portal summary of a technical assessment of drought conditions and affected agricultural areas during 2021–2025, published 1 September 2026.
sources.methodology: FAO describes satellite remote sensing and geospatial analysis of drought frequency, severity, duration and affected agricultural areas.
sources.limitations: Accessible portal summary gives national estimates but no named governorate-level hotspots or underlying detailed tables.

sources.title: Syrian Arab Republic Appeal: Humanitarian Action for Children 2026
sources.temporal_coverage: UNICEF's August 2026 revised annual appeal reports needs and displacement through 2026 and planned response targets.
sources.methodology: UNICEF operational appeal summarizing humanitarian needs, response priorities and planned agency targets.
sources.limitations: Operational needs and targets are not independent causal estimates or an evaluation of response outcomes.

sources.title: FAO scales up irrigation rehabilitation to strengthen agricultural recovery and climate resilience in Aleppo
