sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO report dated 29 April 2025 on rehabilitation works at the West Maskanah Farm No. 9 irrigation scheme.
sources.methodology: FAO project report describing the rehabilitation scope and intended beneficiaries, drawing on assessments and community discussions.
sources.limitations: The page reports works and intended access, not independently measured household reach or resilience outcomes.

sources.title: FAO launches its emergency and recovery plan of action to restore agriculture in Syria
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO's 19 March 2025 launch description of the proposed Emergency and Recovery Plan of Action for 2025–2027.
sources.methodology: FAO announcement summarizes its planned emergency, recovery, resilience and early-recovery package.
sources.limitations: This is a plan-launch page; proposed reach, activities and peace effects are intentions, not verified delivery or evaluated results.

sources.title: Syria Context Report
sources.temporal_coverage: FEWS NET context assessment dated 31 December 2025, including the post-December 2024 transition and conditions reported through 2025.
sources.methodology: Country context synthesis of conflict, livelihood, market, food-security and agroclimatic evidence with cited partner sources.
sources.limitations: The report synthesizes heterogeneous sources and identifies data gaps; its multi-driver framing does not quantify each driver's separate contribution.

sources.title: Analysis of the Frequency and Impacts of Flooding in Chad
sources.organization: World Bank Sahel Adaptive Social Protection Program Technical Paper Series; Pierre E. Biscaye (external contributor)
sources.temporal_coverage: Flood incidence analysis over approximately 2012–2024 and modeled present-day exposure under 2020 conditions
sources.methodology: External technical study compares flood-hazard models, survey reports and satellite-detected floods, then maps population exposure using administrative and population datasets.
sources.limitations: Modeled exposure is not observed damage; estimates vary by flood model and population data. Some satellite years are missing and built-up areas can be harder to detect.

sources.title: Chad Economic Update: Improving Resilience to Floods
sources.temporal_coverage: Disaster-risk context and observed events through 2022, with climate-impact projections to 2050 and end-century
sources.methodology: Economic update combining flood-risk context, service data and climate-impact modeling summarized from the Sahel CCDR.
sources.limitations: Physical PDF page 4 permits noncommercial reproduction with attribution; no unrestricted open licence is asserted. Report-level mechanisms are not measured local causal effects.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief on Chad
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: GIEWS reference date 7 September 2026; reports crop conditions through mid-August 2026 and outcomes for the 2025 cereal season.
sources.methodology: FAO GIEWS combines cereal-balance, price, Cadre Harmonisé and satellite crop-monitoring information.
sources.limitations: This dated brief is a snapshot; its 2026 seasonal outlook is not a verified final harvest result.

sources.title: When the Waters Rise: How the City of N’Djamena, Chad, Prepared for Floods and Averted Disaster
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank results brief on the N’Djamena Urban Resilience Project's 2024 flood-preparedness activities and reported results, published 26 May 2026.
sources.methodology: World Bank results brief describes PILIER activities and reported 2024 results.
sources.limitations: Project results are self-reported; the page provides no counterfactual or independent evaluation of flood losses avoided.

sources.title: Chad Humanitarian Situation Report No. 2 (End of Year), 31 December 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: UNICEF report published 9 February 2026, covering 1 January to 31 December 2025 and summarizing humanitarian needs and response.
sources.methodology: UNICEF operational annual report.
sources.limitations: Some OCHA data are relayed; flood data lack household detail.

sources.title: Chad Situation Report #1 – July 2024
sources.temporal_coverage: UNFPA report on the July 2024 humanitarian situation, published August 2024.
sources.methodology: UNFPA operational situation report summarizing reported flood impacts, displacement and service delivery.
sources.limitations: The brief gives no named flood-affected provinces or detailed breakdown of affected women and girls.

sources.title: Première Communication relative à l'Adaptation aux Changements Climatiques au Togo
sources.organization: Ministère de l'Environnement et des Ressources Forestières, République Togolaise
sources.temporal_coverage: Synthesis of 2017-2023 vulnerability studies; projections to 2050 and 2100
sources.methodology: Government communication synthesizes assessments, document review, stakeholder consultations and field visits.
sources.limitations: Regional indices summarize cited sector studies rather than one unified underlying dataset.

sources.title: Contributions Déterminées au Niveau National Révisées du Togo: Document Intérimaire
sources.organization: Ministère de l'Environnement et des Ressources Forestières, République Togolaise
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical sector impacts and climate observations; basin and sector projections to 2030 and 2050
sources.methodology: Interim revised NDC compiles climate projections, sector vulnerability assessments and reported impacts.
sources.limitations: Sector figures cite distinct studies and periods; climate-conflict links are not causal event analyses.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief on Togo
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: GIEWS reference date 28 August 2026; reports 2026 crop conditions, June 2026 flooding and the 2026 lean season.
sources.methodology: FAO GIEWS integrates crop monitoring, food-security classification and market information.
sources.limitations: Snapshot; seasonal outlook is not a final 2026 harvest result.

sources.title: Response in Coastal Countries Linked to Sahel Crisis Spillover: Humanitarian Situation Report No. 2, End of Year 2024
sources.temporal_coverage: UNICEF regional report covering 1 January to 31 December 2024; published 14 April 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF regional annual situation report with country-level humanitarian needs and programme reporting.
sources.limitations: The Togo chapter is operational and its displacement and access figures describe 2024, not current prevalence.

sources.title: Togo Hydromet and Early Warning Services
sources.temporal_coverage: WMO project portfolio page lists the project as completed; the accessible page does not state dates.
sources.methodology: WMO project portfolio page lists objectives, partners and output areas.
sources.limitations: The page lists outputs but does not report which were delivered or measure resulting forecast or warning performance.

sources.title: Analyse du paysage climatique pour les enfants au Togo: Placer les droits des enfants au cœur de l’action climatique
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment and Forest Resources of Togo, with support from the United Nations Children’s Fund
sources.temporal_coverage: Publisher webpage summary for the French-language Ministry–UNICEF climate landscape for children, published November 2025.
sources.methodology: Accessible publisher summary identifies the report authors and summarizes child-focused climate risks and policy findings.
sources.limitations: The underlying 19 MB French report was not readable; the page summary gives national themes without local estimates or detailed methods.

sources.title: Thailand's National Adaptation Plan (NAP)
sources.organization: Office of Natural Resources and Environmental Policy and Planning, Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment, Thailand
sources.temporal_coverage: National adaptation plan; provincial climate-risk rankings modelled for 2016–2035 under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5.
sources.methodology: National plan reproduces ONEP consultant models and sectoral risk assessments for climate adaptation planning.
sources.limitations: Provincial top-ten lists are model outputs attributed to ONEP 2021, not measured current impacts; the settlements-and-security sector label is not a conflict indicator.

sources.title: Thailand Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Published 2025; includes historical/current diagnostics, projections and a Khon Kaen provincial water-management case.
sources.methodology: World Bank country assessment with biophysical modeling and policy analysis; Industrial Economics supported physical-risk modeling.
sources.limitations: Model scenarios and dates are stated claim-by-claim; the Khon Kaen institutional case describes planning processes, not evaluated climate-resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Climate Change Adaptation Implementation and Governance in Thailand: Increased Resilience and Potential Conflicts
sources.organization: Springer Nature, in Risks, Resilience and Interdependency
sources.temporal_coverage: Open-access chapter published 2025; reviews climate-adaptation governance and source-reported conflict examples, including a 2004 drought case.
sources.methodology: Qualitative text analysis of policies, government data, public records and climate/conflict literature.
sources.limitations: Document review, not primary causal research; authors say Thailand linkages remain understudied.

sources.title: Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Analysis (Thailand, 2025)
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 gender and social inclusion study prepared for the CINTALAM youth-led climate-action project.
sources.methodology: Publisher abstract describes the study as mixed-methods; extracted findings are limited to that official abstract.
sources.limitations: Full report PDF was not retrievable; sample, detailed methods and locality-level results were not inspected, and the abstract does not establish causal effects.

sources.title: Women leading peace and climate resilience in southern Thailand
sources.organization: United Nations in Thailand / UN Women
sources.temporal_coverage: UN story published 2 April 2026; includes participant accounts and captions on the Yupo flood of 25 November 2025.
sources.methodology: Qualitative UN country feature profiles women and community organizations, with named-site observations, participant accounts and captions.
sources.limitations: A feature story, not representative monitoring or climate-attribution research; local event estimates and reported experiences are not population-level measures.

sources.title: Updated Nationally Determined Contribution of the Republic of Tajikistan
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Tajikistan; UNFCCC repository
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC planning through 2030; cited climate forecasts extend to 2050.
sources.methodology: Government NDC compiles national strategies, sector programs, and stakeholder consultations.
sources.limitations: Government estimates; NDC notes monitoring gaps.

sources.title: Green Transition is Key to Tajikistan’s Economic Revival and Climate Resilience
sources.temporal_coverage: CCDR summary includes projections and investment needs through 2050.
sources.methodology: World Bank Group press-release summary of the Tajikistan Country Climate and Development Report.
sources.limitations: Only the publisher’s release text was inspected; figures and recommendations are not independently re-estimated here.

sources.title: Environment Program in Central Asia
sources.temporal_coverage: RESILAND Tajikistan project status summarized in a 2025 World Bank brief; project launched in November 2022.
sources.methodology: World Bank program brief summarizing country project scope and reported implementation status.
sources.limitations: Publisher summary, not an independent project evaluation; reported outputs are not attributed to climate outcomes.

sources.title: CCRI-DRM Sub-national Tajikistan
sources.temporal_coverage: Subnational child climate and disaster risk model published July 2026; indicator vintages are not stated in the narrative PDF.
sources.methodology: UNICEF's model combines 57 indicators across hazard exposure and child vulnerability for 62 districts.
sources.limitations: Index scores compare districts within Tajikistan; the narrative does not give indicator vintages or detailed component methods.

sources.title: Climate change as a trigger of border river conflicts in Central Asia
sources.temporal_coverage: Article summarizes regional field research conducted in 2021 and a reported April 2021 border confrontation.
sources.methodology: Article summarizes field research in Sughd and regional climate-conflict dialogue.
sources.limitations: Multi-country qualitative summary; no measured climate attribution or causal estimate.

sources.title: The Nexus between Climate Change, Labour Migration, and Radicalisation among Tajik Labour Migrants
sources.organization: Royal United Services Institute and Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung Multinational Development Policy Dialogue
sources.temporal_coverage: RUSI project interviews were conducted March-May 2025; report published 28 November 2025.
sources.methodology: Qualitative scoping study with 80 interviews in Tajikistan, Turkey and remotely.
sources.limitations: Targeted sample, no survey; climate-migration attribution is uncertain and interviewees rarely cited climate directly.

sources.title: Building Resilience Across Tajikistan for a More Inclusive Economy
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank results summary reports projects and results mainly for 2014-2023, with some operations continuing through 2027.
sources.methodology: Publisher results page summarizes several World Bank-supported programs and reported implementation outputs.
sources.limitations: Results are publisher-reported program outputs; this page does not provide an independent evaluation or isolate climate effects.

sources.title: Risks from Climate Change for Water & Agriculture in Turkmenistan: Assessment Report on Climate Risk, Vulnerability, Gender and Vulnerable Groups
sources.organization: HYDROPHIL / UNDP, for Ministry of Environmental Protection
sources.temporal_coverage: Assessment November 2023–June 2024; climate comparisons 1991–2010 to 2041–2060; longer projections to 2099.
sources.methodology: Stakeholder-informed impact chains and 29-model climate ensemble.
sources.limitations: Selective assessment; conditional risks, not causal conflict estimates.

sources.title: Independent Country Programme Evaluation: Turkmenistan
sources.temporal_coverage: Evaluation conducted 2024, covers 2021–2024; published June 2025.
sources.methodology: Document review, 116 informants and site observation; evaluation of 2021–2024 programming.
sources.limitations: Contribution assessment, not experimental impact attribution; some beneficiaries were difficult to reach.

sources.title: Local communities from Dashoguz and Akhal velayats discuss efficient water management practices as adaptation to climate change
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration / UN Turkmenistan
sources.temporal_coverage: Seminars in late April and mid-May 2025; publication 20 May 2025.
sources.methodology: Official account of two-day local training seminars.
sources.limitations: Reported activities and participant feedback, not evaluated resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Protecting Turkmenistan's economic and social future from Climate Change: Insights from the Water-Agriculture Nexus in Dashoguz Province and Ashgabat City
sources.organization: Robert Bierkandt and Sven Willner / UNDP
sources.temporal_coverage: June 2024 synthesis of risks and proposed adaptations.
sources.methodology: Policy synthesis of the 2024 water-agriculture risk assessment.
sources.limitations: Derived from source 101; not independent replication or an implementation evaluation.

sources.title: Drought and Fire Risk in Timor-Leste: What El Niño Means for Our Communities
sources.temporal_coverage: 2023–2024 drought and July 2026 risk communication
sources.methodology: UNDP synthesis of cited assessments and hazard mapping.
sources.limitations: Secondary synthesis within an official feature; historic losses are not a measured 2026 national harvest.

sources.title: Timor-Leste Launches ASIS Portal and National Drought Monitoring Tool
sources.temporal_coverage: May 2026 launch
sources.methodology: Programme launch and technical-training account.
sources.limitations: Design commitments and intended benefits are not verified outcomes.

sources.title: Safeguarding rural communities and their physical assets from climate-induced disasters in Timor-Leste
sources.temporal_coverage: Undated implementation update
sources.methodology: Project description with reported outputs.
sources.limitations: Undated implementer reporting; intended final coverage and reported achievements differ.

sources.title: Human Security of Border Communities in Covalima, Bobonaro and RAEOA, Timor-Leste: Mapping and Assessment Report
sources.organization: Institute for Peace, Conflict and Social Studies, Universidade Nacional Timor Lorosa’e; commissioned by UNICEF and IOM
sources.temporal_coverage: Participatory assessment fieldwork in 2023; includes historical examples, including a 2021 displacement event.
sources.methodology: Qualitative mapping through 2023 focus groups, interviews and workshops in 23 border villages.
sources.limitations: Sampled participant accounts, not prevalence or climate-attribution analysis.

sources.title: Climate Rationale for Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Services in Timor-Leste
sources.organization: IVL Swedish Environmental Research Institute and UNICEF Timor-Leste
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate and WASH policy/risk review published August 2025; projections vary by stated scenario and horizon.
sources.methodology: Climate and WASH policy/literature review with expert task-force validation and a June 2025 workshop.
sources.limitations: Mixed data vintages; the cited water-dispute evidence is from 2017, not a current conflict assessment.

sources.title: UNICEF Timor-Leste Annual Report 2024: Action and Impact for Every Child
sources.temporal_coverage: Reported 2024 programme activities and outputs.
sources.methodology: UNICEF annual programme reporting of activities and outputs.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported outputs; expected water benefits are not measured impacts.

sources.title: Mercy Corps, EU, and KOICA hand over Early Warning System devices to DNMG
sources.temporal_coverage: Early-warning handover and project descriptions reported in March 2024.
sources.methodology: Local news report on project handover and statements by implementing partners.
sources.limitations: Descriptive reporting; the article gives inconsistent counts for supported PREPARADU sucos.

sources.title: European Union and Mercy Corps celebrate successful conclusion of Maloa Urban Resilience Initiative Program
sources.temporal_coverage: Implementer-reported programme outputs at June 2024 close-out.
sources.methodology: EU and Mercy Corps close-out account of programme outputs.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported capacity and works; no independent impact evaluation.

sources.title: New World Bank Support to Help Build a More Resilient, Sustainable Future for Tonga
sources.temporal_coverage: May 2025 reforms
sources.methodology: Policy-operation announcement.
sources.limitations: Design commitments and intended benefits are not verified outcomes.

sources.title: World Bank and Asian Development Bank Partner with Tonga to Strengthen Jobs, Connectivity, and Resilience
sources.temporal_coverage: May 2026 approval
sources.methodology: Transport and urban project design.
sources.limitations: Design commitments and intended benefits are not verified outcomes.

sources.title: World Bank Boosts Support for Tonga to Build Resilience, Strengthen Disaster Preparedness
sources.temporal_coverage: January 2024 financing and policy announcement
sources.methodology: Publisher metadata date; body dateline is 21 January.
sources.limitations: Design commitments and intended benefits are not verified outcomes.

sources.title: Tonga Second Nationally Determined Contributions Review Report
sources.organization: Government of Tonga, Department of Climate Change (MEIDECC)
sources.temporal_coverage: Government review of NDC 2.0 implementation; includes 2020-2023 measures and earlier studies with projections to about 2090 and 2100.
sources.methodology: Government review of NDC implementation and sector evidence; estimates also cite earlier studies.
sources.limitations: Evidence vintages vary; projections cite earlier studies, and mangrove effectiveness is unquantified.

sources.title: Kingdom of Tonga Technology Needs Assessment Adaptation Report
sources.organization: Department of Energy, Government of Tonga; GEF-funded UNEP Technology Needs Assessment with UNEP-CCC and University of the South Pacific support
sources.temporal_coverage: Adaptation technology-needs assessment prepared in December 2023; includes water-risk data and citations from 2019-2021.
sources.methodology: Government-led review and stakeholder prioritization for agriculture and water technologies.
sources.limitations: Risk estimates cite older studies; priorities and proposed support are not evaluated results.

sources.title: Innovative Approaches to Water Resilience in Tonga
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports on water-sector workshops in November 2023 and a stakeholder roundtable on 10 May 2024.
sources.methodology: UNDRR account of stakeholder consultation on water infrastructure resilience.
sources.limitations: Consultation recommendations are not completed works or measured local resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Climate Resilient Islands
sources.temporal_coverage: The project page describes a six-year 2021-2026 programme.
sources.methodology: Implementer webpage summarizing programme design, locations and planned activities.
sources.limitations: The page does not report completion or evaluated outcomes; participant and household figures are programme targets.

sources.title: Two Years on, the Tonga Tsunami Shows Effective Risk Communication Saves Lives
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction
sources.temporal_coverage: Retrospective account of preparedness and response to the 15 January 2022 volcanic eruption and tsunami; follow-up reported in January 2024.
sources.methodology: UNDRR retrospective using community and government accounts of warning and evacuation.
sources.limitations: The event was volcanic and tsunami-related, not a climate-attributed hazard; the article is not an impact evaluation.

sources.title: National Adaptation Plan for the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago, Ministry of Planning and Development
sources.temporal_coverage: Government's first NAP, November 2023; sector risk assessments include next-ten-year likelihood judgments.
sources.methodology: Government-led, multi-year plan with stakeholder input and sector technical-working-group risk assessments.
sources.limitations: Local risk levels are plan-era assessments, not measured outcomes; scenario detail varies by table.

sources.title: Forecasting Trinidad's Evolving Flood Future: A Susceptibility Mapping Approach with Long-Term Rainfall Projections (2010-2100)
sources.organization: ISPRS Annals of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
sources.temporal_coverage: Peer-reviewed 2026 study combines historical rainfall and projected rainfall layers to map Trinidad flood susceptibility at five-year intervals through 2100.
sources.methodology: GIS weighted-overlay susceptibility model combines rainfall, elevation, slope, road and drainage density, and locally derived land cover.
sources.limitations: Model uses 2007 land cover and equal factor weights, downscales coarse rainfall data, and lacks independent validation; susceptibility is not event probability.

sources.title: Commonwealth Caribbean Cities, Climate Change Adaptation and Resilience: Empowering Local Government
sources.organization: Commonwealth Journal of Local Governance, University of Technology Sydney
sources.temporal_coverage: Peer-reviewed article published October 2024; Trinidad case evidence includes 2023 interviews and earlier planning documents.
sources.methodology: Comparative case study uses a 2022 workshop, 2023 interviews, legislation, policy documents and literature.
sources.limitations: Trinidad findings include two participant perspectives, not a representative survey; some context is attributed to earlier literature.

sources.title: Written submission by the Ministry of Rural Development and Local Government to the Joint Select Committee on Land and Physical Infrastructure: Climate Change Inquiry
sources.organization: Ministry of Rural Development and Local Government, Trinidad and Tobago
sources.temporal_coverage: Ministry response submitted March 2023; training counts and implementation descriptions are dated to 2021-2023.
sources.methodology: Ministry's parliamentary written response on climate impacts, municipal disaster management and adaptation.
sources.limitations: Government self-report, not an independent evaluation; stated programme status is dated and was not reverified for 2026.

sources.title: Multi-sectoral Adaptation Measures to Flood Relief in the South Oropouche River Basin Project
sources.organization: Environmental Policy and Planning Division, Government of Trinidad and Tobago
sources.temporal_coverage: Government page describes the project's September 2023 launch, design targets and four-year implementation period.
sources.methodology: Government page reports project launch, targets and partner statements.
sources.limitations: Launch-stage aims and targets are not audited outcomes or final results.

sources.title: Tunisie - Évaluation de la vulnérabilité climatique et sanitaire (Encadré Politique)
geographic_coverage: Tunisia; named governorates include Béja, Ben Arous, Bizerte, Jendouba, Manouba, Tunis, Ariana, Sfax and Nabeul
sources.temporal_coverage: Health and climate baselines; projections through 2100; adaptation recommendations over 1-5 years
sources.methodology: Five-page summary of the 92-page CHVA; flood chart cites FATHOM v3 and Ministry facility data.
sources.limitations: Not full CHVA; scenario and model detail is incomplete.

sources.title: Review of Employment-Intensive Investment Programme (EIIP) water projects in Tunisia
geographic_coverage: Kesra, Oued El Barka, Zaouiet Ben Ammar and Sned Jebel project sites in Siliana, Jendouba, Kasserine and Gafsa governorates
sources.temporal_coverage: 2023 review of EIIP water projects implemented during 2012-2017 and 2018-2025
sources.methodology: Six-page ILO summary of a 2023 review of EIIP project cycles (2012-2017, 2018-2025).
sources.limitations: Project findings, not nationally representative or climate attribution.

sources.title: Country programme document for Tunisia (2021-2025)
geographic_coverage: Tunisia, including coastal zone, rural areas and national regional disparities
sources.temporal_coverage: 2021-2025 country programme; water statistics and coastal indicators mostly dated 2015-2019
sources.methodology: UNDP Executive Board programme document summarizing national climate, water, regional-disparity and institutional indicators and programme priorities.
sources.limitations: Most cited baselines are dated; proposed programme actions are not evidence of delivery or impact.

sources.title: Tunisia
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
geographic_coverage: Tunisia; named localities include Kairouan, Sfax, Sidi Bouzid, Kébili, Tataouine and Kasserine
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical droughts and indicator vintages ranging from 2013 to 2023
sources.methodology: FAO Drought Portal country page organizes social, economic, infrastructure, environmental and institutional drought indicators and consulted sources.
sources.limitations: Indicators have different reference years; page does not provide one integrated local assessment method.

sources.title: Le changement climatique en Tunisie
sources.organization: Institut National de la Météorologie, Ministère du Transport
geographic_coverage: Northern, central and southern Tunisia; named example Nabeul
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed trends 1978-2012; multi-model projections for 2050 and 2100 under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5
sources.methodology: National Meteorological Institute portal summarizes observed national trends and multi-model projections under two RCP pathways.
sources.limitations: Page omits constituent models and downscaling details; its observed trend period ends in 2012.

sources.title: World Bank: Stronger Water Management Could Unlock Growth, Protect Jobs, and Build Resilience in Tunisia
geographic_coverage: Tunisia; national freshwater availability, rural employment and water-sector management
sources.temporal_coverage: Water availability and employment baseline in 2026; economic projections through 2050; Plan Eau 2050
sources.methodology: World Bank press release summarizes the 2026 Tunisia Economic Monitor and its water-scarcity analysis.
sources.limitations: Press release omits the Monitor's detailed modeling, assumptions and subnational breakdown.

sources.title: Climate Change Adaptation Strategy and Action Plan (2024–2030)
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change / Presidency of Climate Change
geographic_coverage: Türkiye; urban assessments name cities in the Mediterranean, Black Sea, Central Anatolia and Southeastern Anatolia; water assessment covers provinces
sources.temporal_coverage: Strategy 2024–2030; assessment method covers 81 provinces, a 1990–2019 current period and 2021–2100 projections under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5.
sources.methodology: Provincial and urban vulnerability/risk assessments; national method uses current and future climate periods.
sources.limitations: The cited local results do not identify a scenario or assessment period; urban infrastructure data are incomplete and city-wide conclusions may mislead.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Türkiye
geographic_coverage: Türkiye; Şanlıurfa, Mardin, Antalya, Adana, Hatay and Istanbul subregion
sources.temporal_coverage: Published June 2022; cited wildfire land-burned averages cover 2011–2021; flood poverty estimates use a 200-year return-period case.
sources.methodology: CCDR analytical estimates draw on referenced household, disaster-risk and poverty analyses.
sources.limitations: Publication is dated June 2022 and underlying data vintages vary; the 200-year flood is a modeled case, not a dated event.

sources.title: Decent and Sustainable Job Opportunities for Refugees and Host Communities in Turkish Textile Sector
geographic_coverage: Türkiye; Istanbul and major southeastern cities discussed; field-work locations listed include Gaziantep, Hatay, Mersin, Adana, Kilis, Şanlıurfa, Mardin, İzmir and İstanbul
sources.temporal_coverage: Project dates are November 2022–January 2025; the page does not date its refugee-population counts.
sources.methodology: UNDP page on a Türkiye refugee-host textile employment project.
sources.limitations: Population counts are undated; the project completed in January 2025 without an outcome evaluation.

sources.title: World Bank Approves $600 million for Türkiye to Build Resilience Against Floods and Drought
geographic_coverage: Türkiye; North Aegean, East Black Sea, Kızılırmak, Büyük Menderes, West Mediterranean, East Mediterranean, West Black Sea and Ceyhan basins
sources.temporal_coverage: June 2024 approval announcement and planned project components; it does not report implementation results.
sources.methodology: World Bank approval announcement summarizing project components, target basins and intended reach.
sources.limitations: Beneficiary figures and activities are targets at approval, not completed results; the release gives no local implementation schedule.

sources.title: World Bank and Government of Türkiye Kickoff a $400 Million Project to Make the Country’s Forests More Resilient
geographic_coverage: Türkiye; 2021 wildfires in southern and western regions; project focus is 14 unnamed highest-risk provinces
sources.temporal_coverage: 2021 wildfire impacts and May 2024 project launch.
sources.methodology: World Bank announcement summarizing 2021 wildfire impacts and the planned forest-resilience project.
sources.limitations: The release gives broad regions, not the 14 province names, and does not attribute the specific 2021 fires to climate change.

sources.title: The Closing Event of the ‘Enhancing Adaptation Action in Türkiye’ Project was held on 3 October 2025
sources.organization: EU IPA Environment and Climate Programme; implemented with Türkiye’s Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change and UNDP Türkiye
geographic_coverage: Türkiye; pilot provinces Samsun, Sakarya, Muğla and Konya; awareness activities in 20 cities, not named
sources.temporal_coverage: Project implementation October 2019–October 2025; local plans cover 2025–2030.
sources.methodology: Project close-out page reports outputs from a six-year EU-funded ministry/UNDP adaptation project.
sources.limitations: The site states content is the sole responsibility of Frankfurt School and may not reflect government or EU positions; reported outputs are not independent impact evaluations.

sources.title: How Tuvalu has challenged climate threats: TCAP in the media
sources.temporal_coverage: TCAP Phase I through December 2025
sources.methodology: Implementer's retrospective and media synthesis.
sources.limitations: Reported outputs, not independent evidence of permanent flood protection.

sources.title: GEF approvals advance major climate adaptation investments across the Pacific
sources.temporal_coverage: June 2026 preparatory approvals
sources.methodology: Project-preparation announcement.
sources.limitations: Preparation grants and concept approval are not final implementation approval.

sources.title: Tuvalu National Adaptation Plan 2025
sources.organization: Government of Tuvalu, Climate Change Department, Ministry of Home Affairs, Climate Change and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 national adaptation plan; includes current social-risk assessment and island-specific coastal projections to 2060 and 2100.
sources.methodology: Government plan informed by consultations across six priority sectors and Funafuti and outer islands.
sources.limitations: Social-risk discussion cites Deloitte CIVRA (2024); projections summarize cited modeling rather than new measurements.

sources.title: Tuvalu Climate Security Risk Assessment Profile
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, in collaboration with the Government of Tuvalu under the UNDP-IOM Climate Security in the Pacific project
sources.temporal_coverage: Preliminary 2022 climate-security profile; pathways described as provisional and still being finalized.
sources.methodology: UNDP-IOM preliminary high-level climate-security assessment prepared with government collaboration.
sources.limitations: UNDP labels the profile preliminary; its pathways are provisional, not a final assessment or quantified incidence study.

sources.title: Pacific
sources.temporal_coverage: UNCDF programme page reporting three community-grant cycles and local-official training in 2024-2025; page publication date not stated.
sources.methodology: Implementer webpage summarizing community-grant outputs and training reach.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported outputs; page provides no independent evaluation of sustained resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Treaty text Falepili Union
sources.organization: Governments of Tuvalu and Australia; Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
sources.temporal_coverage: Treaty signed 9 November 2023; entered into force 28 August 2024, as confirmed by DFAT's treaty overview.
sources.methodology: Bilateral treaty obligations, articles 2 and 3.
sources.limitations: Legal arrangements, not evaluated adaptation outcomes; no universal recognition claim.

sources.title: Australia-Tuvalu Falepili Union treaty
sources.organization: Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
sources.temporal_coverage: Treaty chronology and mobility pathway as accessed on 27 October 2026.
sources.methodology: Official treaty and mobility overview.
sources.limitations: Administrative overview, not an impact evaluation.

sources.title: United Republic of Tanzania Country Climate and Development Report: Executive Summary
sources.temporal_coverage: Current climate-risk exposure and climate-development scenarios through 2050, reported in 2024
sources.methodology: CCDR executive summary reports macroeconomic, climate, sectoral, institutional and financial modeling under climate and growth scenarios.
sources.limitations: Summary-level results are modeled and scenario-dependent; detailed methods are outside this executive summary.

sources.title: Tanzania's Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.organization: United Republic of Tanzania, Vice President's Office (Union and Environment)
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate through 2016 and projections through 2090 reported in the 2021 NDC
sources.methodology: NDC draws on the Second National Communication, national adaptation planning and cited Future Climate for Africa projections.
sources.limitations: NDC reports results from earlier studies; its climate-risk assessment methods were still to be developed when submitted.

sources.title: Performance Audit Report on the Management of Floods
sources.organization: National Audit Office of Tanzania, Controller and Auditor General
sources.temporal_coverage: Flood-management audit covering 2020/21-2023/24; includes field observations and cited event reports from 2023-2024.
sources.methodology: Government performance audit combining interviews, records review and physical site observations in selected flood-prone local authorities.
sources.limitations: Visited local authorities were selected for flood exposure; results are not a representative survey of all councils.

sources.title: Water Sector Development Programme Phase III: Annual Water Sector Status Report 2024
sources.organization: United Republic of Tanzania, Ministry of Water
sources.temporal_coverage: Water-resource, rainfall and service delivery reporting for 2024, published March 2025.
sources.methodology: Annual ministry reporting on hydrology, water services, programme performance and implementation constraints.
sources.limitations: Annual basin and station summaries do not establish anthropogenic climate attribution or household-level impacts.

sources.title: Perceived existence of farmer-pastoralist conflicts in relation to climate change in Kilosa District, Tanzania
sources.organization: Emmanuel E. Chingonikaya and Farida Salehe; published by AkiNik Publications and hosted in the Sokoine University of Agriculture Institutional Repository
sources.temporal_coverage: 2021 cross-sectional study of farmer-pastoralist relations in selected Kilosa wards and villages.
sources.methodology: Repository abstract reports a cross-sectional design with 120 respondents, household surveys, focus groups and key-informant interviews.
sources.limitations: Only the repository abstract was readable; no causal identification, conflict prevalence or ward-level results were available.

sources.title: Local governance and climate change adaptation: evidence from Monduli and Longido districts, Tanzania
sources.organization: Maeda, Namwata and Kumburu; Moshi Co-operative University Institutional Repository
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 mixed-methods study of local-authority adaptation implementation; study fieldwork dates not stated in the abstract.
sources.methodology: Repository abstract reports a 351-member committee survey, 20 key-informant interviews and six focus groups.
sources.limitations: The full article PDF timed out; the abstract supplies no district-specific estimates or detailed measurement definitions.

sources.title: Climate adaptation in Tanzania's national budgeting process: embedding flood and drought preparedness
sources.organization: London School of Economics Grantham Research Institute and Behavioural Adaptation for Water Security and Inclusion project partners
sources.temporal_coverage: Eight-page August 2026 policy brief using 2025 interviews and national budget-cycle analysis.
sources.methodology: Multi-actor behaviour-journey analysis drawing on 43 purposively selected 2025 government and non-government interviews.
sources.limitations: National budgeting analysis, not a district impact evaluation; some budget shares are attributed to cited external reports.

sources.title: Enhancing the Adaptive Capacity of Semi-Arid Agropastoral Communities through Local Adaptation Plans in Dodoma
sources.organization: IKI Small Grants programme; implemented by the Forum on Climate Change (FORUMCC)
sources.temporal_coverage: Completed project page for July 2023-August 2025; reports district planning and engagement outputs.
sources.methodology: Grant-programme page summarizes project context, implementation locations and implementer-reported outputs.
sources.limitations: Project-reported outputs and engagement; approved funding is not evidence of expenditure or independently evaluated impact.

sources.title: Uganda Country Climate and Development Report: Executive Summary
sources.temporal_coverage: Recent weather-shock exposure and climate-development projections through 2050 reported in 2025
sources.methodology: CCDR executive summary reports six climate scenarios, two economic futures and modeled impacts with and without additional climate action.
sources.limitations: Summary-level modeled results; migration estimate is not tied to a specific scenario in the inspected passage.

sources.title: Updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)
sources.organization: Republic of Uganda, Ministry of Water and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC actions for 2020-2030, with climate projections summarized through 2050
sources.methodology: NDC update uses national risk and vulnerability assessments, the Third National Communication and climate/emissions projections.
sources.limitations: Assessment ratings and national projections are summarized; rainfall projections carry wide uncertainty.

sources.title: WASH National Adaptation Plan for Uganda (2026-2030)
sources.organization: Republic of Uganda, Ministry of Water and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: WASH sector adaptation plan for 2026-2030; vulnerability analysis combines hazard and service indicators from cited datasets of varying dates.
sources.methodology: Plan combines a WASH vulnerability assessment, hazard mapping and district service indicators.
sources.limitations: Inputs include OPM's 2019 atlas; the plan is not an impact evaluation.

sources.title: Conducting and Developing the Climate Change and Vulnerability Assessment (CCVA) Framework Report for Kampala Capital City Authority
sources.organization: Republic of Uganda, Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA)
sources.temporal_coverage: Kampala assessment published June 2025; combines historical climate data, projections, GIS and stakeholder evidence across five divisions.
sources.methodology: GIS and climate/social datasets, 400 household surveys, 20 focus groups and 30 interviews used purposive stratified sampling.
sources.limitations: Vulnerable-area sampling is not population-representative; some local narratives cite older studies.

sources.title: Pastoral conflict on the greener grass? Exploring the climate-conflict nexus in the Karamoja Cluster
sources.organization: Rebecca Navarro, Lamis Saleh and Evelyne Owino; International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction; abstract hosted by PreventionWeb
geographic_coverage: Karamoja Cluster, cross-border; country-level findings not disaggregated
sources.temporal_coverage: Abstract describes conflict dynamics in 2018-2023 and an empirical environmental-variable analysis.
sources.methodology: Abstract describes informant interviews and empirical linkage/prediction analysis using environmental variables and conflict data.
sources.limitations: Only the abstract was readable; the journal full text was inaccessible, and cross-border cluster findings are not disaggregated for Uganda.

sources.title: Ukraine: Building Climate Resilience in Agriculture and Forestry
sources.temporal_coverage: Observations mainly from the 1980s onward and RCP projections through 2100.
sources.methodology: Climate-model ensemble across approximately 7,400 grid points with sector and distributional modelling.
sources.limitations: Prepared before the full-scale invasion, uses older RCPs, and has no war-adjusted exposure baseline.

sources.title: Ukraine's Climate Change Adaptation Communication to UNFCCC
sources.organization: Government of Ukraine and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, national and sectoral with some subnational references
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical evidence and policy status mainly through 2023-2024, with projections to 2100.
sources.methodology: Official synthesis of climate risks, policy arrangements, barriers, needs, and sector priorities.
sources.limitations: Mostly repackages pre-invasion assessments and has limited post-2022 quantitative risk updating.

sources.title: Ukraine Fifth Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment: February 2022-December 2025
sources.organization: Government of Ukraine, World Bank Group, European Commission and United Nations
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, with sector, oblast and hromada detail where available
sources.temporal_coverage: Damage through 31 December 2025, losses with an 18-month projection, and needs for 2026-2035.
sources.methodology: Joint administrative, engineering, remote-sensing, partner, and modelling assessment using sector damage, loss, and needs methods.
sources.limitations: Occupied and frontline data are incomplete, methods evolve, and needs are not outcomes or firm finance commitments.

sources.title: Status of Environment and Climate in Ukraine: Assessing the Impact of War and Implications for Reconstruction
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, with mapped subnational and ecosystem evidence
sources.temporal_coverage: Pre-war baseline through approximately 2024-2025.
sources.methodology: Multi-source environmental synthesis using remote sensing, administrative data, mapped analysis, and policy review.
sources.limitations: Coverage is weakest in occupied and combat areas and attribution among climate, warfare, and land management is often limited. Reuse terms: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0.

sources.title: Attacks against Ukraine's Energy Infrastructure and Update on the Human Rights Situation in Ukraine, 1 December 2025-31 May 2026
sources.organization: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
geographic_coverage: Government-controlled Ukraine and selected affected cities and facilities
sources.temporal_coverage: 1 December 2025 through 31 May 2026.
sources.methodology: Field monitoring, 180 visits, 1,926 interviews overall, and specialized energy-impact visits and interviews.
sources.limitations: No direct occupied-territory access; seasonal cold and heat are not attributed to climate change.

sources.title: Rapid Environmental Assessment of Kakhovka Dam Breach, Ukraine, 2023
sources.organization: United Nations Environment Programme and UNEP-DHI
geographic_coverage: Lower Dnipro, Kakhovka reservoir, downstream and irrigation-dependent areas
sources.temporal_coverage: June-October 2023 with longer-term risk discussion.
sources.methodology: Remote sensing, hydrological analysis, partner data, desk evidence, and expert assessment under access constraints.
sources.limitations: Many impacts were modelled or preliminary; the breach is a conflict-related infrastructure disaster, not a climate event. Reuse is permitted for educational or other non-profit purposes with source acknowledgement.

sources.title: Impact of the Russia-Ukraine Armed Conflict on Water Resources and Water Infrastructure
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, concentrated in eastern and southern incident evidence
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly the first three months after 24 February 2022.
sources.methodology: Systematic compilation of realized and potential impacts from verified public reports and supplementary evidence.
sources.limitations: Early-war and undercounted snapshot with reporting bias and no climate attribution.

sources.title: Rebuilding Ukraine by Reinforcing Regional and Municipal Governance
sources.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sources.temporal_coverage: Primarily pre-February 2022 capacity evidence interpreted for recovery.
sources.methodology: Surveys of 741 municipalities, 119 rayons and 24 oblasts plus Kyiv, with administrative and efficiency analysis.
sources.limitations: Pre-full-scale-war, partly self-reported baseline; current municipal capacity can differ substantially.

sources.title: Final Evaluation of Mykolaiv Recovered
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Evaluation Resource Centre / external evaluation team
geographic_coverage: Mykolaiv Oblast and participating municipalities and institutions
sources.temporal_coverage: Project from July 2023 through December 2025; evaluation October 2025-February 2026.
sources.methodology: External mixed-method final evaluation using interviews, document review, site evidence, and participant surveys.
sources.limitations: Limited counterfactual and causal attribution, low response rates for some surveys, and no national generalizability.

sources.title: Ukraine: Reframing the Narrative of Climate, Environmental Degradation and Conflict
sources.organization: adelphi / Weathering Risk / International Rescue Committee
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, with southern, eastern and community examples
sources.temporal_coverage: Primarily 2022-2024 with pre-war climate baseline.
sources.methodology: Desk review, expert consultations, and qualitative pathway synthesis.
sources.limitations: Expert synthesis rather than causal evaluation; some chains rely on secondary evidence and remain inferential.

sources.title: Priorities for Agricultural Support in Ukraine
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, national and agroecological with east-central hotspots
sources.temporal_coverage: War context through 2024 with climate scenarios at 1.5 and 3 degrees Celsius warming.
sources.methodology: Agricultural-sector review, policy analysis, and model-derived green-water-scarcity estimates.
sources.limitations: Some modelling was forthcoming, scenario results are not observed impacts, and exposure is not fully war-adjusted.

sources.title: Policy Brief: State Strategy on Internal Displacement
sources.organization: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees Ukraine
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, national, regional and community implementation
sources.temporal_coverage: Strategy period 2026-2030.
sources.methodology: Review of the adopted strategy, legal framework, targets, responsibilities, and implementation arrangements.
sources.limitations: Newly adopted policy; first formal assessment is due in 2027 and financing and local delivery remain uncertain. The cover is dated July 2026; an internal page header says June 2026.

sources.title: Southern Bug River: water security and climate changes perspectives for post-war city of Mykolaiv, Ukraine
sources.organization: Snizhko et al., Frontiers in Water
sources.temporal_coverage: Water-supply disruption from April 2022; water-quality conditions reported in the study; hydrological projections for near-future 2021–2050 and far-future 2051–2080.
sources.methodology: WaterGAP2 flow and climate-model ensemble assessment under SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5.
sources.limitations: Separates wartime damage from modeled risks to a proposed replacement; projections are not observed.

sources.title: Water quality in the Dnipro–Donbas canal (Ukraine) under conditions of war and climate change
sources.temporal_coverage: Monitoring observations from 2015–2024; discussion of post-2023 infrastructure changes; author projection to 2050.
sources.methodology: Original canal-water study using official monitoring observations from 2015–2024 and irrigation-water quality indicators.
sources.limitations: Only three sampling campaigns per growing season; the authors say this misses short-term salinity peaks and represents background or seasonal-average conditions.

sources.title: UNDP Ukraine Annual Report 2025: Resilient Recovery and Inclusive Development
geographic_coverage: 22 cities participating in municipal solar-energy contracts
sources.temporal_coverage: UNDP-reported programme activities and results during 2025; report published 22 April 2026.
sources.methodology: Annual implementation report summarizing reported 2025 UNDP energy, recovery and service-support activities.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported outputs; the report does not provide a counterfactual or isolate climate-adaptation effects.

sources.title: Розподілена генерація в Україні: як децентралізовані рішення допомагають тримати тепло та водопостачання в умовах війни
sources.organization: Ministry for Communities and Territories Development of Ukraine
sources.temporal_coverage: Government-reported commissioning and support through 4 January 2026; includes 2025 implementation figures and 2026 plans.
sources.methodology: Ministry news page describing reported distributed-energy commissioning and support for heat, water and other critical services.
sources.limitations: National aggregate figures without named-hromada allocation; operational capability statements are not independent service-outcome evaluations.

sources.title: Evaluación multi-amenaza en cuatro zonas del Uruguay, considerando escenarios de cambio climático. Etapa C: Informe preliminar, Producto 3
sources.organization: Factor CO2 for Uruguay's NAP Ciudades project, with DINAGUA and DINAMA counterparts
sources.temporal_coverage: Report delivered 22 April 2020; local vulnerability indicators use 2011 census data; climate projections cover 2020–2044 and 2045–2099.
sources.methodology: Preliminary multi-hazard GIS combines climate scenarios, urban exposure, census sensitivity and qualitative adaptation capacity.
sources.limitations: Preliminary; local validation pending. Adaptation capacity was not quantified.

sources.title: Uruguay: 2024 Article IV Consultation—Staff Report, IMF Country Report No. 24/215
sources.temporal_coverage: Article IV report completed 14 June 2024; drought analysis includes 2022Q4–2023Q2 and the SMDI reference series 2000–2023.
sources.methodology: IMF macro study uses soil-moisture data, SVAR and DSGE models.
sources.limitations: Weather shocks are not anthropogenic attribution; relocation passage gives no locations.

sources.title: Informe de situación por inundaciones - Fin de la emergencia (08/01/24)
sources.temporal_coverage: Closeout of the 80-day Uruguay River flood emergency of October 2023–January 2024.
sources.methodology: National emergency situation report drawing on SINAE, DINAGUA, meteorological and departmental response information.
sources.limitations: Event-specific official reporting; it does not attribute the flood to long-term anthropogenic climate change.

sources.title: Balance anual de emergencias: los eventos adversos más significativos de 2024
sources.temporal_coverage: Annual emergency balance for 2024, published 10 January 2025.
sources.methodology: SINAE annual summary of hydrometeorological emergencies with affected-people and housing tables by event and department.
sources.limitations: This event inventory reports impacts, not anthropogenic attribution; its aggregate prose conflicts with the table total, so claims use the flood-specific table row or event-specific figures only.

sources.title: Updated Nationally Determined Contribution of the Republic of Uzbekistan
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Uzbekistan; UNFCCC repository
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical warming since the early 1950s; NDC adaptation planning through 2030 and projections through 2050.
sources.methodology: Government NDC with interagency climate and adaptation planning.
sources.limitations: Official assessment; not an implementation evaluation.

sources.title: Climate Action Could Accelerate Growth and Improve Living Standards in Uzbekistan: World Bank Group Report
sources.temporal_coverage: CCDR release gives population risk estimates to 2030 and economic projection to 2050.
sources.methodology: World Bank Group press-release summary of the Uzbekistan Country Climate and Development Report.
sources.limitations: Only the official release was inspected; it does not reproduce all report model assumptions or uncertainty ranges.

sources.title: Karakalpakstan Agriculture Risk Profile for Climate Resilience Capacity Development
sources.temporal_coverage: Four-district climate-resilience risk profile published March 2025; assessment period not specified in the publisher summary.
sources.methodology: GGGI risk profile summarizes climate-resilience factors and vulnerability findings for four target districts in Karakalpakstan.
sources.limitations: Only the substantive publisher summary was accessible; it omits sample design, indicator construction, and district-specific breakdowns.

sources.title: Water and conflict in Central Asia
geographic_coverage: Amu Darya and Syr Darya basins
sources.temporal_coverage: Review published in 2025; assesses regional water/conflict evidence, including 1990-2024 and future prospects.
sources.methodology: Twelve-page research synthesis compares six water-scarcity metrics and reviews regional climate, water, and conflict evidence.
sources.limitations: Conflict evidence is regional, not Uzbekistan-specific; scarcity-conflict causality is debated.

sources.title: UNDP in Uzbekistan and Uzhydromet sum up the results of joint activities on developing climate resilience of farming communities in Karakalpakstan
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme; Center of Hydrometeorological Service of Uzbekistan (Uzhydromet)
sources.temporal_coverage: Adaptation Fund project implemented 2014-November 30, 2021; closeout results announced November 2021.
sources.methodology: UNDP-Uzhydromet project-closeout announcement reports equipment, service reach, and uptake figures presented at the final coordination meeting.
sources.limitations: This is a project announcement, not an independent evaluation; beneficiary counts may overlap and the page provides no comparison group or measured impact estimates.

sources.title: From local knowledge to local action: Communities shape restoration in three regions of Uzbekistan
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
geographic_coverage: Lower Amu Darya State Biosphere Reserve
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO-reported field visits and community workshops, including June 2026 consultations.
sources.methodology: FAO account summarizes field assessments, June 2026 workshops, participant proposals, and visits to candidate restoration sites under FOLUR-Uzbekistan.
sources.limitations: The page reports consultation findings and proposals, not a sampled vulnerability study, implemented restoration outcomes, or an independent evaluation.

sources.title: Building back better and stronger in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
sources.temporal_coverage: Beryl impacts in 2024 and recovery outputs through 2025.
sources.methodology: Implementer feature with beneficiary accounts.
sources.limitations: Reported outputs; no attribution of Beryl to climate change or independent impact evaluation.

sources.title: St. Vincent and the Grenadines Secures $20 Million to Strengthen Disaster Resilience
sources.temporal_coverage: Risk diagnosis and policy financing announced inApril2025.
sources.methodology: Financing announcement with vulnerability assessment.
sources.limitations: Policy commitments and credit availability are not evaluated resilience outcomes.

sources.title: UNDP part of multi-agency response to Hurricane Beryl
sources.temporal_coverage: 2024 emergency recovery and training.
sources.methodology: Operational account.
sources.limitations: Reported support and training; no independent causal or peacebuilding evaluation.

sources.title: Hurricane Beryl 2024: Global Rapid Post-Disaster Damage Estimation (GRADE) Report
sources.organization: World Bank Group and Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery
sources.temporal_coverage: Rapid direct-damage assessment following Hurricane Beryl on 1 July 2024; report as of 26 July 2024.
sources.methodology: Rapid engineering-based damage estimation using reported assessments, exposure data, satellite imagery and modeled wind fields.
sources.limitations: Preliminary rapid estimates; damage to buildings on Saint Vincent was not disaggregated by census division or damage level.

sources.title: National Climate Change Policy of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
sources.organization: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines; prepared with technical assistance from CANARI
sources.temporal_coverage: Policy priority period 2018–2030; vulnerability narrative draws on historical events and farmer observations through 2019.
sources.methodology: Government policy document informed by literature, climate modeling and three rounds of stakeholder consultation during 2018–2019.
sources.limitations: The document mixes historical observations with policy priorities; stated actions are not evidence of implementation or current outcomes.

sources.title: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines on the Path to Recovery with support from UNDP, Canada and CDEMA
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Barbados and the Eastern Caribbean
sources.temporal_coverage: Post-Beryl recovery activities, including workshops in November 2025 and March 2026.
sources.methodology: UNDP news account of partner-supported post-disaster training and school-equipment activities.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported outputs; the page provides no independent evaluation of preparedness or resilience effects.

sources.title: Building Resilience with Frontier Technology: Union Island’s 3D Printing and Design Capacity Building
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Accelerator Lab, Barbados and the Eastern Caribbean
sources.temporal_coverage: Workshop and printer handover in November 2025; blog published 16 December 2025.
sources.methodology: UNDP Accelerator Lab account of a local design-and-fabrication workshop and stakeholder engagement.
sources.limitations: This is a programme blog; intended local-use cases are not evidence of tested emergency response or measured climate outcomes.

sources.title: Evaluación de la vulnerabilidad ante el efecto del cambio climático: República Bolivariana de Venezuela
sources.organization: Ministry of Popular Power for Ecosocialism (MINEC), with FAO implementation support
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 assessment; projections for 2021–2040, 2041–2060 and 2061–2080, with 1970–2000 baseline.
sources.methodology: Sectoral projections use two GCMs and SSP2-4.5/SSP5-8.5.
sources.limitations: Full text read on user-uploaded Scribd mirror, not official host.

sources.title: Annual Report 2025: Chapter IV.B, Venezuela
sources.organization: Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (IACHR), Organization of American States
sources.temporal_coverage: Annual human-rights monitoring for 2025; climate-event passages cover the first half of 2025.
sources.methodology: IACHR annual monitoring chapter synthesizes state statements, UN findings and cited reporting.
sources.limitations: Some environmental and event details are attributed to cited sources; this is not a climate-attribution study.

sources.title: Venezuela Situation Report No. 2 (Year-End), 31 December 2024
sources.temporal_coverage: Situation and UNICEF response from 1 January to 31 December 2024; issued 6 February 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF country situation report combines humanitarian monitoring and agency response data.
sources.limitations: Agency-reported reach and needs; not a population-wide impact evaluation or climate-attribution analysis.

sources.title: Venezuela Humanitarian Situation Report No. 1 (Mid-Year), 30 June 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Situation and UNICEF response from 1 January to 30 June 2025; issued 1 August 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF country situation report combines humanitarian monitoring and agency response data.
sources.limitations: Agency-reported reach and needs; reported access constraints are contextual, not a causal evaluation.

sources.title: Living or Leaving: Life in the Mekong Delta Region of Viet Nam
sources.temporal_coverage: Report published 2025; the Life in the Mekong Survey covered 5,000 households across 13 delta provinces in April–June 2024; poverty simulations extend to 2050.
sources.methodology: 2024 household survey, official statistics and climate-shock simulations.
sources.limitations: Not causal; regional, not province-specific.

sources.title: Report on Children’s Perspectives on Climate Change, Environmental Protection and Socio-Economic Development
sources.organization: UNICEF Viet Nam and Viet Nam Ministry of Planning and Investment
sources.temporal_coverage: Published July 2025; student survey and consultations concern climate perceptions and policies in three Mekong Delta provinces.
sources.methodology: Questionnaire survey of 756 students in six schools, plus focus groups and institutional consultations in three provinces.
sources.limitations: Self-reported school sample; findings do not estimate province-wide prevalence.

sources.title: Insights from Viet Nam: Delivering child-responsive rapid response and resilience-building interventions informed by the principles of Accountability to Affected Populations
sources.organization: UNICEF Innocenti – Global Office of Research and Foresight
sources.temporal_coverage: Case study covers UNICEF response to Typhoon Yagi from September 2024 through June 2025; published December 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF case study reports response activities and draws on the government-led multi-sector damage assessment.
sources.limitations: Agency case study; not a counterfactual evaluation of impacts or outcomes.

sources.title: Viet Nam: Typhoon Yagi and Floods Joint Response Plan, September 2024–June 2025
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs on behalf of the UN Country Team and partners
sources.temporal_coverage: Joint response plan issued 27 September 2024 for typhoon and flood response and early recovery through June 2025.
sources.methodology: OCHA-consolidated interagency plan uses government disaster data and sector assessments to set needs, targets and response priorities.
sources.limitations: Planning estimates and commitments, not an outcome evaluation; event-specific and dated.

sources.title: Improving Lives and Building Resilience in Vanuatu
sources.temporal_coverage: 2015 cyclone; 2016–2023 programme results
sources.methodology: Implementer's results account.
sources.limitations: Reported construction and access outputs, not an independent causal or climate-attribution study.

sources.title: Strengthening resilience of the Vanuatu energy sector against climate-induced disasters
sources.temporal_coverage: Undated energy-resilience design
sources.methodology: Project diagnosis and proposed institutional/technical work.
sources.limitations: Design commitments and intended benefits are not verified outcomes.

sources.title: Impact of Climate Change on Tropical Cyclones Over Vanuatu: A Case for Informing Disaster Planning and Adaptation Strategies
sources.organization: Krishneel K. Sharma, Savin S. Chand and Soubhik Biswas, Federation University
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed cyclone tracks 1971–2021; CMIP5 future-climate comparisons 2071–2100 versus 1971–2000 under RCP8.5.
sources.methodology: Analyzes SPEArTC cyclone tracks and calibrated CMIP5 simulations using a 500-km buffer for provincial estimates.
sources.limitations: Province-level cyclone proximity is not a direct-landfall count. Future projections use CMIP5 RCP8.5 and model-dependent estimates.

sources.title: As the water flows – remote communities in Vanuatu creating pathways to climate resilience
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Pacific Office
sources.temporal_coverage: Community consultations, project design and reported implementation status through March 2025.
sources.methodology: UNDP project case account drawing on statements from Vanuatu government officials and community participants.
sources.limitations: Not an independent impact evaluation; the project was not yet reported as delivering operating household water service.

sources.title: National Policy on Climate Change and Disaster-Induced Displacement
sources.organization: Government of Vanuatu, National Advisory Board on Climate Change and Disaster Risk Reduction
sources.temporal_coverage: National displacement policy and conditions described in the 2018 document, including 2018 relocation activity.
sources.methodology: National policy framework informed by stakeholder consultations and inter-agency planning.
sources.limitations: Policy describes risks and intended safeguards, not a current implementation review; pathway statements are conditional and multi-causal.

sources.title: Ministry of Climate Change Annual Report 2024
sources.organization: Government of Vanuatu, Ministry of Climate Change
sources.temporal_coverage: Ministry activities, project progress and constraints reported for calendar year 2024, mostly as of 31 December 2024.
sources.methodology: Government ministry annual administrative and project-progress reporting.
sources.limitations: Self-reported progress; several items are procurement, plans or targets rather than independently verified service outcomes.

sources.title: Climate-related disasters and temperature extremes are not associated with conflict risk in Pacific Island countries
sources.organization: Tobias Ide, Ore Koren and Luke Derrick, Environment and Security
sources.temporal_coverage: Geocoded social-conflict and climate analysis for 2012–2020 in three Pacific Island countries.
sources.methodology: Peer-reviewed panel analysis uses 0.5-degree grid-cell-year units, geocoded social conflict events and climate-disaster data.
sources.limitations: Results are pooled across three countries; the study cannot test proposed mediating pathways and does not cover all precipitation or slow-onset effects.

sources.title: Samoa set to strengthen disaster readiness, protect livelihoods and create jobs with new World Bank support
sources.temporal_coverage: March 2026 approval
sources.methodology: Project announcement; body publication date differs from URL.
sources.limitations: Project design and intended benefits; implementation and outcomes are not established.

sources.title: Safer, more resilient and reliable transport for Samoa
sources.temporal_coverage: 2018/2020 flooding and 2022 approval
sources.methodology: Transport project announcement.
sources.limitations: Project design and intended benefits; implementation and outcomes are not established.

sources.title: Improved roads driving renewed confidence in Samoa
sources.temporal_coverage: 2023 feature and earlier storm damage
sources.methodology: Project feature and business testimony.
sources.limitations: Implementer reporting and testimony, not an independent impact evaluation.

sources.title: Climate micro-mobilities as adaptation practice in the Pacific: the case of Samoa
sources.organization: Anita Latai-Niusulu, Masami Tsujita and Andreas Neef; Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
sources.temporal_coverage: Talanoa fieldwork June–August 2021; mobility histories cover participants' prior 10–30 years; site context includes 2016 census data and 2009 tsunami experience.
sources.methodology: Qualitative comparison using Samoan-language talanoa interviews; 40 households invited across two sites.
sources.limitations: Small non-random sample; mixed movement drivers; not prevalence or causal-violence research.

sources.title: The effects of Climate Change on the small village of Salei'a
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate risks and Adaptation Fund-supported works reported as of October 2019; programme began in 2013.
sources.methodology: UNDP project case story drawing on project information and a statement by Salei'a's mayor.
sources.limitations: Sponsored project account, not an independent impact evaluation; reported completion and benefits are bounded to the article's 2019 account.

sources.title: Community-Based Adaptation in Small Island Developing States, and Mekong-Asia-Pacific Regions
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Global Environment Facility Small Grants Programme
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional programme case account, including Matafa'a outcomes reported during and after the 2011 El Niño drought.
sources.methodology: UNDP-GEF SGP regional report summarizing Matafa'a adaptation-project implementation.
sources.limitations: Programme-reported, not independently evaluated; historical, not current water status.

sources.title: Pacific Peoples and Climate-Related (Im)Mobility: A Synthesis Report on Scale, Pattern and Impact, Now and in the Future
sources.organization: Bruce Burson, Evelyn Marsters, Richard Bedford and Sandy Morrison; prepared for New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade
sources.temporal_coverage: Synthesis published June 2024, drawing on earlier and commissioned Pacific household, community and mobility research; Samoa examples include 2009 tsunami relocation and 2023–2024 fieldwork synthesis.
sources.methodology: Synthesis of published/commissioned Pacific studies, case reports, fieldwork and policy sources.
sources.limitations: Regional, not Samoa prevalence research; violence signal is caveated.

sources.title: Pacific Region Preparedness, Adaptation, and Resilience Program – Samoa Project: Environmental and Social Management Framework
sources.organization: Government of Samoa, Pacific Region Preparedness, Adaptation and Resilience Program – Samoa Project
sources.temporal_coverage: Framework dated June 2025 for a six-year project planned to begin in August 2025; township-plan works and risks were preliminary at report date.
sources.methodology: Project framework identifying preliminary risks, safeguards and responsibilities.
sources.limitations: Preparation-stage risks and plans, not outcomes.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Western Balkans 6, Kosovo Country Compendium
sources.temporal_coverage: Country compendium dated October 2024; includes hazard history and climate projections.
sources.methodology: Country assessment combining climate and hazard exposure, socioeconomic vulnerability, adaptation analysis, and economic modeling.
sources.limitations: The report summarizes model outputs and cited hazard inventories; figures are not a new event-attribution study.

sources.title: Climate Change Strategy 2019-2028 and Action Plan on Climate Change 2019-2021
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment and Spatial Planning, Government of Kosovo
sources.temporal_coverage: Government strategy document dated 2018; action-plan period 2019-2021.
sources.methodology: Strategy developed by an inter-ministerial working group with expert support and stakeholder consultation, including a local questionnaire exercise.
sources.limitations: The inspected PDF is the 2018 strategy version and contains dated baseline data; it is not evidence of current implementation status.

sources.title: Kosovo's First and Voluntary Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure, Government of Kosovo
sources.temporal_coverage: Voluntary NDC adopted in 2025; mitigation targets extend to 2030 and adaptation sections describe current and prospective risks.
sources.methodology: Government submission synthesizing climate-risk evidence and proposed measures.
sources.limitations: Many measures are voluntary, conditional, and unfunded.

sources.title: A Climate Landscape Analysis for Children: Policy Brief
sources.temporal_coverage: Child climate and environmental vulnerability synthesis, including observed events and health reports through 2023.
sources.methodology: Four-page UNICEF policy brief summarizing its 2024 Climate Landscape Analysis for Children.
sources.limitations: Brief-level summary; it gives no district rates or causal estimates.

sources.title: Mine Action and the Resilience of Communities to Climate Change
sources.organization: Geneva International Centre for Humanitarian Demining (GICHD)
sources.temporal_coverage: Mine-action policy and community case studies, including clearance activity through 2023 and status statements made in the report.
sources.methodology: Document review and interviews; Kosovo material covers mine-action institutions and two local cases.
sources.limitations: Qualitative cases are not causal impact evaluations; status reflects the report period.

sources.title: Intervention Plan for Rural Development to Mitigate and Adapt to Climate Change, 2023–2028
sources.organization: Municipality of Prizren, with support from UNDP Kosovo
sources.temporal_coverage: Municipal rural-development plan for 2023–2028, dated November 2022.
sources.methodology: Municipal sectoral intervention plan with proposed actions, timelines, responsible offices and estimated costs.
sources.limitations: The plan records proposals and scheduled actions, not verified implementation; 2023–2025 milestones are now elapsed.

sources.title: Community Flood Vulnerability and Adaptive Capacity in the Municipality of Podujeva: Results of the CLIPP Household Survey
sources.organization: University of Prishtina and Municipality of Podujeva
sources.temporal_coverage: Household survey conducted 1 June–31 July 2026; record version published 5 August 2026.
sources.methodology: Municipal household survey with 101 responses; the publisher record summarizes aggregated findings and methods.
sources.limitations: Publisher record only was accessible; findings describe participating households, not a representative municipal sample; item denominators vary.

sources.title: Yemen Country Climate and Development Report: Policy Note
geographic_coverage: Yemen, national with spatial exposure and sector modelling
sources.temporal_coverage: Recent baseline with projections mainly to 2050 and economic scenarios to 2040.
sources.methodology: Climate and macroeconomic modelling, spatial exposure analysis, and sector policy synthesis.
sources.limitations: Scenario results are not forecasts; the PDF contains erroneous West Bank and Gaza running headers and substantial data gaps. Reuse terms identified in the publisher catalog: CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO.

sources.title: Charting the Course: A Water Security Diagnostic for Yemen
