geographic_coverage: Yemen, national with basin and city cases including Taiz
sources.temporal_coverage: Structural history and conflict-era evidence through 2024.
sources.methodology: Administrative and remote-sensing evidence, mobile survey, literature synthesis, modelling, and consultations with nearly 1,700 participants.
sources.limitations: Hydrological monitoring is degraded, groundwater information is incomplete, and consultation evidence is not a causal estimate. The full PDF exceeded the browser extraction limit; indexed primary text was inspected for the Foreword, Executive Summary, section 3.1.1 at printed p. 61, and section 6.2.3. The cited institutional passage at printed pp. 95-111 was not inspected, so the dependent evidence record was excluded.

sources.title: Yemen's NDC 3.0 Vision
sources.organization: Republic of Yemen and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate 1971-2020, mid-century projections, and policy roadmap through 2035.
sources.methodology: Official climate-risk and policy synthesis with sector goals and institutional roadmap.
sources.limitations: The registered document calls itself a Vision and says final NDC preparation and submission would occur in 2026; operational status is unclear.

sources.title: Water-related Conflict Assessment Report
geographic_coverage: Selected districts in Abyan, Hadramawt, and Dhamar
sources.temporal_coverage: Field and project evidence mainly from 2022-2023.
sources.methodology: Local conflict assessment, interviews, community consultation, institutional analysis, and project-linked field evidence.
sources.limitations: Narrow local coverage and project-linked evidence without independent measurement of durable conflict reduction. Originally published April 2022; updated September 2023; PDF copyright 2024. The publication states that reproduction requires prior permission.

sources.title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Yemen 2023
sources.organization: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute and Norwegian Institute of International Affairs
geographic_coverage: Yemen, national with selected local examples
sources.temporal_coverage: Conflict period through 2023.
sources.methodology: Four-page secondary synthesis of climate, livelihood, mobility, and conflict pathways.
sources.limitations: Secondary and concise; it identifies conditional mechanisms rather than demonstrating causal climate-conflict effects.

sources.title: Climate and Health Vulnerability Assessment: Republic of Yemen
sources.temporal_coverage: Recent baseline with CMIP6 projections to mid-century.
sources.methodology: Desktop health-vulnerability assessment using CCKP and CMIP6 climate indicators, facility data, and adaptive-capacity indicators.
sources.limitations: Facility exposure does not establish structural vulnerability or service failure; some labels and units appear inconsistent.

sources.title: Yemen, Government-Controlled Areas: Acute Food Insecurity Analysis, March-December 2026
geographic_coverage: 118 districts in 12 Government of Yemen-controlled governorates
sources.temporal_coverage: March-December 2026 analysis and projection periods.
sources.methodology: IPC convergence-of-evidence classification using food security, livelihoods, prices, assistance, conflict, and hazard evidence.
sources.limitations: Medium evidence level and partial territorial coverage; results are multi-causal and not attributable to climate alone. The full report is dated 23 June 2026; the associated snapshot and IPC portal were released on 21 May 2026.

sources.title: Independent Country Programme Evaluation: Yemen
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Independent Evaluation Office
geographic_coverage: Yemen with fieldwork in seven governorates
sources.temporal_coverage: UNDP country programme 2022-2025.
sources.methodology: Independent evaluation using document review, 169 interviews, more than 25 visits, and 13 focus groups.
sources.limitations: No focus groups in de facto authority areas and limited causal attribution of welfare, resilience, or peace outcomes.

sources.title: Inter-Agency Humanitarian Evaluation of the Yemen Crisis
geographic_coverage: Yemen with six-governorate survey and field evidence
sources.temporal_coverage: Humanitarian response from 2015 through 2021.
sources.methodology: Independent theory-based evaluation with 144 interviews, 64 focus groups, project visits, aid-worker survey, SMS survey, and secondary analysis.
sources.limitations: Low SMS response, restricted Marib and de facto authority access, agency data-sharing constraints, and no climate-specific evaluation design. The final report is dated 13/14 July 2022; the WFP publisher page is dated 7 December 2022.

sources.title: Yemen Emergency Crisis Response Project P159053: Implementation Completion Report Review
geographic_coverage: Yemen, project areas and participating local institutions
sources.temporal_coverage: Emergency project implementation and completion through 2022.
sources.methodology: Independent desk review of completion evidence, monitoring, third-party verification, outputs, and stated outcomes.
sources.limitations: Welfare effects and causal mechanisms were inadequately specified, and output delivery is stronger evidence than sustained resilience.

sources.title: Final Evaluation: Strengthening Institutional and Economic Resilience in Yemen
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme and European Union external evaluation team
sources.temporal_coverage: Programme implementation through 2025.
sources.methodology: External mixed-method evaluation with document review, 105 stakeholders, site evidence, and qualitative assessment.
sources.limitations: No structured impact assessment or counterfactual; maintenance, inclusion, and peace effects remain incompletely measured.

sources.title: Conflict Resilience of Water and Energy Supply Infrastructure: Insights from Yemen
geographic_coverage: Urban Yemen, including Sana'a and Taiz
sources.temporal_coverage: Conflict-era evidence primarily from 2014-2019.
sources.methodology: Qualitative resilience framework using interviews, narratives, utility information, and secondary data.
sources.limitations: Limited representativeness and incomplete quantitative data; continuity is not consistent system performance. Reuse terms: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0.

sources.title: Livelihood Resilience and Adaptation Practices Among Agricultural Communities in Yemen
geographic_coverage: Six rural study areas in Abyan, Hadramawt, Marib, and Taiz
sources.temporal_coverage: Fieldwork July-October 2025; publication 2026.
sources.methodology: Purposive survey of 164 people, 20 interviews, six focus groups, ethnographic observation, and grounded-theory analysis.
sources.limitations: Non-representative local sample, only 13 survey respondents in Marib, and causal claims rely heavily on perceptions and qualitative evidence. The PDF is publicly downloadable and copyrighted by the Sana'a Center, but no permissive reuse licence was identified.

sources.title: Undercurrents: How Conflict, Climate Change and the Environment Intersect in Yemen
sources.organization: adelphi research and the European Institute of Peace, under the Weathering Risk Peace Pillar
sources.temporal_coverage: Primary fieldwork in 2023–2024 and reported conditions/cases through 2024.
sources.methodology: Mixed methods: 2,283 survey respondents, 69 focus-group participants and 58 interviews across nine governorates.
sources.limitations: Security constrained access; comprehensive climate data and projections were lacking. Cases are not nationally representative estimates.

sources.title: UNDP Yemen: Building Resilience: Supporting Farmers to Face the Impact of Climate Change in Yemen
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, published by United Nations in Yemen
sources.temporal_coverage: FSRRP implementation and farmer accounts reported in March 2024, with project photos dated 2023.
sources.methodology: UNDP project feature using named farmer and implementing-partner accounts and reported project outputs.
sources.limitations: Programme reporting and attributed testimony, not an independent impact evaluation; no comparison group is provided.

sources.title: From Seasonal to Sustainable: Year-Round Farming
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO-supported Shibam interventions and farmer accounts reported in February 2026.
sources.methodology: FAO feature story based on project implementation and local farmer accounts in Shibam.
sources.limitations: Project feature, not an independent evaluation; outcomes are reported by FAO and participants.

sources.title: Addressing Community Needs While Redressing the Impact of Climate Change in Yemen
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Regional Bureau for Arab States
sources.temporal_coverage: SIERY project implementation and local authority actions reported in April 2025.
sources.methodology: UNDP project feature describing local-authority investments and reported programme outputs.
sources.limitations: Promotional implementation account; it provides no independent impact design and some metrics lack denominators or baselines.

sources.title: Cluster Evaluation of FAO Resilience Activities in Yemen 2018–2024
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Office of Evaluation
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO resilience activity period 2018–2024; date of the evaluation webpage not stated.
sources.methodology: FAO publisher-page summary of a cluster evaluation covering water-focused natural-resource management, agriculture, livestock and governance under the HDP nexus.
sources.limitations: Only the official webpage summary was accessible; the linked report returned 403 and its local detail was not verified.

sources.title: South Africa's Second Nationally Determined Contribution under the Paris Agreement
sources.temporal_coverage: Recent climate impacts, current vulnerability reporting, adaptation commitments for 2031-2035, and future climate risks.
sources.methodology: Government NDC and adaptation communication.
sources.limitations: National self-report; disaggregated impact data are limited.

sources.title: 3 Sector Climate Readiness Study: Consolidated Workshop Report
sources.organization: Presidential Climate Commission; prepared by OneWorld Sustainable Investments
sources.temporal_coverage: Sector adaptation-readiness workshops and synthesis, with discussion of current capacity and institutional arrangements.
sources.methodology: PCC workshop synthesis of sector presentations and group discussions.
sources.limitations: Consultative report; no representative survey.

sources.title: Cape Winelands District Municipality Risk Profile Report
sources.organization: Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), GreenBook
sources.temporal_coverage: Vulnerability indices for 1996 and 2011; climate baselines and modeled drought, flood and water-supply risks through 2050.
sources.methodology: GIS model using secondary indicators, hazard data and settlement projections.
sources.limitations: Not locally surveyed; social indicators are dated; water estimates omit reticulation condition.

sources.title: Weather and Crime—Cautious evidence from South Africa
sources.organization: Jorg Ankel-Peters, Anna Bruederle and Gareth Roberts; Q Open
sources.temporal_coverage: Monthly crime and weather observations from January 2001 to March 2012.
sources.methodology: Peer-reviewed reduced-form study of monthly police crime records and gridded weather across 1,158 wards, using an SPEI drought measure.
sources.limitations: Weather, not anthropogenic climate, is studied; effects are subtle, no mediation analysis is conducted, and monthly data limit mechanism interpretation.

sources.title: Zambia Country Climate and Development Report: Executive Summary
sources.temporal_coverage: Current impacts and dry-hot scenario projections through 2050, reported in 2026
sources.methodology: CCDR assesses climate-development scenarios, including a dry-hot pathway, and economy-wide effects.
sources.limitations: Executive-summary results are scenario-specific; detailed methods are outside this document.

sources.title: National Adaptation Plan for Zambia
sources.organization: Government of Zambia, Ministry of Green Economy and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: Current vulnerability assessment and medium- to long-term adaptation plan, reported in 2023
sources.methodology: NAP uses a qualitative climate-vulnerability and adaptive-capacity matrix.
sources.limitations: Matrix is qualitative, not quantified loss or causal analysis.

sources.title: Zambia: Drought Response Appeal May 2024 - December 2024
sources.organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator Office in Zambia and OCHA
sources.temporal_coverage: 2023/2024 rainfall-season drought impacts and response outlook, as reported in May 2024.
sources.methodology: UN appeal page summarizes government crop assessment, meteorological and IPC information available in May 2024.
sources.limitations: Appeal-era figures and anticipated risks are dated; provincial and assessed-district totals do not identify local causal incidents.

sources.title: Zambia Country Office Humanitarian Situation Report - 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: UNICEF Zambia humanitarian needs and programme reporting for 2025, including lingering effects of the 2023/2024 drought.
sources.methodology: UNICEF annual report of humanitarian needs and programme outputs.
sources.limitations: National and programme aggregates; limited district attribution and independent outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Post-Implementation Beneficiary Satisfaction and Protection Monitoring Survey
sources.organization: UNICEF Zambia, with the University of Zambia and government partners
sources.temporal_coverage: Cross-sectional perceptions of assistance delivered during the 2023/2024 drought and floods, collected in 2025.
sources.methodology: Mixed-methods survey and focus groups with 950 assistance recipients; descriptive district comparisons.
sources.limitations: Programme-area recipients; summary lists eight districts, methods seven.

sources.title: New Beginnings for Farming Families Rebuilding After Drought in Zambia
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO and partner drought-recovery activities and participant accounts reported in March 2026; effects of the 2023/2024 drought and 2025/2026 rains.
sources.methodology: FAO feature describing programme outputs and accounts from participating farmers and officials.
sources.limitations: Programme feature, not an independent evaluation; participant examples do not estimate prevalence or impact.

sources.title: Rebuilding Hope After the Lundazi Floods
sources.temporal_coverage: Accounts of heavy-rainfall floods beginning in late December 2025 and UNICEF response reported in January 2026.
sources.methodology: UNICEF field feature based on programme reporting and named household accounts in flood-affected districts.
sources.limitations: Human-interest and response account; named household testimony is illustrative, not representative, and response impact is not independently evaluated.

sources.title: Zimbabwe's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0) Country Statement, 2025-2035
sources.organization: Government of Zimbabwe, Ministry of Environment, Climate and Wildlife
geographic_coverage: communities dependent on climate-sensitive natural resources
sources.temporal_coverage: Reported drought seasons from 2012 to 2024 and climate-hazard outlook, in a 2025 NDC
sources.methodology: NDC summarizes national hazard trends and adaptation priorities drawn from the NAP.
sources.limitations: Hazard section provides no district-level event-loss counts or event attribution.

sources.title: Zimbabwe Economic Update: Improving Resilience to Weather Shocks and Climate Change
sources.temporal_coverage: National agriculture profile and 2023-2024 El Nino drought impacts, reported in January 2025
sources.methodology: World Bank update summary reports sector exposure and agricultural and macroeconomic effects of the El Nino drought.
sources.limitations: Press page summarizes the update; calculation methods and subnational outcomes are not shown.

sources.title: Zimbabwe Drought Flash Appeal: May 2024–April 2025
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs and UN Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator for Zimbabwe
sources.temporal_coverage: El Niño drought conditions through May 2024 and the humanitarian appeal period May 2024–April 2025.
sources.methodology: UN inter-agency appeal drawing on the government crop assessment, ZimVAC and sector-cluster analyses.
sources.limitations: Appeal-era estimates and risk analysis; protection links are not incident-level causal evaluations.

sources.title: Humanitarian Action for Children Factsheet, 2025 Projection: Zimbabwe
sources.temporal_coverage: 2024 drought, nutrition and water-source data with a UNICEF appeal outlook for the now-expired 2025 response period.
sources.methodology: UNICEF appeal using ZimVAC, health-surveillance and water-point data plus a named field account.
sources.limitations: 2025 targets expired; claims use dated 2024 conditions and one illustrative case.

sources.title: Chizivano Shava: Innovating Water Harvesting and Climate-Smart Agriculture in Mwenezi
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate Resilient Livelihoods project practices and reported outputs through 2024, described in March 2025.
sources.methodology: UNDP project feature using a named lead farmer and extension officer account and reported project outputs.
sources.limitations: Project feature and individual testimony, not a representative household survey or independent impact evaluation.

sources.title: GCF Secretariat Witnesses Climate Investment in Action Across Zimbabwe
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Zimbabwe, reporting a Green Climate Fund Secretariat field mission
sources.temporal_coverage: GCF/UNDP field visit in August 2026 and project results reported in September 2026.
sources.methodology: UNDP narrative of a GCF Secretariat field mission, project outputs, officials and farmer accounts.
sources.limitations: Implementer and mission reporting; results are not independently evaluated and participant accounts are illustrative.

sources.title: Towads a common vision of climate, peace and security in Zimbabwe
sources.organization: Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, CGIAR Climate Security team, SAPPC and ACCORD
sources.temporal_coverage: A two-day stakeholder workshop and report published in 2024; publisher page summarizes the report's shared vision.
sources.methodology: Official publication-page summary of a two-day multi-stakeholder climate, peace and security workshop convened in Harare.
sources.limitations: Only the publisher-page excerpt was accessible; pathways reflect workshop synthesis, not tested causal findings or named local cases.

pathways.climate_pressure: Recurrent drought, above-normal heat and possible spring rainfall decline.
pathways.documented_impact: Crop/rangeland and water stress; reduced agricultural livelihood security.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Income loss, food prices, debt, thin labour markets and reduced humanitarian assistance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where household reserves, markets and assistance are weak, climate-related livelihood losses may increase negative coping, distress mobility and localized grievances; violence is not an automatic result.
geographies: National mechanism with high exposure documented in Central Highlands and multiple drought-affected districts
pathways.uncertainty: No national causal study demonstrates a drought -> conflict effect while controlling for these factors. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought can deepen livelihood stress through agriculture, water, markets and aid constraints, potentially increasing harmful coping or grievances, but available evidence does not demonstrate that it causes violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, slower recharge and higher evaporative demand.
pathways.documented_impact: Difficult household water access and declining groundwater availability.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Large return flows, population concentration, over-extraction, weak infrastructure, water costs and queues at shared sources.
pathways.possible_consequence: Local water disputes or host-returnee tension may increase where scarce supplies and costs cannot be managed equitably.
geographies: broader mechanism plausible but not nationally demonstrated
pathways.uncertainty: The relative contribution of drought versus return flows and long-term over-extraction is not quantified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: humanitarian WASH investment and demand management
pathways.compact_statement: In surveyed Herat and Kandahar communities, drought and recharge constraints interact with returns, extraction and weak infrastructure; this compound water stress has been associated with localized tensions but not demonstrated organized conflict.

pathways.climate_pressure: Prolonged drought and episodic floods.
pathways.documented_impact: Loss of livelihoods/assets and deteriorating access to food, water and shelter.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Household savings/assets, debt, rental costs, service access and social networks.
pathways.possible_consequence: When coping options are exhausted, households may relocate; displacement can then reproduce exposure and increase protection and livelihood risks.
geographies: Nahr Shahi and Sholgareh in Balkh
pathways.uncertainty: Purposive qualitative data cannot estimate how frequently drought produces displacement nationally. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Balkh evidence documents a gradual drought-livelihood-displacement process, but household resources and social/service conditions substantially mediate whether movement occurs.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, flood and associated livelihood/service shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: Greater need for income diversification, disaster assistance and health/WASH services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Restrictions on women’s work, mobility and public participation, plus sociocultural norms and shortages of women service providers.
pathways.possible_consequence: Women and female-headed households may have fewer adaptation and recovery options and may depend more heavily on home-based or informal coping.
geographies: with detailed livelihood evidence from Herat
pathways.uncertainty: Restrictions and enforcement vary spatially; available studies do not estimate an independent climate-adaptation effect. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: targeted financial/assets support and availability of women service staff
pathways.compact_statement: Political and social restrictions can narrow women’s options for responding to climate shocks, although household resources and provincial context produce substantial variation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought/flood demand on food, health, water and livelihood systems.
pathways.documented_impact: High food/water needs and increased demand for recovery support.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Declining international assistance, political constraints on engagement and non-standard delivery channels.
pathways.possible_consequence: Lower service and adaptation coverage may prolong vulnerability after climate shocks and weaken household buffers.
alternative_explanations: workforce shortages and general fiscal constraints
pathways.uncertainty: No study located quantitatively estimates how much aid contraction changed climate-specific recovery outcomes. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Aid and institutional constraints plausibly reduce climate-recovery capacity by weakening already strained services, but climate-specific outcome effects remain poorly evaluated.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and climatic stress on transboundary river systems.
pathways.documented_impact: Greater pressure on available water.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Dam/irrigation decisions, allocation rules, weak transboundary mechanisms and bilateral politics.
pathways.possible_consequence: Water disputes may contribute to interstate tension; conversely, cooperative water governance may create dialogue opportunities.
pathways.uncertainty: The climate contribution to the 2023 dispute cannot be isolated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: water diplomacy and joint disaster preparedness
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress can intensify the importance of shared water, but allocation and political decisions are indispensable mediators; water cooperation can also support dialogue.

pathways.climate_pressure: Continuing drought, flood and temperature risk.
pathways.documented_impact: Continuing need for climate information, DRR, resilient livelihoods and water management.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Political transition in 2021, altered institutional structures, donor engagement constraints and project suspension.
pathways.possible_consequence: Institutional learning, national/provincial capacity building and continuity of adaptation programmes may weaken even when some community assets remain.
geographies: National institutions plus former CDRRP project areas
alternative_explanations: funding cycles and weak M&E independent of political transition
pathways.uncertainty: Current provincial and sectoral institutional capacity has not been systematically mapped; the pathway is supported by projected climate pressure, governance constraints and the interrupted 2017-2021 project, not the unread 2015 INDC. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: international technical support and alternative monitored financing
pathways.compact_statement: Political and institutional disruption can interrupt higher-level adaptation capacity even where some community-level resilience investments persist.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, flood and compound displacement/return pressures.
pathways.documented_impact: High unmet needs among displaced and returning households.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Strength of family, neighbourhood, charity and community-support networks.
pathways.possible_consequence: Strong informal support may reduce immediate exclusion, destitution and host-returnee tension, although its durability under prolonged poverty is uncertain.
pathways.uncertainty: No evaluation measures whether solidarity mechanisms actually prevent conflict or improve long-run resilience. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Informal solidarity is a documented coping asset in some communities, but its peace and long-term resilience effects have not been independently evaluated.

pathways.climate_pressure: Prolonged drought in Namibe in the incident reported for August 2025.
pathways.documented_impact: Pressure around access to a water dam.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Contested dam access between two unnamed communities.
pathways.possible_consequence: The UN Secretary-General's report records violent clashes on 17 August 2025, a 12–20 fatality range and thousands displaced.
affected_groups: people displaced by the reported clash
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing access rules, local disputes, governance and social relations may also shape violence; the report does not isolate them.
pathways.uncertainty: One UN-reported historical episode. No named communities, independently identified climate effect, anthropogenic drought attribution or current violence map. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Equitable water access and dispute resolution are relevant responses, but their operation or effect is not documented for this incident.
pathways.compact_statement: The UN reports that contested dam access amid prolonged drought preceded a deadly intercommunal clash in Namibe in August 2025; it does not establish climate as the sole cause or a national violence trend.

pathways.climate_pressure: Hurricane Irma's 2017 impact on Barbuda.
pathways.documented_impact: Evacuation to Antigua and disruption of education, health and livelihoods for affected women and girls.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Post-disaster land redistribution decisions and women's participation in recovery governance can affect communal tenure and access to recovery resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: CEDAW warned in 2019 of possible loss of women's communal land rights; this is a concern/recommendation, not an adjudicated or verified later outcome.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing tenure systems, gender inequality and independent land-policy decisions also shape recovery rights.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical treaty-body risk assessment, not proof of dispossession, a causal violence estimate or present legal advice; no attribution of Irma itself to anthropogenic change. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: CEDAW recommended meaningful women's participation and equitable access to recovery resources; implementation/effectiveness was not established.
pathways.compact_statement: After Irma's Barbuda evacuation, CEDAW warned that recovery land decisions could undermine women's communal tenure without inclusive participation; the bank retains this as a historical governance risk, not a verified dispossession outcome.

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate stress and land degradation.
pathways.documented_impact: Potential decline in arable productivity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Existing land scarcity and intercommunal tensions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Land disputes may intensify.
alternative_explanations: Population pressure and conflict legacies also matter.
pathways.uncertainty: Prospective report mechanism; no causal estimate or current conflict forecast. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Lower productivity may intensify existing land-scarcity tensions.

pathways.climate_pressure: Climatic pressures.
pathways.documented_impact: Widening spatial disparities.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Existing northern insecurity.
pathways.possible_consequence: Additional displacement risk.
affected_groups: People exposed to insecurity in northern Benin
alternative_explanations: Insecurity and regional mobility have independent drivers.
pathways.uncertainty: Qualitative CCDR warning; Sahelian in-migration is not a Benin-only causal estimate. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate pressures may compound disparities, insecurity and displacement.

pathways.climate_pressure: Northern drought, dry spells and water scarcity described in the country context.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced crops and pasture can change the resources available to farming and pastoral livelihoods.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Altered transhumance and competition over scarce or degraded land and water interact with pre-existing farmer-herder tensions.
pathways.possible_consequence: The project document warns of heightened local tensions; it does not attribute particular incidents or armed-group activity to climate.
alternative_explanations: Land governance, mobility restrictions and insecurity can cause livelihood losses and tensions independently of climate.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional contextual mechanism combining FEWS NET and appraisal narrative; not a localized incident study, causal estimate or prediction. Named attack sites are not treated as climate-conflict cases. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Proposed participatory refugee/host support is a design response, not an evaluated peace outcome.
pathways.compact_statement: In northern Benin, climate-related resource stress may alter transhumance and compound farmer-herder tensions, mediated by land and mobility conditions.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat, and rainfall variability affecting rainfed production
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced crop and livestock productivity, water stress, food insecurity, and livelihood loss
pathways.fcv_mediator: High rainfed-agriculture dependence, poverty, weak market and input access, displacement, and insecurity
pathways.possible_consequence: Household distress, mobility, protection risks, and localized grievances may intensify where alternative livelihoods and assistance are inaccessible
alternative_explanations: Armed violence, inflation, market disruption, poverty, and policy choices can produce food insecurity and distress without a climate shock.
pathways.uncertainty: The interaction is well supported at national scale, but the relative contribution of climate pressures is not estimated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought, heat, and erratic rainfall can deepen livelihood and food-security stress where rainfed dependence, poverty, insecurity, and weak access limit alternatives.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, rainfall variability, and land degradation affecting pasture, water, and cropland
pathways.documented_impact: Changed resource availability and livelihood mobility among farmers and pastoralists
pathways.fcv_mediator: Overlapping land claims, weak resource governance, armed-group exploitation, and disrupted customary dispute resolution
pathways.possible_consequence: Farmer-herder disputes or political exploitation of local grievances may become more likely, but are not an automatic result of climate pressure
alternative_explanations: Agricultural expansion, herd growth, political exclusion, weapons, insurgency, and unresolved tenure disputes independently shape violence.
pathways.uncertainty: Available evidence supports conditional mechanisms rather than a Burkina Faso-wide causal effect. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related resource stress may aggravate farmer-herder disputes when land governance and dispute resolution are weak or grievances are exploited.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heavy rainfall and flooding in towns receiving conflict-displaced households
pathways.documented_impact: Damage to temporary shelters, asset loss, and repeated housing insecurity
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict displacement, scarce safer urban land, poverty, and limited municipal shelter capacity
pathways.possible_consequence: Repeated shelter loss and constrained access to safer land and services may deepen household insecurity and prolong displacement.
alternative_explanations: Housing exclusion, poverty, conflict displacement, and poor drainage can create the same shelter risks without climate change.
pathways.uncertainty: Direct flood exposure and shelter loss are documented at selected sites; repeated displacement is plausible, while local tension was not measured. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict displacement can place households on flood-prone land, where heavy rain compounds shelter loss and housing insecurity.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, flood, and food-system shocks requiring timely assistance and adaptation
pathways.documented_impact: Higher need for food, water, livelihood, and climate-risk services
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed insecurity, blocked transport, disrupted markets, weak services, and constrained humanitarian access
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate shocks may produce larger and more unequal losses because conflict limits early warning, farming, markets, assistance, and recovery
alternative_explanations: Chronic poverty, remoteness, underinvestment, and macroeconomic shocks can independently reduce response reach and worsen losses.
pathways.uncertainty: The sources establish access and performance constraints but do not quantify the additional climate loss attributable to conflict. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict and access constraints can magnify climate losses by restricting farming, markets, early warning, assistance, and recovery.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rainfall uncertainty affecting crop-calendar decisions and local preparedness
pathways.documented_impact: Risk of mistimed sowing, seed loss, and weak local climate information
pathways.fcv_mediator: Uneven last-mile services, institutional coordination, community liaison coverage, and insecurity-related access gaps
pathways.possible_consequence: Accessible climate information may protect livelihoods and reduce distress, while unequal coverage could leave high-risk communities behind
alternative_explanations: Input quality, soil conditions, market access, extension services, and insecurity also determine crop and livelihood outcomes.
pathways.uncertainty: Outputs and testimonials do not establish forecast accuracy, equitable uptake, yields, or conflict-sensitive coverage. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Last-mile hydrometeorological services may reduce livelihood losses when information is trusted, timely, and accessible in insecure areas.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heavy rain, landslides, flash floods and severe weather in Cox's Bazar.
pathways.documented_impact: Reported shelter and infrastructure damage and repeated displacement in refugee camps.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Forced-displacement settings combine crowded temporary hillside shelters, restricted mobility, degraded slopes and limited services.
pathways.possible_consequence: These conditions narrow safe evacuation and coping options and magnify weather-related losses; they do not establish climate-caused refugee-host violence.
geographies: Cox's Bazar camps and adjacent host communities
alternative_explanations: Site design, poverty, infrastructure and service gaps shape losses independently of the displacement history; individual contributions are not measured.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional reverse interaction grounded in camp context and dated July 2026 impacts, not a causal estimate or attribution of a weather event to climate change. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Reported warning/gauge capacity and planned inclusive training may support preparedness; performance and access were not independently evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: Displacement-related settlement and mobility constraints in Cox's Bazar magnify vulnerability to heavy rain, landslides and flooding, without implying climate-driven violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: May 2014 flooding and landslides; no event-specific anthropogenic attribution is asserted.
pathways.documented_impact: Water and slope movements displaced legacy mines/UXO into previously safe or suspected areas.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict-era contamination and uncertain marking/survey status made reconstruction and farm access unsafe until professional survey and clearance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Potential accidents and restrictions on essential-service reconstruction and agricultural recovery; later delay duration is not established.
alternative_explanations: Direct flood damage and general reconstruction capacity also affect recovery.
Potential contamination estimates require professional verification.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical source-stated interaction and planned safety restrictions, not a current contamination map, clearance instruction or causal estimate of recovery delay. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Professional mine-risk assessment, marking and clearance with coordinated recovery planning; reported response outputs are not proof that all land became safe.
pathways.compact_statement: Floods mobilized conflict-era mines/UXO, making recovery access contingent on professional survey and clearance in affected areas.

pathways.climate_pressure: 2024 flooding and associated livelihood disruption.
pathways.documented_impact: Affected households faced displacement, overcrowding and psychological distress.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Disrupted protection services and constrained survivor reporting can weaken safeguards.
pathways.possible_consequence: The rapid assessment anticipated possible increased GBV risk, not measured violence incidence.
geographies: flood-affected areas of Bosnia and Herzegovina
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing protection gaps, reporting access and household conditions affect risk independently.
Anticipation draws partly on other crises, not incident data from this event.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical anticipated risk, not verified harm, a current forecast or a nationally representative local assessment. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Accessible survivor-centred services, safe shelter and mobile support can address stated gaps; effects not evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: The 2024 flood assessment anticipated GBV risks through livelihood loss, crowding and disrupted protection services; no incidence increase was verified.

pathways.climate_pressure: 2024 wildfire hazard in the Chaco; ignition is not attributed here to climate change.
pathways.documented_impact: Fire threatens habitat used by Ayoreo people in voluntary isolation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Habitat destruction could force unwanted contact where territorial and non-contact safeguards are inadequate.
pathways.possible_consequence: Conditional exposure to violence and disease and threats to physical/cultural survival; no contact or violence event is asserted.
alternative_explanations: Land-use pressures and deforestation also affect habitat independently of climate.
Extent of damage in uncontacted territory was unknown to the mission.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated conditional protection mechanism, not a verified violence outcome, precise exposure map or anthropogenic attribution of the fires. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Territorial protection and fire prevention must respect peoples' right to remain in voluntary isolation; do not use this pathway to justify forced contact.
pathways.compact_statement: Wildfire habitat loss could force unwanted contact and heighten violence risk for isolated Ayoreo; REDESCA does not report that this occurred.

pathways.climate_pressure: The 2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods.
pathways.documented_impact: Displacement into emergency shelters.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Inadequate shelter divisions, privacy and security, as described by the rights mission.
pathways.possible_consequence: Reports of sexual and gender-based violence in shelters, including Porto Alegre; not a measured population-wide increase.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing gender inequality and violence, shelter arrangements and reporting access also affect harm and recorded cases.
pathways.uncertainty: Mission-reported cases and risk mechanisms, not prevalence, a counterfactual causal estimate or anthropogenic event attribution. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The mission recommended protection protocols and documented women-and-children-only shelters; coverage and effectiveness were not evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: Flood displacement into inadequately protected shelters was associated with reported sexual and gender-based violence in the 2024 response.

pathways.climate_pressure: Amazon drought and low river levels.
pathways.documented_impact: River-dependent communities face isolation and reduced access to services and assistance.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed-group resource exploitation, recruitment and forced displacement compound access restrictions in drought-affected areas.
pathways.possible_consequence: Greater difficulty reaching already isolated communities and heightened protection needs.
alternative_explanations: Remoteness, transport infrastructure, service coverage and enforcement limitations also shape access.
pathways.uncertainty: ACAPS secondary qualitative synthesis; armed-group citations were not independently rechecked. No claim that drought created armed groups or that a quantified interaction effect was estimated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Reported food, water and medical distribution offers a response channel; effectiveness and safe coverage were not evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: ACAPS describes insecurity compounding drought-related isolation and humanitarian access constraints, not drought causing armed conflict.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rising heat, rainfall variability and episodic drought/heavy rainfall.
pathways.documented_impact: Agricultural production and food availability are sensitive to rainfall and climate shocks.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict, displacement, degraded roads, prices and weak purchasing power shape whether production changes translate into household food access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate-related production losses could worsen acute food insecurity where conflict and market-access constraints limit coping.
geographies: drought concern greater in northern CAR
pathways.uncertainty: IPC does not quantify a separate climate causal effect; future drought direction is uncertain. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate shocks can affect food production, but whether this produces severe food insecurity in CAR is strongly mediated by conflict, markets, roads, poverty and assistance. (IPCinfo)

pathways.climate_pressure: Rainfall variability, drought and pasture/water pressures in CAR and surrounding regions.
pathways.documented_impact: Changes in timing or geography of pastoral movements.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak cross-border regulation, land/water access rules, armed-group involvement and local dispute-management capacity.
pathways.possible_consequence: Altered livestock movement may increase the likelihood of localized farmer-herder tensions where regulation and negotiated access are weak.
affected_groups: sedentary farmers and communities along corridors
pathways.uncertainty: NUPI explicitly identifies a lack of robust CAR-specific climate-security monitoring. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: compensation arrangements and functioning local mediation
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related mobility pressure can matter, but governance of routes and resources - and armed insecurity - determines whether mobility becomes cooperative, disruptive or violent. (NUPI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, rainfall variability and seasonal pasture/water stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Pastoralists require mobility and negotiated resource access.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed violence and state withdrawal can remove route controls, compensation procedures and dispute-resolution mechanisms.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate and seasonal resource stress may become harder to manage peacefully when conflict erodes institutions that previously organized mobility.
pathways.uncertainty: Practitioner evidence is not a nationally representative causal study. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict can reduce the institutional capacity needed to manage ordinary and climate-amplified pastoral resource pressures. (NUPI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Rainfall variability and production shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: Agricultural output and food availability vary with rainfall and other shocks.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Persistent conflict, displacement and degraded roads restrict market and humanitarian access; high prices and low purchasing power further constrain households.
pathways.possible_consequence: A localized climate-related production shock could have larger food-security effects where conflict has already impaired transport and markets.
alternative_explanations: assistance coverage and local harvest conditions
pathways.uncertainty: Relative contributions of climate, conflict and market variables are not causally decomposed. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict-damaged access and weak purchasing power can magnify the household consequences of climate-sensitive food-production changes. (IPCinfo)

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat, rainfall variability, floods and drought.
pathways.documented_impact: Effective adaptation requires observations, risk analysis and water/hydrometeorological information.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak institutions, limited staff/equipment, fragmented planning and broader fragility constrain data generation and use.
pathways.possible_consequence: Poor climate information can reduce the timeliness and targeting of adaptation and disaster-management decisions.
alternative_explanations: Fiscal scarcity and technical constraints may exist independently of armed conflict
pathways.uncertainty: Reviewed documents do not estimate the share of climate-information deficits caused specifically by FCV. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Fragile institutional capacity constrains the information systems required to anticipate and manage climate risks, although the specific contribution of conflict is not quantified. (UNFCCC)

pathways.climate_pressure: Seasonal variability in pasture, water and agricultural resources.
pathways.documented_impact: Pastoral mobility creates recurring needs for negotiated access to land and water.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Local agreements, compensation, regulated routes and farmer-pastoralist exchange can reduce disputes.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where legitimate local governance functions, resource variability may be managed through negotiation rather than escalation.
alternative_explanations: Economic complementarity between livestock and crop systems
pathways.uncertainty: No experimental or quasi-experimental evaluation was identified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: reciprocal agricultural-pastoral exchange and local dispute resolution
pathways.compact_statement: CAR evidence contains not only risk pathways but also peace-supporting institutions that can mediate resource variability without violence. (ICRC)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought.
pathways.documented_impact: Changed pastoral movement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Farmer-herder competition over land and water.
pathways.possible_consequence: Potential community tensions.
alternative_explanations: Historical tensions and resource governance also matter.
pathways.uncertainty: Prospective qualitative mechanism; no measured recruitment or causal conflict effect. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought-related mobility may increase resource competition and tensions.

pathways.climate_pressure: Long dry seasons and rainfall disruption described in the Bafing proposal.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced pasture and water concentrate herds and farm plots near residual resources, increasing crop damage risk.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Transhumance, overlapping land/water use, corridor encroachment and weak pastoral infrastructure shape resource competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: The proposal describes recurrent farmer-herder tensions and crop/livestock damage across Koro, Touba and Ouaninou, with social-cohesion consequences.
alternative_explanations: Land-use expansion, corridor access, herd management, tenure and cross-border insecurity can cause tensions independently of climatic change.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated proposal/context mechanism using local studies and consultation; no representative incident sample or separate climate causal estimate. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Planned pastoral water/fodder areas and conflict-management support are proposed responses, not evaluated outcomes.
pathways.compact_statement: In Bafing, seasonal resource scarcity intersects with transhumance, overlapping land use and crop damage to compound farmer-herder tensions.

pathways.climate_pressure: Erratic rainfall, drought periods and flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Reported reductions/disruptions in pasture, livestock water, crops and fishing/farming livelihoods.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competition over water, channels, grazing areas and crops, interacting with local resource-sharing rules.
pathways.possible_consequence: Under adverse governance and security conditions, these pressures may contribute to intercommunal clashes and displacement.
pathways.uncertainty: Interview-based evidence cannot estimate the climate contribution to violence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related livelihood stress may aggravate already-governed resource disputes; it is not demonstrated as a sufficient cause of violence. (Refugees International)

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate shocks affect already vulnerable livelihood systems.
pathways.documented_impact: Acute food insecurity and constrained household coping.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict displacement, loss/restriction of land and livelihood access, concentration of needs.
pathways.possible_consequence: Displaced and host households may become less able to absorb subsequent climate or price shocks.
geographies: Far North and other crisis regions
pathways.uncertainty: No reviewed study decomposes the relative climate/conflict contributions. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: accessible markets and conflict-sensitive resource access
pathways.compact_statement: Climate shocks occur inside a conflict-displacement system that can weaken coping, rather than independently producing acute hunger. (UNHCR Data Portal)

pathways.climate_pressure: Unreliable rainfall and dry spells.
pathways.documented_impact: Poorer pasture and longer livestock movements.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Crop/grazing encroachment, livestock density, crop damage and land-tenure pressures.
pathways.possible_consequence: These interacting pressures may aggravate farmer-pastoralist conflict.
pathways.uncertainty: No national extrapolation is justified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: In Kilum-Ijim, climate variability interacts with herd pressure and land governance rather than operating as a stand-alone conflict driver. (Frontiers)

pathways.climate_pressure: Urban flood and other hazard exposure.
pathways.documented_impact: Need for resilient urban infrastructure and services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Security problems restricted implementation and caused reductions in project scope.
pathways.possible_consequence: Conflict may leave some exposed urban communities with delayed or incomplete resilience investments.
geographies: Particularly Far North and NW/SW project locations
alternative_explanations: counterpart funding and staffing also constrained implementation
pathways.uncertainty: Project experience cannot be generalized to every municipality. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: municipal capacity support and conflict-sensitive delivery
pathways.compact_statement: Recent project evidence directly shows insecurity delaying or narrowing resilience investment. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Multi-hazard exposure requiring coordinated adaptation.
pathways.documented_impact: Climate policies require sectoral/local implementation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Institutional fragmentation, limited decentralization capacity, fiscal constraints and weak data systems.
pathways.possible_consequence: Adaptation may be slower, less spatially targeted or less sustainable.
affected_groups: Especially populations dependent on weak local service systems
sectors: Cross-sectoral climate policy and public services
systems_assets_resources: Cross-sectoral climate policy and public services
alternative_explanations: normal administrative complexity and project design
pathways.uncertainty: No reviewed nationwide study estimates adaptation losses attributable to governance fragmentation. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Cameroon has an increasingly articulated climate architecture, but implementation bottlenecks may weaken conversion of policy into local resilience. (UNFCCC)

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate shocks are one contributor to humanitarian needs.
pathways.documented_impact: Severe food insecurity in conflict-affected regions.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Displacement and insecurity elevate needs while donor shortages reduce delivery.
pathways.possible_consequence: Reduced aid coverage could increase harmful coping or deepen vulnerability to subsequent shocks.
pathways.uncertainty: Downstream conflict/stability effects have not been evaluated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Reliable multi-year humanitarian finance and livelihood-support transitions
pathways.compact_statement: Assistance capacity is itself a mediator of whether multi-causal shocks become deeper household crises. (World Food Programme)

pathways.climate_pressure: Natural-resource stress may intensify livelihood-management challenges.
pathways.documented_impact: Water/pasture access can be a focus of community disputes.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Quality of dialogue, dispute management and inclusive resource rules.
pathways.possible_consequence: Stronger local institutions may reduce escalation even under resource stress.
alternative_explanations: Wider security trends and other interventions may explain perceived conflict reductions
pathways.uncertainty: No independent counterfactual evaluation of peace outcomes. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Evidence suggests local resource institutions can be peace-supporting, but the measured magnitude of their effect remains uncertain. (MPTF Gateway)

pathways.climate_pressure: Participant households face climate and non-climate shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: AEP-Youth improved measured food security but did not improve measured shock-recovery ability.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict/insecurity was explicitly included among non-climate shocks in the evaluation framework.
pathways.possible_consequence: Economic or food-security improvements should not automatically be interpreted as climate/FCV resilience.
alternative_explanations: Differential shock exposure among participants and comparison households
pathways.uncertainty: Programme geography excludes major Far North and East crisis contexts. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Targeted programming that explicitly measures recovery
pathways.compact_statement: Measurable livelihood gains did not automatically produce measurable shock resilience. (IFAD) ---

pathways.climate_pressure: Rising heat, changing rainfall, drought/flood episodes.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced or disrupted agricultural production and climate-sensitive livelihood stress.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Existing land disputes, unequal access, weak resource governance and lack of alternative livelihoods.
pathways.possible_consequence: Livelihood pressure may intensify existing disputes or grievances over land and water in parts of eastern DRC.
alternative_explanations: demographic pressure and market conditions independently generate conflict
pathways.uncertainty: SIPRI explicitly states that specific livelihood-to-conflict mechanisms remain less clear than the climate-to-livelihood link. (SIPRI2) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: extension services and inclusive resource planning
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related livelihood stress may increase pressure on already contested land and water, but political and governance conditions determine whether tension escalates.

pathways.climate_pressure: Recurring drought, rainfall variability and declining pasture/water availability.
pathways.documented_impact: Altered livestock mobility and competition for water/pasture.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Pre-existing farmer-pastoralist disputes, identity conflict and land-access arrangements.
pathways.possible_consequence: Greater tension, livestock theft or violence has been reported locally where altered movement intersects with existing disputes.
pathways.uncertainty: Local, largely qualitative evidence; it must not be generalized across South Kivu or nationally. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: participatory land/water governance and agro-pastoral cooperation
pathways.compact_statement: In the Ruzizi Plain, climate-sensitive changes in pasture and livestock movement appear to interact with - not originate independently from - existing farmer-pastoralist conflict.

pathways.climate_pressure: Extreme rainfall, floods and rainfall-triggered landslides.
pathways.documented_impact: Housing/livelihood loss and displacement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Overcrowded sites, inadequate basic services, resource scarcity and weak post-disaster recovery.
pathways.possible_consequence: Displacement may create or intensify localized tensions between displaced and host communities where services/resources are already scarce.
alternative_explanations: Conflict displacement is far larger in many eastern areas and may independently overwhelm services
poor planning and infrastructure condition flood losses
pathways.uncertainty: Disaster-displacement figures should not automatically be interpreted as anthropogenic-climate displacement. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Flood displacement can add pressure to fragile local service/resource systems, potentially worsening grievances where recovery is weak.

pathways.climate_pressure: Future drought, flood, heat or rainfall shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: Households require access to farmland, markets, services and humanitarian support to cope.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed-group control, insecurity, road blockage, displacement and restricted territorial access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Communities exposed to conflict may experience greater livelihood loss, food insecurity and slower recovery when climate shocks occur.
geographies: North/South Kivu and other conflict-affected eastern provinces
institutions: local authorities and armed actors controlling access
alternative_explanations: infrastructure deficits and commodity-price shocks can also reduce coping capacity outside active conflict
pathways.uncertainty: Effects on quantified adaptation outcomes have rarely been evaluated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: conflict-sensitive adaptation and locally trusted delivery channels
pathways.compact_statement: Insecurity can convert otherwise manageable climate shocks into deeper crises by removing access to land, markets, services and recovery assistance. (SIPRI2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate mitigation/adaptation requires functioning forest, land and ecosystem governance.
pathways.documented_impact: Armed actors and political-economic networks exploit forests/minerals and damage environmental governance.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict financing, corruption, weak state authority and elite competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: FCV-linked extraction may compound already uneven local forest-management implementation and weaken institutions needed for mitigation and adaptation.
alternative_explanations: regulatory design and global commodity demand also drive environmental loss
pathways.uncertainty: FCV-linked extraction, climate/forest-policy institutions and uneven local implementation are separately documented; retained evidence does not estimate the causal effect of extraction on mitigation or adaptation performance. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: forest monitoring and conflict-sensitive natural-resource governance
pathways.compact_statement: FCV-linked extraction can undermine institutions needed for climate mitigation and adaptation, while remaining an independent environmental and political-economy driver. (NUPI3)

pathways.climate_pressure: Extreme rainfall and flood hazard.
pathways.documented_impact: Damage to roads, water, electricity, housing and agricultural assets.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Poverty, informal settlement, weak drainage/DRM capacity, fiscal limitations and weak coordination.
pathways.possible_consequence: Repeated losses could deepen service deficits, recovery burdens and public grievances; violence is not demonstrated by the evidence reviewed.
pathways.uncertainty: No source reviewed demonstrates that urban floods cause violence or conflict. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Flood losses place additional pressure on weak urban service systems, but any transition from service stress to FCV outcomes remains unproven. (World Bank5)

pathways.climate_pressure: Multi-hazard climate exposure requiring sustained adaptation investment.
pathways.documented_impact: Large planned adaptation requirements and implementation needs.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Fiscal pressure, weak coordination, governance limitations and - where relevant - conflict-related access constraints.
pathways.possible_consequence: Delayed, incomplete or unsustained adaptation may leave households and infrastructure exposed to future shocks.
alternative_explanations: COVID-19 and maintenance failures independently affect performance
pathways.uncertainty: National adaptation effectiveness has not been comprehensively evaluated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: predictable financing and locally owned implementation
pathways.compact_statement: Policy ambition exceeds demonstrated delivery capacity, leaving a gap between adaptation plans and sustained resilience outcomes. (IMF7)

pathways.climate_pressure: Livelihood and environmental stresses.
pathways.documented_impact: Communities face livelihood, displacement and resource-management challenges.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Social cohesion, inclusion, local legitimacy and collective action.
pathways.possible_consequence: Well-supported women-, youth- and community-led initiatives could reduce vulnerability and strengthen peaceful problem-solving, although programme-level effects on violence are not established.
alternative_explanations: Community organizations may have limited resources
pathways.uncertainty: No reviewed evaluation measures whether these initiatives reduce conflict incidence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: agro-pastoral cooperatives and inclusive customary/local governance
pathways.compact_statement: Local social institutions provide credible resilience and peace-supporting capacity, but their impact has not been rigorously quantified. (SIPRI2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Dry conditions during the 2023–2024 El Niño cycle.
pathways.documented_impact: Conditions more favorable for clearing forest in the Colombian Amazon.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Existing dissident factions regulate and profit from land transactions, deforestation and cattle economies, amid shifting negotiations and state control.
pathways.possible_consequence: Armed actors can exploit dry conditions for revenue and bargaining leverage, as described by the study; no quantified increase in violence is established.
alternative_explanations: Political negotiations, group fragmentation, commodity incentives, land speculation and enforcement changes also influence behavior.
pathways.uncertainty: Qualitative subregional study using El Niño as a proxy; not attribution of the event to anthropogenic warming or causal identification of armed-group behavior. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Community water conservation and restoration offer coping channels but need resources and safe institutional access.
pathways.compact_statement: The Guaviare study describes existing dissidents exploiting El Niño dryness for deforestation revenue and negotiating leverage, not climate causing an insurgency.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and environmental degradation in the Guaviare case-study area.
pathways.documented_impact: Communities require water conservation, restoration and environmental response.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed-group territorial control and insecurity limit state access and environmental operations.
pathways.possible_consequence: Environmental enforcement and reforestation responses are constrained, weakening support for longer-term resilience.
alternative_explanations: Agency budgets, technical capacity, weak state presence and resource shortages also limit response.
pathways.uncertainty: Subregional participant accounts, not a national estimate of conflict blocking all adaptation or a measured resilience effect. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Community wells, Indigenous medicinal gardens and local restoration are documented coping efforts; outcomes were not evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: Insecurity and territorial control restrict environmental response and reforestation in the Guaviare study area, not all Colombian adaptation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and water stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced water availability.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Constraints on water access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Possible water-access conflict and displacement.
alternative_explanations: Water governance and infrastructure can affect access independently.
pathways.uncertainty: NDC risk table, not observed conflict attribution; project-area verification required. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Water stress may contribute to access disputes and displacement.

pathways.climate_pressure: Hurricane Maria's 2017 destructive wind and rain.
pathways.documented_impact: Severe post-disaster disruption of livelihoods and basic services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Extreme social conditions and inadequate protection of property during recovery.
pathways.possible_consequence: Government strategy reports episodes of looting/unrest and business recovery delays; not sustained armed conflict.
alternative_explanations: Response logistics, data gaps, institutional capacity and pre-existing vulnerability also affected recovery.
pathways.uncertainty: Single historical government's account, not measured causal attribution, anthropogenic event attribution or a current FCV classification. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Preparedness, targeted support and accountable recovery institutions are relevant capacities; coercive responses are not endorsed as proven resilience measures.
pathways.compact_statement: The government reports limited looting/unrest after Maria amid severe disruption, with property-protection gaps complicating recovery.

pathways.climate_pressure: Scenario-dependent climate and livelihood pressures through 2050 and 2100.
pathways.documented_impact: Modeled internal and Haiti-origin migration into urban, farming and border areas.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Under-served border infrastructure and unequal access to limited resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: Possible host–migrant tensions, not observed violence or a claim that migrants inherently create insecurity.
alternative_explanations: Border policies, Haiti's political-economic conditions, labor demand and social networks alter migration and integration.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional modeled pathway, not an observed 2026 forecast or causal violence estimate; border-policy assumptions may not hold. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The report recognizes safe, dignified migration as adaptation and recommends inclusive service planning.
pathways.compact_statement: Projected mobility may expose gaps in border services and resource access; tension is conditional, not a migrant threat attribution.

pathways.climate_pressure: Recurrent climate disasters damaging infrastructure and safe-water access.
pathways.documented_impact: Assistance needs overlap with violence-related service deprivation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed actors, insecurity and mobility restrictions constrain assessment, monitoring and sustained humanitarian operations.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate-disaster assistance may be harder to sustain within the constrained multisector response.
alternative_explanations: Road damage, isolation, institutional capacity and response resources also constrain access.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional synthesis of an official summary; no named climate-adaptation project suspension or measured climate-response effect is demonstrated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Existing humanitarian capacity is acknowledged, but the source judges it insufficient for needs.
pathways.compact_statement: Insecurity constrains multisector response where climate disasters add needs; climate-specific operational effects remain an inference.

pathways.climate_pressure: Seasonal water and pasture dependence in a dryland livestock system.
pathways.documented_impact: War left Tekezze–Setit watering areas inaccessible and concentrated herds around Goluj and reintegration sites.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict-related loss of transhumance/watering access and concentrated use of wells and cropland.
pathways.possible_consequence: Narrower seasonal coping options and localized livestock–farmer tensions were reported.
alternative_explanations: Borehole siting, herd numbers, settlement patterns and crop-residue management also shaped pressure.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical dryland coping mechanism from 1999–2001 research, not measured climate-change impact, current violence or an evaluated adaptation project. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Maintaining equitable water access and mobility options is relevant, without attributing pressures solely to displaced/returning people.
pathways.compact_statement: Near Goluj, border-war restrictions narrowed seasonal livestock water access and concentrated local resource pressures; findings are historical and exceptional.

pathways.climate_pressure: Extreme heat.
pathways.documented_impact: Higher heat exposure is associated with more food-insecure households.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Household food insecurity and livelihood stress.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where other political, economic and security conditions are adverse, food insecurity may contribute to greater conflict risk.
pathways.uncertainty: Causal direction and omitted-variable effects remain material. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Extreme heat may raise conflict risk through food insecurity, but available Ethiopia evidence is correlational rather than proof that heat causes conflict. (World Food Programme1)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and poor pasture/water availability.
pathways.documented_impact: Pastoralists adjust mobility and other coping strategies.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competition over common water and pasture.
pathways.possible_consequence: Increased probability of local intercommunal tension or conflict in some Somali Region settings.
pathways.uncertainty: Strongly location-dependent. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
