pathways.compact_statement: Drought can affect local conflict risk through mobility and governed access to pasture/water; it is not an automatic conflict trigger. (SIPRI7)

pathways.climate_pressure: Heavy rainfall and flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Infrastructure, crops, livelihoods and settlements are exposed to flood damage.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Displacement, service congestion, lost assets and unequal recovery.
pathways.possible_consequence: In fragile or poorly governed settings, these stresses could exacerbate grievances or reduce social cohesion.
pathways.uncertainty: No verified source here demonstrates a national flood -> violence causal effect. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Flood impacts may interact with displacement and service deficits, but a conflict consequence remains inferential. (World Bank2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Any concurrent drought/heat/flood shock.
pathways.documented_impact: Conflict exposure is associated with materially higher food poverty in surveyed pastoral/agropastoral communities.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Violence, market disruption and household asset/income loss.
pathways.possible_consequence: Households affected by conflict may have fewer resources with which to cope with subsequent climate shocks.
pathways.uncertainty: Direct effect on specific adaptation outcomes was not measured. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict-associated food poverty plausibly reduces household climate-coping capacity, but the complete adaptation chain has not been directly evaluated. (World Bank2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Heavy-rain and flood exposure affecting humanitarian needs and delivery contexts.
pathways.documented_impact: Insecurity creates risks and raises WFP operating costs.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Access restrictions, insecurity and increased delivery costs.
pathways.possible_consequence: Assistance, recovery and resilience services may reach fewer people, arrive later or cost more.
geographies: Particularly Amhara in current WFP reporting
pathways.uncertainty: Flood risk and insecurity-related delivery costs are separately documented; their joint effect is not estimated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Flood exposure and insecurity-related operating constraints are separately documented; their joint effect on humanitarian or resilience outcomes is not quantified. (World Food Programme8)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and seasonal water/pasture scarcity.
pathways.documented_impact: Pastoral dry-season grazing and water access are important to livelihood continuity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unrecognized communal tenure, expropriation/displacement risk and contested access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Poorly governed land change may heighten livelihood vulnerability and potentially aggravate local fragility.
institutions: Formal land administration and customary institutions
pathways.uncertainty: National incidence is not quantified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Recognition of communal rights and locally grounded customary governance
pathways.compact_statement: Institutions governing land and seasonal access can mediate whether climate stress becomes a livelihood or fragility problem. (World Bank2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought.
pathways.documented_impact: Drought insurance/cash can help households maintain livestock or meet needs.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Reduced need for drought-driven mobility and competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: Intercommunal conflict risk may fall where mobility-related resource competition is a relevant conflict mechanism.
pathways.uncertainty: Severe drought still generated migration; peace effect not rigorously estimated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Insurance has a plausible peace-supporting pathway, but evidence is mixed and programme targeting can generate its own tensions. (SIPRI7)

pathways.climate_pressure: Coastal flooding/erosion and climate-related pressure to consider relocation.
pathways.documented_impact: Relocation decisions can separate households from valued land, livelihoods and community arrangements.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Incomplete consensus, insecure tenure and pre-existing mistrust in government or policing can shape the process.
pathways.possible_consequence: The practice paper warns of possible cohesion loss or disputes if relocation proceeds without adequate consensus; this is not measured conflict incidence.
alternative_explanations: Housing policy, development-led relocation, service inequality, policing and generational preferences may drive disputes independently of climate.
pathways.uncertainty: Prospective source-stated mechanism with qualitative local examples; no causal estimate or current legal interpretation. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Trusted mediation and inclusive consensus-building are proposed safeguards; their effects are not independently evaluated here.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related relocation may interact with tenure, consent and trust to create disputes; Fiji evidence supports a conditional risk mechanism, not climate-caused violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and climate-related disasters that reduce nearby water/fuel availability.
pathways.documented_impact: Longer collection journeys and greater unpaid care demands for rural women and girls.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Gendered allocation of domestic work, poverty and unequal access to assets/protection constrain safe alternatives.
pathways.possible_consequence: The CCDR describes heightened harassment/sexual-assault exposure and lost educational/economic opportunities; no estimated climate-attributable incidence.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing gender inequality, poverty, protection-service availability and violence independently affect safety.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional mechanism in 2025 CCDR synthesis, not event-level attribution, a village-specific finding or a measured rise in violence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The report recommends gender-responsive disaster planning and locally inclusive institutions; effectiveness remains unevaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: The Gabon CCDR describes how drought/disaster-related collection burdens can expose rural women and girls to protection risks through gendered work and constrained safe alternatives; this is a conditional mechanism, not an incidence estimate.

pathways.climate_pressure: Flooding, drought and geological hazards in the source's regional climate-risk assessment.
pathways.documented_impact: Climate impacts threaten displaced households' safety and economic stability.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Protracted conflict-related displacement, inadequate housing and limited services and livelihood opportunities increase vulnerability.
pathways.possible_consequence: Displaced households may sustain greater hazard-related harm and livelihood disruption; no new violent conflict is inferred.
alternative_explanations: Poverty, building quality and hazard exposure also shape losses independently of displacement.
Regional synthesis is not a matched local comparison.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated vulnerability mechanism, not causal identification; do not assign uniform exposure to all IDPs or named conflict territories. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Adequate housing, accessible basic services and livelihood support can reduce the stated vulnerability; effectiveness is not evaluated here.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict-related displacement and inadequate housing/services can magnify climate-hazard vulnerability in Georgia; no climate-caused conflict claim.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Unreliable northern food systems.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Migration and land/water competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: Potential conflict risk.
affected_groups: People dependent on northern food systems
alternative_explanations: Mobility and resource disputes can have non-climatic drivers.
pathways.uncertainty: Policy-brief risk through 2080; scenario unspecified and no causal conflict estimate. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Northern livelihood pressures may contribute to mobility and resource tensions.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat stress and changing availability of water and fodder.
pathways.documented_impact: Reported changes in herding/feeding practices can lead to crop damage or contested tree use.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Land/tree tenure rules, resource allocation, politicized identities and limited trust/enforcement in dispute institutions.
pathways.possible_consequence: The Gushegu account describes verbal disputes and warns of escalation; climate is an exacerbating factor, not the primary or sufficient cause.
alternative_explanations: Political mobilization, land acquisition, population pressure, crop damage, stigmatization and weak dispute mechanisms independently shape tensions.
pathways.uncertainty: A 2022 case-based brief and interviews, not a climate-attributable conflict estimate or current incident map. Ethnic identity is not treated as a propensity for violence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Inclusive, trusted dispute resolution is relevant; committee existence alone is not evidence of enforceable or fair outcomes.
pathways.compact_statement: In Gushegu, reported heat-related herding adjustments can encounter crop/tree-tenure disputes within a politically mediated conflict setting; no independent climate effect is estimated.

pathways.climate_pressure: Agricultural climate shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: Hunger and resource scarcity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak tenure, dispute resolution and local capacity.
pathways.possible_consequence: Heightened resource-conflict risk.
affected_groups: People dependent on agriculture and natural resources
pathways.uncertainty: Report-level risk statement, not quantified conflict attribution. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate livelihood shocks may compound weak land governance and conflict risk.

pathways.climate_pressure: Coastal flooding, salinity and source-described sea-level pressure around Djobel.
pathways.documented_impact: Damage to rice-field/dike systems and pressure to establish safer settlement space.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Longstanding contested upland access, unresolved resource rights, limited support and labour constraints.
pathways.possible_consequence: The case documents obstacles to safer settlement/adaptation and renewed land tensions; it does not isolate climate change as the origin of the dispute.
alternative_explanations: Longstanding territorial history, state action, resource rights, livelihood dependence and external assistance also shape adaptation and tensions.
pathways.uncertainty: Localized historical qualitative evidence; no attribution of the 2017 flood to anthropogenic change, quantified violence trend, or present land adjudication. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Equitable negotiated access, dike maintenance and appropriate technical support are relevant capacities; effectiveness is not established.
pathways.compact_statement: In Djobel, flood exposure and pressure to retreat interact with an older upland land dispute that constrains safer settlement; the case is local and multi-causal.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and erratic rainfall affecting rural livelihoods.
pathways.documented_impact: WFP reports historical agricultural and household-income damage in 2024.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal access to basic services, violence, displacement and limited coping/implementation capacity can compound livelihood stress.
pathways.possible_consequence: Further food/water insecurity, migration, displacement and land tensions are conditional risks, not attributed observed conflict effects.
alternative_explanations: Violence, inequality, limited services and economic opportunity independently influence migration and food insecurity.
Tenure disputes and institutional weaknesses are not caused solely by weather.
pathways.uncertainty: Coordinator synthesis combining a historical impact account and a qualitative CCDR warning. No local causal test, quantified probability or event attribution; mechanisms require project-area verification. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: CCDR-recommended tenure security, livelihood diversification and locally led resilient investment.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related livelihood loss may compound existing exclusion and institutional constraints, increasing displacement or land-tension risks; the evidence does not establish climate-caused violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rainfall deficits and associated livelihood stress.
pathways.documented_impact: The 2012–2019 departmental study finds higher subsequent US family-unit apprehensions associated with rainfall shortfalls.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Higher homicide rates strengthen the observed relationship; the authors interpret unsafe internal alternatives as a possible mobility constraint.
pathways.possible_consequence: Cross-border movement may reflect intertwined livelihood and safety concerns; the study does not establish that drought causes violence or individual migration.
alternative_explanations: Wealth, networks, enforcement/apprehension patterns, poverty, governance and household preferences influence migration.
pathways.uncertainty: Observational aggregate models using department of birth, not necessarily pre-departure residence; author interpretation is not a directly tested household mediation chain. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The authors propose farmer participation and agricultural resilience alongside governance/security measures; effects are not evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: Honduras evidence finds a stronger rainfall-deficit/migration association in higher-violence departments; the proposed safety constraint is interpretive, not causal proof.

pathways.climate_pressure: Tropical cyclones, heavy rainfall, flooding, and coastal pressures affecting dense settlements and infrastructure
pathways.documented_impact: Damage to homes, roads, health facilities, crops, water systems, and local livelihoods
pathways.fcv_mediator: Poverty, deforestation, unsafe urbanization, weak services, limited municipal resources, and low institutional legitimacy
pathways.possible_consequence: Displacement, unequal recovery, livelihood loss, and perceived exclusion may deepen social tension, but violence is not an automatic climate outcome
alternative_explanations: Political instability, armed violence, poor land-use planning, chronic poverty, and infrastructure underinvestment can independently produce displacement and grievance.
pathways.uncertainty: Hazard and vulnerability are documented, but no admitted source estimates a climate effect on social tension or conflict. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Cyclone and flood losses may deepen displacement and exclusion where poverty, unsafe settlement, and weak local delivery constrain recovery.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat, rainfall variability, flooding, and soil and water stress affecting rainfed agriculture
pathways.documented_impact: Lower or less reliable production, livestock and water stress, food insecurity, and livelihood loss
pathways.fcv_mediator: Rainfed dependence, market disruption, poverty, insecurity, weak safety nets, and armed-group control of transport and commerce
pathways.possible_consequence: Distress, indebtedness, migration, or political grievance may increase when households lack viable alternatives; a recruitment effect is not established.
alternative_explanations: Inflation, trade and market disruption, violence, policy choices, land degradation, and chronic poverty independently affect food security and mobility.
pathways.uncertainty: The sources establish interacting livelihood pressures but do not estimate the relative climate contribution or causal effects on migration, grievance, or recruitment. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress can worsen food and livelihood insecurity where rainfed dependence, market disruption, poverty, and violence restrict alternatives.

pathways.climate_pressure: Flood, cyclone, heat, and disease risks requiring functioning water, health, transport, and humanitarian systems
pathways.documented_impact: Higher demand for safe water, medical care, emergency transport, supplies, and public information
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed-group control, violence, blocked supply chains, facility damage, fuel shortages, staff insecurity, and constrained humanitarian access
pathways.possible_consequence: Weather and health shocks may cause larger and more unequal losses because conflict disables preparedness, access, response, and recovery
institutions: International Committee of the Red Cross
alternative_explanations: Chronic underinvestment, workforce shortages, poverty, and weak maintenance can disrupt health and water systems without armed violence.
pathways.uncertainty: Service disruption is directly documented, but its additional effect during a defined climate event is not quantified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Armed violence can magnify climate and health losses by disabling water, health, transport, and humanitarian delivery systems.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heavy rainfall, flooding, heat, and disease exposure in displacement sites and overstretched host communities
pathways.documented_impact: Overcrowding, inadequate shelter, unsafe water and sanitation, and pressure on health and other basic services
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict displacement, site location, armed-group control, poverty, gendered protection risks, and weak local services
pathways.possible_consequence: Displaced and host households may face repeated displacement, disease, deeper deprivation, or local tension when hazards strike already overloaded settings
alternative_explanations: Housing shortages, land-use failure, poverty, and weak WASH services can create similar site risks independently of climate change.
pathways.uncertainty: Displacement and poor site conditions are documented, while added flood or heat effects, repeated displacement and local tension remain conditional and unquantified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Violence-driven displacement can place households in overcrowded, poorly serviced settings where flood, heat, and disease risks may compound insecurity.

pathways.climate_pressure: Cyclones, floods, and other hydroclimatic emergencies requiring coordinated local preparedness and response
pathways.documented_impact: Demand for warnings, evacuation, shelters, damage assessment, road access, and rapid assistance
pathways.fcv_mediator: Uneven municipal capability, limited finance, weak coordination and legitimacy, insecurity, and damaged transport links
pathways.possible_consequence: Capable and accountable local systems can reduce unequal losses, while weak or inaccessible systems can deepen exclusion and delayed recovery
institutions: Ministry of Public Works, Transport and Communication
alternative_explanations: Hazard magnitude, remoteness, transport quality, national political decisions, and external financing also determine response performance.
pathways.uncertainty: Reported capacity gains are not independently evaluated and earthquake response cannot be interpreted as climate-response effectiveness. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Municipal civil-protection and transport capacity mediate whether emergencies lead to timely, inclusive response or delayed and unequal recovery.

pathways.climate_pressure: Overlapping climate, food, displacement, and violence pressures affecting young people and livelihood systems
pathways.documented_impact: Eroded livelihoods, reduced coping options, displacement, and greater need for social and economic reintegration
pathways.fcv_mediator: Poverty, coercive recruitment, exclusion, weak legitimacy, limited livelihood alternatives, and fragmented climate-security coordination
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate-resilient livelihood and dialogue initiatives may support reintegration and reduce vulnerability, but peace effects remain unmeasured
alternative_explanations: Recruitment and violence are principally shaped by armed-group coercion, political economy, security conditions, exclusion, and criminal incentives.
pathways.uncertainty: The admitted evidence supports a policy rationale and coordination platform, not causal effects on recruitment, reintegration, or peace. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-resilient livelihoods and dialogue may support reintegration where poverty and exclusion narrow alternatives, but peace outcomes are unproven.

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate-mitigation-driven coal transition, not a physical climate hazard.
pathways.documented_impact: The World Bank anticipates job losses and worker/family dislocation in coal-dependent regions if transition is poorly managed.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Dependence on coal, unequal adjustment opportunities and reduced access to social/economic services can distribute transition costs unevenly.
pathways.possible_consequence: The source warns of possible mistrust, insecurity and social instability without mitigation; it does not document realized conflict.
alternative_explanations: Wider economic change, labour conditions, service provision and governance can independently affect trust and insecurity.
pathways.uncertainty: Prospective 2023 executive-summary mechanism. No measured transition-related violence, causal effect or emissions scenario; this is distinct from physical-hazard risks. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The report identifies inclusive local governance and knowledge as capacities; social/economic mitigation is a proposed safeguard, not an evaluated peace outcome.
pathways.compact_statement: In coal-dependent East Kalimantan and South Sumatra, a poorly managed mitigation transition could transmit job/service losses through unequal adjustment into mistrust and instability; the World Bank frames this as prospective risk, not observed conflict.

pathways.climate_pressure: Higher temperatures and warming-enhanced evaporative demand during multi-year drought.
pathways.documented_impact: More severe agricultural drought and water stress.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Irrigation dependence, livelihood losses, high input costs and limited alternatives.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where household buffers are weak, these pressures could increase distress mobility or socioeconomic grievances; violence is not demonstrated.
geographies: strongest livelihood relevance in irrigated agricultural areas
pathways.uncertainty: No national causal estimate links drought exposure to migration or grievances. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Warming-enhanced drought can worsen irrigation stress, but household and FCV consequences depend heavily on water governance and economic alternatives. (World Weather Attribution)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought/climate variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced water availability and perceived worsening of water insecurity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Allocation disputes, upstream/downstream differences, perceived injustice and competing sectoral claims.
pathways.possible_consequence: Local and regional water disputes may intensify when water insecurity and perception gaps are not managed.
alternative_explanations: agricultural policy and historical claims to water
pathways.uncertainty: Survey-based perception evidence cannot establish a unique climate causal effect. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Social-learning platforms and conflict-sensitive stakeholder dialogue recommended by the study
pathways.compact_statement: In ZayandehRud, climate-related water stress is documented as one factor interacting with allocation and perceived injustice in local disputes - not as a stand-alone conflict cause. (Directory of Open Access Journals)

pathways.climate_pressure: Meteorological/hydrological drought.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced recharge and increased groundwater depletion during dry conditions.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unsustainable withdrawals and governance of access to groundwater.
pathways.possible_consequence: Persistently depleted aquifers could deepen livelihood insecurity and competition among water users.
pathways.uncertainty: The groundwater study quantifies physical depletion drivers, not conflict or distributional outcomes. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought can accelerate groundwater depletion, but human withdrawal was the dominant documented 2002-2015 driver; downstream FCV effects remain unmeasured.

pathways.climate_pressure: Multiple climate hazards requiring adaptation.
pathways.documented_impact: Need for finance, technology and institutional capacity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Sanctions and restrictions on finance, technology and international cooperation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Adaptation planning or implementation may be slower, more expensive or narrower than otherwise possible.
pathways.uncertainty: The INDC is a government position and does not quantify sanctions' marginal adaptation effect. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Iran's own climate policy identifies sanctions and external restrictions as adaptation-capacity constraints, but the scale of their effect remains unevaluated. (Asia Pacific Energy Policy)

pathways.climate_pressure: Concurrent water and energy shortages.
pathways.documented_impact: Stress on economic activity and infrastructure.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict-related damage, sanctions, trade disruption, weak investment and import constraints.
pathways.possible_consequence: These conditions may reduce capacity to maintain, finance or upgrade water, energy and other climate-sensitive infrastructure.
pathways.uncertainty: No source in the verified set directly estimates lost adaptation investment. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Institutional delivery arrangements insulated from direct financing channels
such as the World Bank/WHO COVID project model
pathways.compact_statement: Current FCV and economic disruption can plausibly narrow infrastructure-resilience capacity, although quantitative adaptation losses are unmeasured. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and water scarcity.
pathways.documented_impact: Pressure on wetlands and dependent livelihoods.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competing water use, weak inter-organizational collaboration and livelihood dependence.
pathways.possible_consequence: Degradation could increase livelihood stress; participatory and integrated basin management may reduce such risk.
pathways.uncertainty: Programme reporting cannot establish counterfactual effectiveness. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Participatory wetland management provides a plausible resilience mechanism, but independent evidence of durable conflict- or vulnerability-reduction effects is missing. (UNDP)

pathways.climate_pressure: Water scarcity/drought.
pathways.documented_impact: Agricultural and economic stress.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Inflation, income pressure, food-market conditions and unequal household buffers.
pathways.possible_consequence: Combined pressures could raise grievances or lower coping capacity, especially among poorer households.
pathways.uncertainty: No verified study demonstrates a complete climate -> poverty -> grievance causal chain nationally. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress can add to household economic pressure, but sanctions, prices and conflict remain independent and potentially dominant explanations. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, scarcity, ecosystem stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Need for more efficient production and basin coordination.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Institutional fragmentation and competing user interests.
pathways.possible_consequence: Multi-stakeholder institutions and livelihood alternatives may reduce vulnerability and provide channels for managing distributional tensions.
alternative_explanations: Programme participation may be uneven and gains may not persist after funding
pathways.uncertainty: No verified independent evaluation demonstrates peace outcomes. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Iran has observable institutional and community adaptation assets, but their contribution to durable peace or FCV reduction has not been independently demonstrated. (FAOHome)

pathways.climate_pressure: Extreme heat exposure affecting agriculture and construction workers, combined in the World Bank scenario with lower water availability.
pathways.documented_impact: Modelled labour-productivity and earnings exposure, plus scenario-modelled GDP, food-price and poverty effects.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Livelihood insecurity, food prices, poverty and unequal exposure.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where social protection, jobs and services are inadequate, these pressures could increase grievances or susceptibility to instability; violence is not an automatic consequence.
pathways.uncertainty: The World Bank modeling quantifies exposure and macroeconomic/poverty implications, but the pathway does not establish that heat or water stress independently causes instability. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Modeled heat exposure and macroeconomic/food-price shocks could worsen labour income and poverty; any instability consequence remains an analytical inference conditioned by markets, protection and governance.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, declining water availability and salinity interacting with other water-management pressures.
pathways.documented_impact: Rural livelihood loss and climate-associated displacement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Rapid rural-urban mobility, inadequate urban services, limited employment, exclusion and harassment.
pathways.possible_consequence: Host-community/displaced-community tensions may increase where service capacity and economic opportunities are already weak.
affected_groups: Rural displaced households and urban host communities
alternative_explanations: urban labour-market weakness and pre-existing service deficits
pathways.uncertainty: Current displacement figures classify “climatic factors”; they do not isolate anthropogenic climate attribution. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: durable-solutions policy and recognition/support of climate-related mobility
pathways.compact_statement: Water-linked rural displacement can transfer stress to urban services and jobs, potentially increasing tensions where local capacity is inadequate. (The United Nations in Iraq)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and lower/less reliable water availability.
pathways.documented_impact: Tighter irrigation and groundwater access.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competition among user groups interacting with customary rights, centralized allocation, political affiliation and widespread weapons.
pathways.possible_consequence: Water disputes may escalate to violence in particular settings.
geographies: Strongest documented examples in southern governorates
affected_groups: Farmers and other local water users
pathways.uncertainty: No basis for a national claim that drought causes communal violence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: customary dispute-resolution mechanisms and transparent water-sharing institutions
pathways.compact_statement: Scarcer water can increase opportunities for violent competition, but escalation depends strongly on governance, allocation systems, weapons and local political relations.

pathways.climate_pressure: Water scarcity and heat create greater value and competition around climate-sensitive resources.
pathways.documented_impact: Armed actors or affiliates have reportedly bypassed regulations, controlled water-intensive activities or obstructed improvements to public systems in selected localities.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Coercion, political influence, regulatory capture and illicit/semi-licit resource markets.
pathways.possible_consequence: Adaptation and equitable resource management can become less effective, increasing vulnerability to future climate stress.
affected_groups: pastoral/nomadic communities and users lacking political protection
alternative_explanations: market incentives and broader corruption independent of organized armed actors
pathways.uncertainty: Representativeness and prevalence are not established nationally. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: transparent allocation and conflict-sensitive resource governance
pathways.compact_statement: In some localities, armed-actor political economy can undermine resource regulation and public services, reducing climate-adaptation capacity.

pathways.climate_pressure: More constrained and variable water availability increases the salience of allocation decisions.
pathways.documented_impact: Local and inter-governorate disputes over centrally allocated water.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Perceived inequity, limited participation, unclear responsibility and political mobilization.
pathways.possible_consequence: Allocation grievances may fuel protests, inter-community disputes or political confrontation.
geographies: Local disputes nationwide in UNAMI synthesis
alternative_explanations: historical allocation rules and political competition
pathways.uncertainty: Climate change is not separable from the broader water-governance system. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Water-governance choices mediate whether physical scarcity translates into cooperation or grievance.

pathways.climate_pressure: Water and livelihood stress contributing to displacement.
pathways.documented_impact: Climate-displaced populations may fall outside consistent registration and assistance systems.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Perceived neglect, unequal assistance, political patronage and exploitation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Distrust, protest risk and erosion of social cohesion may increase.
alternative_explanations: poverty and broader politicization of social assistance
pathways.uncertainty: Institutional treatment varies geographically; local examples cannot establish a uniform national pattern. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Displacement becomes a larger FCV risk when support systems are unclear, unequal or politically manipulated.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat, drought, floods and water stress increase demands on infrastructure and institutions.
pathways.documented_impact: Conflict-damaged or weak infrastructure, limited O&M and fragmented institutional capacity constrain reliable services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Reconstruction burden, weak governance, corruption and prioritization of security.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate shocks may generate larger welfare and livelihood losses because preventive and adaptive systems are weaker.
geographies: conflict-affected and service-deficient areas particularly relevant
alternative_explanations: demographic growth and technical inefficiency independent of armed conflict
pathways.uncertainty: Relative contribution of past conflict versus other institutional drivers is rarely quantified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: institutional coordination and systematic climate integration in reconstruction
pathways.compact_statement: FCV legacies can magnify climate vulnerability by weakening infrastructure, regulation and implementation capacity.

pathways.climate_pressure: Shared exposure to water scarcity and other climate risks.
pathways.documented_impact: Climate and natural-resource issues create common policy problems across communities and institutions.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Participation, dialogue, trust and locally accepted conflict-resolution mechanisms.
pathways.possible_consequence: Inclusive climate action may reduce escalation risks and strengthen social cohesion, although an effect on violence has not been quantitatively demonstrated.
geographies: Kirkuk example plus proposed national/subnational application
alternative_explanations: Existing social relations and political incentives may be more important than the climate forum/action itself
pathways.uncertainty: Evidence demonstrates a plausible entry point, not a measured peace impact. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: transparent allocation and locally legitimate dispute-resolution mechanisms
pathways.compact_statement: Climate action can support peace when it expands inclusive participation and legitimate resource-sharing mechanisms.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, reduced rainfall and water scarcity reported by participants in Nimrud and Hatra.
pathways.documented_impact: The qualitative assessment describes weakened farming livelihoods and agricultural productivity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competition for irrigation and land interacts with unequal access, exclusion and weak services.
pathways.possible_consequence: Participants describe farmer-herder tensions in Nimrud and resource/service pressures in Hatra; further stress could intensify existing grievances, not necessarily produce violence.
alternative_explanations: Post-conflict recovery, unemployment, patronage, service inequality and political influence also shape grievances independently of climate.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated qualitative mechanism from purposive February 2026 fieldwork; no causal estimate, representative prevalence or attribution to anthropogenic climate change. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Tribal mediation, shared economic activity and community networks are described capacities, not evaluated effects; less-connected groups can be excluded.
pathways.compact_statement: In Nimrud/Hatra, participants link water stress and farming losses with irrigation/land competition and existing grievances; local peace capacities are unevenly accessible.

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate/disaster shocks affecting disadvantaged settlements; no particular event or magnitude is specified.
pathways.documented_impact: Household and community vulnerability is heightened where basic services, housing and economic opportunities are weak.
pathways.fcv_mediator: The approach paper links spatial inequality and inner-city decay to crime/violence that hampers economic activity and undermines coping.
pathways.possible_consequence: Greater vulnerability to climate shocks, as stated by the IEG context diagnosis; no measured increase or named-community adaptation-access incident.
alternative_explanations: Poverty, land-use planning, public services, employment and broader economic shocks independently affect vulnerability and crime.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated reverse mechanism in a December 2025 evaluation approach paper. Not a causal estimate, completed evaluation result, current crime map or evidence that climate shocks cause crime. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The source describes social-protection reforms, while the CRVAs propose service and preparedness measures; effectiveness is not established by these passages.
pathways.compact_statement: The IEG Jamaica context diagnosis links crime/violence and constrained economic activity to weaker climate-shock resilience in excluded settlements; this reverse mechanism is generic and unquantified, not a claim that climate causes crime.

pathways.climate_pressure: Projected rainfall/drought pressures exacerbating already stressed water resources.
pathways.documented_impact: Possible further reductions in water/livelihood security and greater service/resource competition.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Pre-existing grievances, unequal/strained service access, resource-management failures and contested allocation can shape how scarcity is experienced.
pathways.possible_consequence: The 2023 roadmap warns of disputes, social discontent and anti-refugee sentiment; no measured climate-attributable violence or local incident trend.
alternative_explanations: Over-extraction, infrastructure, resource governance, poverty, service investment and regional politics independently affect water stress and social relations.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional 2023 synthesis, not a causal evaluation. Not projected onto the small Mafraq survey or used to stigmatize refugees; climate is neither the sole cause of scarcity nor proof of violence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The roadmap recommends integrated climate-security institutions, while local coping and water-system maintenance evidence identify capacities; proven conflict reduction is not asserted.
pathways.compact_statement: Jordan's 2023 roadmap warns that climate-exacerbated water/livelihood pressures can interact with pre-existing grievances and strained allocation to weaken cohesion; this is a conditional national mechanism, not a measured local climate–violence effect.

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate-related water stress as an aggravating factor in the historical transboundary-basin account.
pathways.documented_impact: Pressure on seasonal irrigation-water availability and allocation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Disputed allocations, weak shared information and damaged/lossy canal infrastructure.
pathways.possible_consequence: Risk of cross-border disputes; the source's Aspara account describes diplomacy/accounting as helping avoid violence, not climate inevitably causing violence.
alternative_explanations: Water-demand decisions, crop choice, infrastructure losses, allocation rules and bilateral institutions independently shape disputes.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical qualitative study, not causal attribution, current conflict incidence or measured efficacy of mediation; national drought probabilities are not conflict probabilities. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The study reports public diplomacy, transparent accounting and basin dialogue as prevention capacities in the Aspara case; effectiveness is not independently estimated.
pathways.compact_statement: In the historical Chu–Talas account, climate-related stress can aggravate allocation, information and canal-management disputes; the Aspara prevention example highlights dialogue/accounting without implying climate determinism.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought in arid counties.
pathways.documented_impact: Scarcer water and pasture.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Intercommunity resource competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: Conflict may intensify.
affected_groups: communities competing for pasture and water
alternative_explanations: Non-climatic resource-governance drivers are not isolated.
pathways.uncertainty: Government synthesis, not event-specific causal estimation. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought can intensify water/pasture competition and intercommunity conflict.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat and unreliable rainfall described in Turkana's May 2023 assessment.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced dry-season pasture and water availability undermine pastoral livelihoods.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competition over grazing land and livestock water interacts with political, environmental and economic challenges.
pathways.possible_consequence: The county assessment describes heightened likelihood of conflict and insecurity, not an inevitable violent outcome.
alternative_explanations: Political marginalization, land access, existing insecurity and economic change can independently shape competition and violence.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated qualitative mechanism dated 2023; no causal effect size, event attribution or 2026 conflict prediction. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Community groups and county support are reported resource-management capacities; effects and inclusive access were not independently evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: Turkana's 2023 assessment links drought-related pasture/water loss with competition and heightened insecurity, mediated by existing governance and livelihood pressures.

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate pressures on natural resources.
pathways.documented_impact: Water and livelihood constraints.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Inequitable resource access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Potential social conflict.
alternative_explanations: Gender and access inequalities are not solely climate-driven.
pathways.uncertainty: 2021 NDC risk statement; no observed conflict attribution. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Women's participation in resource allocation, as recommended by the NDC.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate pressures may compound unequal resource access and social tensions.

pathways.climate_pressure: Stream drying attributed to climate change by FAO's May 2024 Ak-Bashat feature.
pathways.documented_impact: A farmer describes lost orchard water and switching toward cattle.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competition over diminished local irrigation water and its distribution.
pathways.possible_consequence: The farmer describes disputes, including between friends; no violent outcome or prevalence is inferred.
alternative_explanations: Water demand, allocation rules and infrastructure can generate scarcity or disputes independently of climate.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated single farmer account in a 2024 agency feature; no representative sample, independent climate attribution or causal estimate. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Other locations' sensor and storage examples are not assumed to have resolved Ak-Bashat disputes.
pathways.compact_statement: A 2024 Ak-Bashat farmer account links stream-water loss, livelihood change and disputes; the mechanism is illustrative and unquantified.

pathways.climate_pressure: Seasonal flooding, storms and altered flood pulses around Tonle Sap.
pathways.documented_impact: The ethnography describes increased exposure and reduced fishing access after forced settlement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Eviction and fixed relocation removed households' ability to move with seasonal water and fish.
pathways.possible_consequence: Narrower livelihood and mobility options can constrain coping with water variability; no climate-induced violence is inferred.
alternative_explanations: Dams, land development, agricultural change and fishing restrictions also alter hydrology and access; climate contributions are not isolated.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical three-community ethnography, not a representative causal estimate. Reverse interaction concerns coercive relocation and exclusion, not armed-conflict classification. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Seasonal mobility was an existing coping practice whose loss is central to the account.
pathways.compact_statement: Forced settlement of Tonle Sap floating communities restricted seasonal mobility and fishing access, increasing vulnerability to water variability.

pathways.climate_pressure: Higher temperatures, declining precipitation and drought; projected dry-season water decline.
pathways.documented_impact: Water shortage, unreliable public supply and costly private alternatives.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal access, affordability, service failure, perceived unfairness and pre-existing group/resource competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where governance and distribution are already contested, additional water stress could worsen grievances or intergroup tensions.
geographies: strongest directly observed perception evidence in Beirut/Mount Lebanon and Beirut/Beqaa tension analysis
pathways.uncertainty: No source reviewed estimates an independent causal effect of climate change on violent conflict. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related water stress may aggravate tension through service failure and perceived inequity, but scarcity alone is not demonstrated to cause conflict. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat, drought, rainfall variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Self-reported livelihood/financial losses, especially among rural and economically precarious respondents.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Informal employment dependence, reduced household income, competition over jobs/resources and existing economic crisis.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate-sensitive livelihood shocks could intensify competition and social tension where labour markets and household finances are already stressed.
affected_groups: displaced Syrians working in climate-sensitive sectors
pathways.uncertainty: Survey respondents attribute losses to climate; causal attribution was not independently tested. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-sensitive livelihood losses may compound job/resource competition, but political economy and labour-market conditions remain independent drivers.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat, drought, floods and other climate hazards remain external pressures.
pathways.documented_impact: Crisis-constrained public finances and conflict-damaged lifeline infrastructure.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Reduced fiscal space, maintenance failures, implementation constraints and reconstruction burdens.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate hazards may produce larger service and welfare impacts because institutions and infrastructure have less capacity to absorb shocks.
geographies: especially conflict-damaged South/Nabatiyeh and service-stressed urban areas
alternative_explanations: Long-standing infrastructure underinvestment and governance weaknesses predate recent hostilities
pathways.uncertainty: Sources demonstrate damage and capacity constraints more directly than they measure resulting changes in climate vulnerability. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: protected maintenance finance and NAP integration
pathways.compact_statement: The strongest reverse pathway is that conflict and economic collapse weaken infrastructure and institutions needed to manage climate risk. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought/heat and water stress may affect agriculture and livelihoods.
pathways.documented_impact: High acute food insecurity in 2025.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict, displacement, loss of purchasing power and reduced humanitarian assistance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Additional climate-related production or income shocks could compound food insecurity and competition for scarce assistance or employment.
geographies: with rural and displacement-affected areas potentially more exposed
alternative_explanations: The cited 2025 evidence explicitly identifies conflict
displacement and reduced assistance - not climate - as the main immediate food-insecurity drivers
pathways.uncertainty: No reviewed source apportions the 2025 IPC burden quantitatively to climate. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate shocks could compound food insecurity, but the recent acute burden cannot be credibly described as climate-driven.

pathways.climate_pressure: Water scarcity/stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Water access can become a focus of local stress and mistrust.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Service-provider accountability, communication and intercommunity dialogue.
pathways.possible_consequence: Well-designed WASH investment may reduce tension while strengthening capacity to manage climate-related water stress.
geographies: candidate nationally only as a programme theory
alternative_explanations: Dialogue or wider political changes may have contributed independently
pathways.uncertainty: No counterfactual evaluation; the observed local experience does not establish general effectiveness. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: WASH projects can potentially serve as peace-supporting adaptation when infrastructure and dialogue are deliberately combined.

pathways.climate_pressure: Increasing water scarcity/drought can add stress to already contested resources.
pathways.documented_impact: Local competition over springs/groundwater and high reliance on informal/private provision.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Ambiguous land/water rights, weak enforcement, fragmented governance and perceived unequal allocation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Under worsening scarcity, unresolved institutional disputes could become harder to mediate and reduce cooperation needed for adaptation.
alternative_explanations: sectarian politics and governance failures can generate conflict independent of climatic change
pathways.uncertainty: Climate's contribution to the specific Bcharreh-Denniyeh conflict is not isolated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress may amplify contested water governance, but the causal core of documented local disputes is institutional and political as well as environmental.

pathways.climate_pressure: Pre-existing climate-related water-supply pressure described by the 2025 UN assessment.
pathways.documented_impact: Attacks damaged water facilities and disrupted household supply, including a named Rmeich case.
pathways.fcv_mediator: War-related infrastructure destruction and restricted inspection compound already strained water provision.
pathways.possible_consequence: Reduced household and service capacity to manage water stress, without attributing the conflict or site-specific water losses to climate.
alternative_explanations: Economic crisis, infrastructure maintenance and service governance also shape water access independently of climate or the assessed hostilities.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical 2024-war assessment; source-stated compounding mechanism, not a measured climate-conflict interaction or current 2026 service audit. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Proposed irrigation and farm recovery are needs and priorities, not evidence of restored capacity.
pathways.compact_statement: War-damaged water facilities in southern Lebanon compound pre-existing climate-related supply pressure and restrict households' coping capacity.

pathways.climate_pressure: Exceptional extreme rainfall during Storm Daniel; anthropogenic influence is plausible but highly uncertain.
pathways.documented_impact: Flooding, dam failures, widespread physical damage, service disruption and displacement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Infrastructure maintenance, institutional fragmentation, disaster planning, warning interpretation and coordination.
pathways.possible_consequence: Extreme rainfall can produce much larger human and economic losses where dam safety, maintenance, emergency governance and exposure are inadequate.
alternative_explanations: infrastructure quality and emergency decisions independently affected losses
pathways.uncertainty: The magnitude of anthropogenic influence on the rainfall is highly uncertain; no evidence apportions total losses quantitatively among rainfall, dams and governance. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Derna demonstrates compound disaster risk, not simple climate causation. (World Weather Attribution)

pathways.climate_pressure: Multiple climate hazards requiring coordinated preparation.
pathways.documented_impact: Weak/incomplete climate planning, degraded infrastructure and uneven emergency/recovery capacity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Divided governance, institutional rivalry, weak coordination and conflict legacy.
pathways.possible_consequence: Fragmentation may reduce the maintenance, planning and coordination needed to prevent climate shocks from becoming disasters.
geographies: with strongest direct disaster evidence in eastern Libya
affected_groups: especially communities relying on fragile public infrastructure
alternative_explanations: procurement and sanctions/external constraints may also affect implementation
pathways.uncertainty: Direct evidence varies by institution; national institutional weakness does not imply identical municipal performance. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: FCV-related institutional fragmentation is a documented constraint on climate resilience.

pathways.climate_pressure: Warming, drought, declining mean rainfall and rainfall variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Water stress, irrigation pressure and reduced rural livelihood resilience.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Water allocation, livelihood dependence, inequality, institutional legitimacy and market conditions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where access is perceived as inequitable and livelihood alternatives are weak, worsening water stress could increase grievances or local tension, but violence is not an automatic result.
pathways.uncertainty: No strong national causal estimate links temperature or rainfall change to violent events. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Water scarcity becomes an FCV risk through governance and livelihoods, not through climate alone. (SIPRI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Chronic water stress potentially intensified by warming and reduced rainfall.
pathways.documented_impact: Dependence on shared, vulnerable water infrastructure.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Allocation rules, control of pumps/infrastructure, perceptions of fairness and mutual dependence.
pathways.possible_consequence: Scarcity and shared infrastructure may produce either contestation or cooperation depending on governance arrangements and incentives.
affected_groups: Communities and users dependent on shared water systems
alternative_explanations: infrastructure condition and local power relationships can drive both service interruptions and cooperation independently of climate
pathways.uncertainty: Duration and transferability of cooperative arrangements are not evaluated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: credible allocation procedures and shared maintenance agreements
pathways.compact_statement: Water dependence is not intrinsically conflictual; institutions determine whether it divides or connects communities. (SIPRI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat and other climate stressors.
pathways.documented_impact: Livelihood disruption among some migrants and climate-sensitive communities.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict, income loss, migration policy, protection conditions, routes, markets and household resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate shocks may contribute to decisions to move, but available Libyan evidence does not establish them as a dominant or sufficient cause of migration.
pathways.uncertainty: The 25% climate-shock figure is sample-based association, not causal attribution. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: service inclusion and safe mobility options
pathways.compact_statement: Climate may be one migration stressor, but Libya's mobility dynamics remain strongly multi-causal. (SIPRI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Major flood/disaster event.
pathways.documented_impact: Humanitarian, service and reconstruction needs after Derna.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competing authorities, checkpoints, securitized access, institutional rivalry and social/legal status.
pathways.possible_consequence: Fragmented security governance can delay aid and make recovery less inclusive, particularly for groups with weak protection or documentation.
alternative_explanations: scale of destruction and administrative capacity also constrained response
pathways.uncertainty: Available evidence is predominantly qualitative regarding the magnitude of delay/exclusion. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: transparent reconstruction processes and status-neutral service provision
pathways.compact_statement: Political-security fragmentation affected who could deliver and receive recovery assistance. (SIPRI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Flooding, heat, drought and water stress.
pathways.documented_impact: WASH, health and education disruption; unreliable services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Pre-existing public-service weakness, displacement status, poverty, documentation and gender/age-related vulnerability.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate shocks may create larger welfare losses for people already facing weak services or barriers to assistance.
geographies: Strongest direct evidence in eastern flood zones
structural service weakness is national with regional differences
alternative_explanations: discrimination and chronic service underinvestment create vulnerability independently of climate
pathways.uncertainty: Differentiated quantitative outcome data are limited. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: resilient WASH/health systems and protection-sensitive disaster planning
pathways.compact_statement: Climate exposure intersects with pre-existing service and protection inequalities.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat, water scarcity and disaster risk.
pathways.documented_impact: Recognition of planning, infrastructure and technical-capacity deficits.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Institutional coordination, financing, local implementation capacity and shared-resource governance.
pathways.possible_consequence: The new drought and water strategies and local water/DRR investments could strengthen resilience and create practical cooperation incentives if implementation becomes sustained and inclusive.
alternative_explanations: Strategies may remain underfunded or fragmented
infrastructure investments may fail without maintenance and governance reform
pathways.uncertainty: Independent outcome evidence for 2025-2026 initiatives is not yet available. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Libya has emerging resilience assets, but implementation rather than policy adoption is the critical test. (UNDP)

pathways.climate_pressure: Cyclone Ditwah flooding and landslides during the November 2025-January 2026 emergency.
pathways.documented_impact: Displacement and damaged access routes increased dependence on temporary shelters and disrupted assistance.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Crowding, insufficient lighting and privacy, shared sanitation and gaps in accessible protection services raised exposure to harm.
pathways.possible_consequence: Heightened gender-based violence risk reported by UNFPA; no measured cyclone-attributable incidence.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing inequalities, household resources and service quality also influence protection risk.
Agency reporting is not an incident-based causal evaluation.
pathways.uncertainty: This is a source-stated post-disaster protection-risk mechanism, not proof of increased violence incidence, anthropogenic attribution of the cyclone, or a national FCV classification. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Accessible shelters, privacy, lighting, sanitation and functioning protection referrals can address the reported risk factors; effectiveness is not evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: Post-Ditwah shelter conditions and protection-service gaps heightened GBV risk; incidence changes were not measured.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought.
pathways.documented_impact: Rural water sources dry up.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Longer water-collection journeys for women and girls.
pathways.possible_consequence: Heightened exposure to abuse and violence.
alternative_explanations: Baseline gender inequalities and protection conditions also shape risk.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical protection-risk account; no measured violence effect or event attribution. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought-related water journeys can increase protection risks for women and girls.

pathways.climate_pressure: Extreme winds associated with Cyclone Gezani in February 2026.
pathways.documented_impact: Housing and service damage displaced people into temporary sites.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Crowding and limited services in displacement sites weakened children's protective environment.
pathways.possible_consequence: UNICEF reports heightened risks of violence and exploitation, not measured post-cyclone incident rates.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing inequalities, household resources and service quality also influence protection risk.
Agency reporting is not an incident-based causal evaluation.
pathways.uncertainty: This is a source-stated post-disaster protection-risk mechanism, not proof of increased violence incidence, anthropogenic attribution of the cyclone, or a national FCV classification. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Accessible shelters, privacy, lighting, sanitation and functioning protection referrals can address the reported risk factors; effectiveness is not evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: Post-Gezani displacement-site crowding and limited services heightened child violence/exploitation risk; incidence changes were not measured.

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate-related pressure on outer-island food and water security.
pathways.documented_impact: The UNDP assessment describes existing movement toward crowded Majuro and Ebeye.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal land access and limited urban services can mediate settlement and resource pressures.
pathways.possible_consequence: Poorly managed movement could increase grievances and resource competition; violence is not established.
alternative_explanations: Employment, education, services and historical relocation also drive mobility.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated prospective mechanism in the 2023 assessment, not causal attribution or a forecast of violence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Migration can provide opportunities; inclusive service provision and customary conflict resolution are proposed buffers.
pathways.compact_statement: Outer-island livelihood stress may interact with uneven land access and crowded urban services; mobility can also improve opportunities.

pathways.climate_pressure: Positive temperature anomalies and/or negative precipitation anomalies.
pathways.documented_impact: Changes in maize production and household food-security status.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Household food insecurity and livelihood stress.
pathways.possible_consequence: Higher subsequent incidence of several ACLED conflict-event categories, conditional on the study model.
pathways.uncertainty: Structural-equation mediation is compatible with the pathway but does not establish event-level climate causality. (Frontiers) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate anomalies may contribute to conflict risk through crop and food-security effects, but the observed relationship is mediated and non-deterministic.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, inadequate rain, late or variable rainy seasons.
pathways.documented_impact: Changes in pasture/water availability and livestock movement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Rules governing access to land, water and seasonal routes; interaction among farmers and pastoral groups.
pathways.possible_consequence: Local disputes or violence may become more likely where mobility intersects poorly governed or contested access.
geographies: Inner Niger Delta and pastoral corridors
pathways.uncertainty: Mobility is itself an adaptation strategy and must not be characterized as inherently destabilizing. (SIPRI) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Rainfall stress can alter pastoral mobility, but whether this becomes conflict depends heavily on institutions and access governance.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heavy precipitation and floods.
pathways.documented_impact: Crop losses, erosion and potential infrastructure damage; FAO specifically reported 2024 flood-related crop losses.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Food prices, market access, household asset depletion and uneven assistance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Higher vulnerability, displacement or local grievances may result where recovery and markets are weak.
pathways.uncertainty: No retained source directly demonstrates that specific Mali floods caused subsequent violence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Flood losses can deepen food and livelihood stress, but an FCV consequence requires additional social and institutional mediators. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat and rainfall-related livelihood stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced or more uncertain natural-resource-based livelihood options.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Poverty, unemployment, absence of alternatives, grievances and armed-group economic incentives.
pathways.possible_consequence: Recruitment vulnerability may increase for some individuals.
geographies: Principally northern and central Mali in the retained qualitative evidence
pathways.uncertainty: SIPRI explicitly describes recruitment as complex and the study as a plausibility probe. (SIPRI) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress may narrow livelihoods and thereby enlarge recruitment opportunities, but it is one contributor among many.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought/rainfall variability remains the environmental stressor to which livelihood systems need to adapt.
pathways.documented_impact: Conflict disrupted irrigation and livestock markets and pushed some herds southward.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Insecurity, market closure and constrained movement.
pathways.possible_consequence: Households may lose access to otherwise effective drought-coping options and face greater resource pressure elsewhere.
pathways.uncertainty: Qualitative evidence documents coping strategies and conflict disruption, but does not estimate the incremental loss of climate-adaptation performance. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict can disable livelihood strategies that would otherwise help households adapt to climatic variability. (SIPRI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Increasing heat, variable rainfall, drought/flood exposure.
pathways.documented_impact: Growing pressure on natural-resource management and demand for coordinated adaptation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak institutional coordination, limited budgets, unequal access and weak local governance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Adaptation gaps and perceived unfairness may aggravate grievances or disputes.
geographies: with greater constraints in conflict-prone localities
pathways.uncertainty: Institutional weakness is independently consequential and should not be relabelled as a climate effect. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate pressures place additional demands on already constrained institutions; weak or unequal responses can in turn worsen both vulnerability and grievance risk. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and rainfall variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Need for mobility, livelihood adjustment and collective natural-resource management.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Local legitimacy, dispute resolution, collective decision-making and grievance handling.
pathways.possible_consequence: Locally legitimate institutions may support coping and reduce escalation risk, but the planned committee mechanism and peace effects are not observed outcomes.
geographies: specific evidence should not be generalized to all Mali
alternative_explanations: Some local institutions can also reproduce exclusion or unequal access
pathways.uncertainty: Strong independent evidence on peace outcomes from climate/resource institutions remains limited. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Locally legitimate coping and resource-governance institutions are plausible peace-supporting capacities, but their distributional and conflict effects require evaluation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Dry-season water scarcity described by Dembala residents.
pathways.documented_impact: Pump/well failures restricted drinking water and vegetable-growing access.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competition at scarce shared water points amid livelihood pressure.
pathways.possible_consequence: Residents reported fights over water; the story does not establish violence incidence or a climate-attributable effect.
alternative_explanations: Pump maintenance, local water governance and livelihood conditions also shape scarcity and disputes.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical resident testimony in a 2025 implementer story; village district not verified; not a representative causal study. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Reported water-point rehabilitation restored access, but conflict reduction was not independently evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: Dembala residents linked dry-season water-point failures with livelihood constraints and disputes; rehabilitation is a reported capacity response.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rising temperature, longer dry spells and inadequate water.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced rain-fed agricultural performance and livelihood security.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Debt, landlessness risk, rising input costs, declining credit, poverty and an existing armed-conflict environment.
