pathways.possible_consequence: These combined pressures may influence grievances and household/community relationships with armed resistance actors; the evidence does not show climate as an independent cause of recruitment or violence.
geographies: Magway and lower Sagaing Dry Zone
pathways.uncertainty: SIPRI/NUPI directly presents the chain but does not estimate the independent effect of climate stress. (SIPRI6) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: climate information and local conflict-sensitive agricultural support
pathways.compact_statement: Dry Zone climate stress can worsen farm hardship, but any effect on conflict dynamics is mediated through finance, livelihoods and pre-existing political violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Cyclone, extreme rain and flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Damage to shelter, WASH, infrastructure, livelihoods and services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Humanitarian-access restrictions, insecurity, territorial contestation and blocked transport.
pathways.possible_consequence: Slower relief and recovery can prolong unmet needs and deepen vulnerability.
affected_groups: Rohingya and ethnic Rakhine populations among others
alternative_explanations: terrain and the scale of the disaster
pathways.uncertainty: Evidence is strong for specific events but cannot be assumed uniform across Myanmar. (Doctors Without Borders4) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict and access restrictions have demonstrably reduced the reach of climate-disaster response in specific Myanmar settings.

pathways.climate_pressure: Floods, cyclones and heavy rain.
pathways.documented_impact: Temporary relocation, camp damage, WASH shortages and mine/ERW uncertainty.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Prior conflict displacement and settlement in vulnerable locations.
pathways.possible_consequence: People displaced by conflict may face repeated displacement and accumulating asset/service losses during climatic disasters.
alternative_explanations: poor settlement siting and inadequate infrastructure can generate vulnerability independently of conflict
pathways.uncertainty: National IDP figures do not indicate how many IDPs are directly climate-exposed. (World Bank5) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict displacement can turn a climatic shock into repeated displacement and additional protection risk.

pathways.climate_pressure: Floods, cyclones, heat and other weather extremes.
pathways.documented_impact: Need to evacuate, migrate or relocate.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict, mobility restrictions, insecurity and contested territory.
pathways.possible_consequence: Households unable to move safely may remain in highly exposed areas or lose access to livelihoods and assistance.
geographies: source emphasizes displaced and minority populations
pathways.uncertainty: Limited quantitative evidence identifies the relative contribution of each mobility constraint. (SIPRI6) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict-related mobility constraints can reduce people's ability to use migration or evacuation as climate coping strategies.

pathways.climate_pressure: Cyclones and other disasters.
pathways.documented_impact: Large relief and governance needs.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competing authorities' attempts to demonstrate governing capacity and legitimacy.
pathways.possible_consequence: Disaster response may reshape grievances and perceived authority without the hazard itself causing renewed conflict.
affected_groups: Disaster-affected communities including marginalized Rohingya populations
institutions: KNU and other local governance actors
pathways.uncertainty: Political effects vary strongly by actor and locality. (SIPRI6) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: In post-coup Myanmar, disaster and climate action can become part of struggles over authority rather than merely technical adaptation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate hazards interacting with seasonal farming needs.
pathways.documented_impact: Threats to harvest and food security.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed confrontation preventing normal agricultural activity.
pathways.possible_consequence: Negotiated agricultural access may create a temporary peace-supporting window.
alternative_explanations: military or political rather than climate-specific
pathways.uncertainty: No evidence of durable peace effects. (SIPRI6) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Locally mediated harvest access can support food security and temporary de-escalation, but it is not evidence that adaptation causes peace.

pathways.climate_pressure: Multi-hazard climate risk requiring information, planning and coordinated adaptation.
pathways.documented_impact: High demand for climate information, agricultural adaptation and disaster preparedness.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Fragmented territorial control, contested institutions and politicization of environmental action.
pathways.possible_consequence: National adaptation plans and services may have uneven territorial reach and may be interpreted through political competition.
alternative_explanations: Long-standing administrative capacity and finance constraints predate the coup
pathways.uncertainty: No national post-2021 implementation audit was located. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict and divided authority appear to make adaptation capacity territorially uneven and politically contested.

pathways.climate_pressure: Flood, drought and livelihood shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: Local infrastructure, food and service needs.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak/contested state reach and security conditions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Community assets, grassroots institutions and third-party implementation may sustain limited resilience where conventional public delivery is constrained.
geographies: Karen areas and conflict-affected World Bank project locations
alternative_explanations: Selection toward more stable areas may itself explain better delivery
pathways.uncertainty: Programme outputs and institutional activity are not evidence of durable resilience or peace outcomes. (World Food Programme3) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Alternative delivery institutions can bridge some resilience gaps, but effectiveness and equity require independent evaluation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Projected longer dry periods and reduced rainfall.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced agricultural and public water availability in the Zeta and Bjelopavlici plains and coastal areas.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competing agricultural, public-supply and tourism water uses place pressure on a shared resource.
pathways.possible_consequence: The 2025 plan warns of possible water-use disputes, particularly involving tourism; it does not report violence.
alternative_explanations: Seasonal tourism demand, infrastructure and allocation decisions also affect scarcity and competition.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional planning risk with unspecified emissions pathway and no dispute counts, actors or violent outcome; not a conflict forecast. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The national plan provides a coordination framework; delivery and local allocation effectiveness were not assessed.
pathways.compact_statement: The 2025 plan links projected dryness and shared water demand to possible water-use disputes, not observed violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Pasture degradation and climatic stress in the dzud-resilience assessment.
pathways.documented_impact: Herders seek Otor pasture in other aimags as grazing access becomes constrained.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal access and limited systematic management of movement and shared pasture can mediate resource competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: The report describes disputes between incoming herders and local users, without event counts or armed-conflict evidence.
alternative_explanations: Herd size, grazing pressure and land-management arrangements also affect degradation and disputes.
Not all mobility or resource competition produces conflict.
pathways.uncertainty: Qualitative source-stated mechanism, not a measured climate-attributable conflict effect or a prediction for named receiving settlements. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Transparent shared-pasture rules and monitoring are proposed governance responses, not evaluated conflict-reduction interventions.
pathways.compact_statement: Pasture stress and inter-aimag grazing mobility can interact with access and governance constraints to produce disputes; armed conflict is not established.

pathways.climate_pressure: Tropical cyclones, intense rainfall and flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Crop/livelihood losses and damage to schools, health facilities and water infrastructure.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Food access, market access, displacement, service scarcity and coping-capacity erosion.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where conflict, poverty or displacement already constrain households, repeated disaster losses could deepen humanitarian dependence and local competition, but violence is not an automatic outcome.
geographies: current 2026 flood areas include Gaza/Sofala and storm-affected Inhambane
alternative_explanations: market isolation and pre-existing service shortages
pathways.uncertainty: No identified national study estimates how much conflict or fragility risk changes because of cyclone exposure alone. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Cyclone/flood losses can worsen food and service stress through livelihoods, markets and displacement, especially where non-climate fragilities are already severe.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat, drought and irregular rainfall.
pathways.documented_impact: Local pressure on arable land, fisheries and food availability.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Food insecurity, poverty, youth unemployment and competition over resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: These conditions may intensify local resource competition in Mecufi, but retained evidence does not establish violent recruitment or violence.
geographies: Mecufi District only for the complete pathway
pathways.uncertainty: Local participatory evidence only; the inaccessible four-location conflict study was removed. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: In Mecufi, climate-related livelihood stress is plausibly linked to competition through food insecurity and socioeconomic inequality rather than directly to violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, cyclone and flood damage affecting productive land.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced or degraded cultivable land in the local assessment.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict displacement, rapid land occupation, unequal access and land governance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Disputes between hosts, displaced households or politically/economically stronger and weaker groups could intensify.
affected_groups: ethnic groups with unequal bargaining power
pathways.uncertainty: The Mecufi assessment identifies a possible land-dispute mechanism; the inaccessible broader study was removed. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: In Mecufi, climate-related land pressure and conflict-driven displacement can interact through land access and governance.

pathways.climate_pressure: Background cyclone, flood and coastal-erosion risk.
pathways.documented_impact: Local mangroves serve as a protective ecological asset.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Insurgency-driven displacement, livelihood loss and pressure on services/natural resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: Unsustainable extraction, including mangrove cutting for salt production, may weaken natural buffering capacity and increase future hazard vulnerability.
pathways.uncertainty: Magnitude of mangrove loss attributable specifically to conflict displacement is not quantified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: mangrove protection/restoration and conflict-sensitive resource governance
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict-related livelihood and displacement pressures can degrade natural assets that otherwise buffer climate hazards.

pathways.climate_pressure: Multiple recurring hazards require functioning health, education, WASH, transport and local governance.
pathways.documented_impact: Northern violence has caused displacement, infrastructure destruction and school closures.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Insecurity, restricted mobility, damaged infrastructure, weakened services and overstretched humanitarian capacity.
pathways.possible_consequence: Hazard preparedness, recovery and long-term adaptation may be slower or less equitable in conflict-affected districts.
pathways.uncertainty: Displacement, service impacts and local capacity constraints are documented; adaptation-delay effects are not quantified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: protected service delivery and anticipatory financing
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict can make climate adaptation harder by disrupting the institutions, services and mobility on which preparedness and recovery depend.

pathways.climate_pressure: Cyclones and flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Damage, poor sanitation and communicable-disease risks.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak public-health/adaptation intervention, rumours and distrust of authorities.
pathways.possible_consequence: The Mecufi assessment reports a pathway toward insecurity, protest or social unrest where disease outbreaks are interpreted through mistrust.
alternative_explanations: disease dynamics unrelated to climate and political grievances
pathways.uncertainty: No incidence/risk effect size is provided. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: responsive health services and community participation
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related disaster disruption may become politically salient through public-health failures and mistrust rather than through climate exposure alone.

pathways.climate_pressure: Multi-hazard climate exposure.
pathways.documented_impact: Large adaptation requirements and recurring livelihood/infrastructure losses.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Fiscal constraints, weak coordination, incomplete technical capacity and unequal service delivery.
pathways.possible_consequence: Uneven implementation could leave poorer or conflict-affected communities with lower resilience, potentially reinforcing existing inequalities and grievances.
affected_groups: Poor households and poorly served districts
pathways.uncertainty: No evidence found demonstrating that adaptation funding gaps themselves cause instability. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Implementation capacity is a mediator of climate vulnerability, but its relationship to fragility requires further empirical testing.

pathways.climate_pressure: Locally identified drought, flood, cyclone and coastal pressures.
pathways.documented_impact: Shared analysis of climate-security risks by authorities, communities and peacebuilders.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Trust, participation, conflict mediation, early warning and locally legitimate decision-making.
pathways.possible_consequence: These capacities could reduce escalation and improve conflict-sensitive adaptation, although effectiveness has not yet been demonstrated.
alternative_explanations: Wider security conditions and state policy may overwhelm local peacebuilding capacities
pathways.uncertainty: The evidence establishes a participatory assessment process, not effects on trust, escalation or adaptation outcomes. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: A participatory multistakeholder climate-security assessment process is documented in Mecufi; effects on trust, escalation or adaptation outcomes have not been demonstrated.

pathways.climate_pressure: Changing rainfall and environmental stress affecting grazing and water resources.
pathways.documented_impact: DPPA describes altered transhumance and pressure around refugee-hosting areas outside Mbera.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Longstanding resentments, grazing competition and unequal representation/access among arrival cohorts.
pathways.possible_consequence: Potential host–refugee or inter-herder tensions; no climate-attributable violence incidence is estimated.
alternative_explanations: Historical resentments, representation, services and insecurity in neighbouring Mali also shape pressures.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated conditional pathway in an executive summary; underlying incident evidence not reviewed, not proof that climate caused armed violence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Communal committees and inclusive resource governance are identified capacities, with effectiveness unverified.
pathways.compact_statement: Around Mbera, climate-related resource pressure can interact with longstanding grievances and grazing/water access; tensions are conditional, not inevitable.

pathways.climate_pressure: El Niño-related drought and livelihood/food insecurity in the 2023/24 period.
pathways.documented_impact: Household economic stress and harmful coping pressures affected children and women.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal control over relief/resources, weak community protection services and economic dependence.
pathways.possible_consequence: The assessment reports exploitation risks and rising reported child marriage; Machinga counts illustrate reporting, not prevalence or attribution.
alternative_explanations: Food-price inflation, accumulated shocks, reporting/access changes and pre-existing gender inequality also matter.
pathways.uncertainty: A source-stated risk mechanism synthesized in July 2024, not a climate-attributable violence estimate or a 2026 protection assessment. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Accessible protection services and inclusive response decisions address identified constraints; effectiveness is not established here.
pathways.compact_statement: The 2024 assessment links livelihood stress and unequal resource access with protection risks, with a historical Machinga reporting example; causal attribution is unresolved.

pathways.climate_pressure: Flood and other climate hazards creating displacement risk.
pathways.documented_impact: Loss of housing/livelihood stability and disruption of social/economic/legal protections.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Recognition, service access and protection gaps can limit safe coping and fair allocation during displacement.
pathways.possible_consequence: The ISIS authors warn of escalating resource competition and tensions with host communities or the state; no measured violence outcome.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing inequality, tenure rules, service investment, urban development and wider political/economic conditions also affect displacement and social relations.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional national policy analysis, not local incident evidence or causal evaluation. Legal-protection claims are attributed to the authors, not current legal advice; no displaced-group threat label. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The CCDR recommends targeted housing/livelihood/financial support and inclusive planning; delivery and peace effects are not established.
pathways.compact_statement: The 2026 ISIS note warns that climate-related displacement can weaken protective systems and, where recognition/services are inadequate, aggravate resource tensions; this is conditional policy analysis, not observed climate-caused violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Below-average rainfall and drought during the period reviewed in 2022.
pathways.documented_impact: Pastoral households move seasonally in search of grazing and water, including between Namibia and Angola.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Concentration of users and increased pressure on scarce grazing and water resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: IFRC associates this movement with resource competition and conflict, without specifying conflict type, incidents or scale.
institutions: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
alternative_explanations: Land access, service provision, pre-existing resource arrangements and livelihood conditions also shape competition; mobility is an established risk-management practice.
pathways.uncertainty: Localized qualitative assessment. Conflict is unspecified and must not be read as armed violence, ethnic hostility or a general risk posed by migrants. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Pastoral mobility can manage climatic risk; water-system rehabilitation and cash assistance were reported separately, without evaluated conflict-prevention outcomes.
pathways.compact_statement: The 2022 IFRC assessment associates drought-related pastoral movement with resource competition and unspecified conflict, not an armed-conflict forecast.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rainfall variability, dry spells and rising temperatures.
pathways.documented_impact: Pressure on rainfed and pastoral livelihood strategies and adaptation choices.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Cultivation encroachment, livestock mobility, access to wells/pasture, demographic pressure and weak/unequal land-governance implementation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Localized disputes or violence between resource users may become more likely where institutions fail to manage competing access.
geographies: particularly pastoral/agropastoral contexts in Tahoua and Tillabéri
pathways.uncertainty: No current national causal estimate. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: protected mobility corridors and equitable water/pasture rules
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress can alter livelihood strategies, but whether this becomes conflict depends strongly on land institutions, access rules and political-economic conditions. (ResearchGate)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, variable rainfall, heat.
pathways.documented_impact: Changing pastoral mobility and water/pasture strategies.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Agricultural encroachment, corridor obstruction, well access, unequal legal representation and weak Rural Code enforcement.
pathways.possible_consequence: Conflict risk may increase at specific encounter points between mobile herders and cultivators.
pathways.uncertainty: Present-day magnitude and geographic distribution are not established. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Legally protected corridors and credible local mediation
pathways.compact_statement: Water or pasture scarcity is not sufficient to produce violence; conflict emerges through contested access and governance. (ResearchGate)

pathways.climate_pressure: Background rainfall variability and agricultural climate dependence.
pathways.documented_impact: Civil insecurity restricted access to fields and caused localized production shortfalls in Tillabéri and Diffa in 2025.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed insecurity and mobility restrictions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Households with reduced farm access may possess less income, stocks and flexibility to absorb subsequent drought/flood shocks.
pathways.uncertainty: Household-level resilience losses are not quantified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Current evidence more clearly demonstrates insecurity constraining climate-sensitive livelihoods than climate shocks directly causing insecurity. (FAOHome)

pathways.climate_pressure: Floods, droughts and other covariate shocks remain background risks.
pathways.documented_impact: Displacement and insecurity increase needs while health, education and other services face access and funding constraints.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Forced displacement, insecure roads/territories, concentrated urban demand and resource constraints.
pathways.possible_consequence: Reduced baseline service capacity may make subsequent climate emergencies harder to absorb.
alternative_explanations: rapid population growth and fiscal constraints
pathways.uncertainty: Direct climate-adaptation outcome evaluation is absent. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: FCV can erode the service base on which effective disaster response and adaptation depend.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought/rainfall uncertainty.
pathways.documented_impact: Farmers and pastoralists diversify, change mobility, intensify agriculture, build wells or monetize previously shared resources.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal capital, tenure, access and institutional representation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Some adaptation choices may shift costs or exclude other groups, creating grievances or disputes.
geographies: Local rural Niger in older field evidence
alternative_explanations: Commercialization and demographic growth independent of climate
pathways.uncertainty: Contemporary prevalence is unknown. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: participatory governance and conflict-sensitive adaptation design
pathways.compact_statement: An adaptation intervention should not be assumed peace-positive merely because it reduces climate exposure. (ResearchGate)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, flood, rainfall variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Niger's policies call for improved forecasting, early warning and locally accessible climate services; UNICEF reports anticipatory flood preparation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Timeliness and inclusiveness of information/assistance, local capacity and financing.
pathways.possible_consequence: Earlier action could reduce livelihood losses and pressure on crisis-response systems, provided services reach insecure and marginalized communities.
alternative_explanations: market access and infrastructure may dominate household outcomes
pathways.uncertainty: Current programme descriptions do not establish avoided losses or peace effects. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Early warning is a plausible resilience mechanism, but current evidence in this packet mostly demonstrates capacity and outputs rather than impacts.

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate variability raises the value of flexible access to land, pasture and water.
pathways.documented_impact: Resource-access disputes occur where mobility and cultivation overlap.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Quality and legitimacy of local dispute-resolution institutions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Inclusive land commissions and mediation may reduce escalation, but the observed conflict-reduction account is old and limited to one community.
geographies: broader mechanisms referenced in the 2026 World Bank diagnostic
alternative_explanations: local power relations and enforcement capacity
pathways.uncertainty: Louma finding is old and one-community evidence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Representation of both livelihood groups and women
pathways.compact_statement: Legitimate institutions may govern resource access and disputes more effectively, but the peace effect is supported only by old, localized evidence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Higher temperatures, drought risk and rainfall variability in northern savanna areas.
pathways.documented_impact: Pressure on pastoral livelihoods/grazing resources and changing mobility patterns.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Movement into farming zones; land/resource access; weak land/livestock governance; small-arms and wider political/social conditions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Farmer-herder disputes may become more difficult to manage and, where governance and security conditions permit escalation, may become violent.
pathways.uncertainty: Climate is neither necessary nor sufficient for violence; spatial evidence directly cautions against a monotonic climate-conflict relationship. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress may shape pastoral mobility, but governance and other conflict drivers determine whether mobility becomes violent competition.

pathways.climate_pressure: Northern livelihood and grazing stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Seasonal or longer-distance pastoral movement toward less climate-exposed areas.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Destination-area competition and institutions governing access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Conflict risk may rise in places where climate impacts are less acute if those areas receive mobile livelihood groups and resource governance is weak.
pathways.uncertainty: One spatial study cannot establish a national law-like relationship. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: The geographic location of climate stress and the location of violence can diverge because mobility transfers pressures across space. (SIPRI2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Background climate stress in the Lake Chad livelihood system.
pathways.documented_impact: Fishers and pastoralists require access to water, fisheries and pasture.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Military/security restrictions, forced evacuation, movement limitations and market closures.
pathways.possible_consequence: Conflict measures can reduce coping options and increase vulnerability to subsequent climate stress.
pathways.uncertainty: Evidence is narrow and older; national generalization is inappropriate. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: livelihood-sensitive security planning and maintaining safe access to productive resources where feasible
pathways.compact_statement: FCV can increase climate vulnerability by restricting access to the resources on which coping livelihoods depend.

pathways.climate_pressure: Not required as the proximate trigger; climate shocks can coexist in the wider food system.
pathways.documented_impact: Violence displaces people from farmland and obstructs humanitarian supply routes.
pathways.fcv_mediator: attacks, illegal checkpoints, partial inaccessibility and displacement.
pathways.possible_consequence: Reduced assistance and market/land access can deepen hunger and reduce households' capacity to withstand additional shocks, including climate shocks.
pathways.uncertainty: Current IPC evidence does not identify climate as a proximate malnutrition driver. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict demonstrably constrains food-assistance delivery; its effect on climate resilience is plausible but not separately quantified. (World Food Programme8)

pathways.climate_pressure: Multiple hazards across very different ecological regions.
pathways.documented_impact: Need for cross-sector, multi-level adaptation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak coordination, limited local-government involvement, inadequate finance/skills and weak M&E.
pathways.possible_consequence: Adaptation may be delayed, fragmented or uneven, potentially leaving vulnerable/conflict-affected areas with lower resilience.
pathways.uncertainty: No evidence reviewed shows these adaptation gaps directly producing violence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Institutional fragmentation is a documented adaptation constraint, but any downstream FCV effect remains unproven. (UNFCCC1)

pathways.climate_pressure: Seasonal flood risk.
pathways.documented_impact: Nigeria has recently experienced large flood exposure and displacement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: preparedness and institutional coordination can affect whether shocks translate into emergency displacement and service overload.
pathways.possible_consequence: Effective early warning, anticipatory financing and evacuation could reduce losses and displacement.
pathways.uncertainty: Current evidence demonstrates activation, not avoided mortality or displacement. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Nigeria is strengthening anticipatory flood mechanisms, but their real-world effectiveness remains an evaluation gap. (NEMA14)

pathways.climate_pressure: Heavy precipitation, erosion and watershed degradation.
pathways.documented_impact: NEWMAP treated erosion sites and supported landscape-management planning.
pathways.fcv_mediator: state capacity, local organization, maintenance and political commitment.
pathways.possible_consequence: Sustained institutions and watershed management may reduce vulnerability and protect livelihoods, helping limit shock-related disruption.
alternative_explanations: site-specific geomorphology and independent environmental changes
pathways.uncertainty: IEG explicitly found insufficient outcome evidence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: NEWMAP built tangible resilience capacities, but independent evidence of the intended reduction in erosion vulnerability was incomplete. (World Bank3)

pathways.climate_pressure: September 2024 flooding and landslides.
pathways.documented_impact: Housing disruption and displacement into temporary accommodation, with gaps in basic and protection services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal access and pre-existing gender/disability vulnerability in displacement settings.
pathways.possible_consequence: The response plan identifies heightened protection risks and calls for violence-prevention and inclusive access; it does not estimate actual new violence.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing exclusion, accommodation design and service availability shape risk independently of hazard severity.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical needs assessment and prospective protection-risk mechanism, not a reported violence rate or climate-attribution estimate. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The plan prioritizes accessible services and protection referral; delivery and effectiveness are not established.
pathways.compact_statement: The 2024 Nepal flood plan identifies protection risks where displacement meets service gaps and unequal access, without measuring new violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Coastal land and infrastructure risks, including projected sea-level rise.
pathways.documented_impact: The national plan proposes higher-ground development and relocation of coastal assets.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Legacy wartime explosives, mined-land pinnacles and rehabilitation costs limit usable higher-ground land.
pathways.possible_consequence: Land rehabilitation for housing, water catchment and infrastructure is constrained, complicating the planned adaptation pathway.
institutions: Government of the Republic of Nauru
alternative_explanations: Phosphate-mining damage, outdated land legislation, finance and technical capacity are additional constraints; the explosives' separate contribution is not quantified.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical war legacy, not current armed conflict. No explosive inventory, clearance cost, site hazard boundary or measured relocation delay is established. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The Higher Ground Initiative and land-use planning offer an adaptation framework; financing and delivery remain conditional.
pathways.compact_statement: Wartime explosive remnants and mined-land rehabilitation costs constrain the usable higher-ground land needed for planned coastal adaptation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Sea-level/storm-surge pressures and reported changes in coastal water/livelihood conditions.
pathways.documented_impact: The Tandubas workshop case describes salinity/freshwater losses, affected fishing/seaweed livelihoods and movement inland.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Inland settlement encountering ancestral sites and contested land/cultural rights.
pathways.possible_consequence: Participants linked this to disputes, cultural conflict and crime/violence; no incidence estimate or causal identification.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing land rights, historical injustice, governance, livelihood change and settlement pressures independently shape conflict.
pathways.uncertainty: A 2023 workshop case, not representative or independently causal evidence. Local/Indigenous/vulnerable residents were not adequately represented; no current violence map or attribution of individual events to anthropogenic change. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Inclusive land-use dialogue and protection of rights are relevant safeguards; the workshop does not evaluate their delivery or peace effects.
pathways.compact_statement: The 2023 Tandubas workshop account links coastal livelihood/water pressures and inland movement with ancestral-site disputes; it is a low-confidence, source-stated local mechanism, not a measured climate effect on violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Increasing heavy rainfall and flood loading in steep Highlands terrain and major river basins
pathways.documented_impact: Flooding, slope saturation, road disruption, settlement exposure, and service isolation
pathways.fcv_mediator: Rugged terrain, weak transport, uneven provincial capacity, insecurity, and limited remote-service reach
pathways.possible_consequence: Repeated isolation and unequal recovery may deepen deprivation and grievance, but climate pressure does not automatically cause violence
alternative_explanations: Road underinvestment, remoteness, insecurity, maintenance failure, and extreme topography can isolate communities without climate change.
pathways.uncertainty: Physical and access links are documented, but grievance and conflict consequences are not causally estimated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Heavy rainfall can deepen service isolation where rugged terrain, weak transport, insecurity, and uneven provincial capacity restrict recovery.

pathways.climate_pressure: El Nino drought, frost and rainfall variability affecting subsistence production
pathways.documented_impact: Crop loss, food and water shortages, reduced meals, and stress on household support networks
pathways.fcv_mediator: Subsistence dependence, market and transport constraints, strained wantok support, poverty, and weak formal safety nets
pathways.possible_consequence: Food insecurity and pressure on household support networks may increase when households exhaust coping options; effects on migration, exclusion, or competition for assistance are not established here.
alternative_explanations: Market prices, crop disease, transport failure, poverty, and policy choices independently shape food insecurity and migration.
pathways.uncertainty: The pathway is supported by operational and qualitative evidence but not a causal estimate of migration or tension. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought and frost can erode food security and coping where subsistence dependence, poor market access, and strained local support narrow alternatives.

pathways.climate_pressure: Coastal flooding, sea-level pressure, erosion, and salinity contributing to mobility and relocation needs
pathways.documented_impact: Loss of habitability, freshwater and livelihood pressure, and movement to receiving land
pathways.fcv_mediator: Customary tenure, lineage rights, host consent, compensation, cultural attachment, population pressure, and weak relocation systems
pathways.possible_consequence: Relocation may stall or generate land and service disputes unless agreements and host-community support are inclusive
geographies: coastal and island Papua New Guinea
alternative_explanations: Tectonic movement, volcanic hazards, population pressure, reef processes, development decisions, and pre-existing land disputes also shape mobility.
pathways.uncertainty: Carteret evidence is multicausal and source-specific; national multi-hazard displacement is context only. The Port Moresby single-site survey (PNG-E-008) is retained standalone, not used as Carteret/coastal relocation evidence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Coastal mobility can create land and service disputes when customary tenure and host consent are not addressed through inclusive relocation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Flood, drought, landslide, heat, and coastal hazards requiring preparedness, assistance, and recovery
pathways.documented_impact: Displacement, service disruption, food stress, and demand for remote delivery
pathways.fcv_mediator: Communal violence, protracted conflict displacement, insecurity, contested return, high transport costs, and implementer risk aversion
pathways.possible_consequence: Conflict-affected communities may experience slower, less complete, and more unequal climate recovery because insecurity restricts reach and return
alternative_explanations: Remoteness, limited fiscal capacity, transport scarcity, and institutional fragmentation can delay recovery independently of conflict.
pathways.uncertainty: The access mechanism is directly reported, but no national quantitative estimate of conflict's additional recovery effect is available. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict and insecurity can prolong displacement and restrict assistance, leaving affected communities more exposed to subsequent hazards and slower recovery in remote areas.

pathways.climate_pressure: Disasters and adaptation projects distributing scarce water, aid, land, infrastructure, or recovery resources
pathways.documented_impact: Resource allocation, WASH sharing, and assistance decisions with uneven local benefits
pathways.fcv_mediator: Perceived favouritism, patronage, weak consultation, unclear sharing rules, gender exclusion, and pre-existing intercommunity disputes
pathways.possible_consequence: Conflict-insensitive interventions may create grievance, mistrust, dispute, or temporary service interruption despite resilience objectives
alternative_explanations: Political competition, historic disputes, project design failure, and institutional weakness can create grievance without a climate hazard.
pathways.uncertainty: Direct local examples demonstrate possible unintended effects but not their prevalence or a national climate-conflict effect. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Resilience interventions can generate local grievance when aid, water, land, or infrastructure decisions are perceived as unfair or poorly negotiated.

pathways.climate_pressure: Repeated climate, disaster, displacement, and livelihood shocks in areas with limited formal state reach
pathways.documented_impact: Demand for information, mediation, shelter, material support, local service delivery, and recovery assistance
pathways.fcv_mediator: Trust, reciprocity, customary authority, church reach, local inclusion, identity boundaries, and unequal power
pathways.possible_consequence: Inclusive local networks can support recovery and cohesion, while strained or captured networks may exclude marginalized households
geographies: selected remote, rural, island, and customary settings
alternative_explanations: Formal public services, household wealth, remittances, geography, and external aid also determine coping and recovery.
pathways.uncertainty: Qualitative evidence does not establish uniform network strength, inclusiveness, or causal peace outcomes. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: links between local and provincial institutions
pathways.compact_statement: Local networks can bridge weak formal reach and support recovery, but their resilience and inclusiveness vary across communities and groups.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rising temperature, increasing hot-day exposure and potentially worsening drought/reduced groundwater recharge.
pathways.documented_impact: Greater water stress, heat exposure and potential agricultural pressure.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Water-access arrangements, infrastructure condition, fiscal constraints, movement restrictions, markets and institutional capacity.
pathways.possible_consequence: Could deepen food, livelihood or service insecurity where households and institutions cannot substitute water, imports, income or services; violence is not demonstrated as an outcome.
geographies: with different exposure and institutional contexts
pathways.uncertainty: Contemporary climate-to-FCV causal outcomes have not been quantified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: humanitarian WASH support and functioning institutional networks where maintained
pathways.compact_statement: Heat and drought may increase water/food stress, but FCV consequences depend on access, infrastructure, institutions and markets rather than following automatically from climate.

pathways.climate_pressure: More volatile rainfall and potentially more intense extreme events.
pathways.documented_impact: Significant modelled flood exposure in parts of the West Bank and flood/drainage risk in urban areas.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Damaged or insufficient drainage/WASH infrastructure, municipal capacity, movement/access constraints and fiscal resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: Flood events could cause greater service interruption, health risk or livelihood loss where repair and emergency access are constrained.
geographies: especially northwest/eastern and urban locations identified by the CCDR
Gaza requires a new post-destruction flood-exposure assessment
alternative_explanations: conflict damage and settlement patterns can independently determine flood losses
pathways.uncertainty: Gaza’s post-2023 asset/exposure geography invalidates many pre-conflict assumptions. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: resilient reconstruction and unrestricted emergency/service access
pathways.compact_statement: Flood hazard may become more damaging when infrastructure and delivery capacity are impaired, but current conflict damage should not itself be classified as climate impact.

pathways.climate_pressure: Sea-level rise, saltwater intrusion, warming and scenario-dependent rainfall/recharge decline.
pathways.documented_impact: Projected worsening pressure on Gaza groundwater quality and water scarcity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Aquifer over-extraction, desalination/energy dependence, conflict-damaged WASH and electricity systems, restrictions on materials/fuel and financing.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate pressure could increase the cost and difficulty of restoring safe water services and deepen reliance on external or energy-intensive supply.
affected_groups: children and communities dependent on damaged water networks
alternative_explanations: infrastructure destruction and power shortage can independently produce water-quality problems
pathways.uncertainty: No post-2023 study located isolates the incremental climate contribution to present Gaza water insecurity. The coastal/recharge component is supported by the revised CCDR record E004; the additional climate contribution to the dated humanitarian snapshot remains inferred. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: aquifer management and diversified water supply
pathways.compact_statement: Gaza’s water vulnerability is a compound system problem; climate can add pressure, but current scarcity and contamination cannot be attributed to climate alone.

pathways.climate_pressure: Future heat, drought, flood and coastal hazards.
pathways.documented_impact: Current conflict has destroyed or damaged large shares of energy, WASH, housing and other service assets.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Direct infrastructure destruction, displacement, access/material restrictions, financing constraints and institutional disruption.
pathways.possible_consequence: These conditions likely reduce the capacity to prepare for, absorb and recover from future climate shocks compared with the pre-2023 policy baseline.
affected_groups: service workers and people with health vulnerabilities
alternative_explanations: infrastructure deficits and institutional constraints limited adaptation
pathways.uncertainty: The magnitude of lost climate-adaptation capacity has not been independently quantified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Inspected 2026 Gaza reports support a prospective FCV-to-climate mechanism: conflict impairs systems needed to cope with future hazards.

pathways.climate_pressure: Increasing heat and potential drought/water stress.
pathways.documented_impact: OCHA reports current damage/removal of water infrastructure and increased emergency water-trucking dependence in specific Area C communities.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Demolitions, settler attacks, movement/access restrictions and land/grazing access.
pathways.possible_consequence: In affected herding communities, future drought could become harder to absorb because water storage, livestock watering and mobility options are already constrained.
geographies: Masafer Yatta and other documented communities
pathways.uncertainty: Current OCHA/UNICEF incidents do not themselves involve a measured drought shock, so the compound pathway remains prospective. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Damage and access restrictions can lower drought-coping capacity for specific West Bank herding communities even where climate was not the cause of the original water disruption.

pathways.climate_pressure: Multiple projected heat, drought, flood and water risks.
pathways.documented_impact: Climate investment requires substantial finance and institutional coordination.
pathways.fcv_mediator: PA fiscal crisis, revenue uncertainty, staffing constraints and pressure to prioritize immediate service and recovery needs.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate-risk screening, infrastructure investment and NDC/NAP implementation may be delayed, reduced or re-prioritized.
geographies: implications for wider Palestinian climate planning
alternative_explanations: donor priorities and incomplete project preparation may also delay climate action
pathways.uncertainty: No current climate-budget expenditure tracing was located. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: protected maintenance budgets and institutional coordination
pathways.compact_statement: Severe fiscal stress plausibly crowds out long-term climate investment, but the size of that effect is not yet quantified.

pathways.climate_pressure: No climate shock is identified as the present primary driver; pathway concerns future compound food/livelihood stress.
pathways.documented_impact: IPC reports large-scale assistance improved food-security conditions after the October 2025 ceasefire, while severe food insecurity persists and is projected to worsen.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Humanitarian access, crossing conditions, markets, supply chains and funding.
pathways.possible_consequence: Reliable assistance could buffer households against additional climate-related livelihood shocks, while access disruptions could remove that buffer.
alternative_explanations: prices and household income also affect food security
pathways.uncertainty: IPC attribution is evidence synthesis, not experimental evaluation; climate-buffering effectiveness was not evaluated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: diversified livelihoods and restored domestic food systems
pathways.compact_statement: IPC's July 2026 analysis attributes food-security improvement to assistance; any buffering of future climate shocks remains an inference, not an evaluated outcome.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rising temperature and rainfall variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Crop/livestock sensitivity and household coping pressures.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Income and food-security loss; market dependence; depletion of assets.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where households lack alternatives, livelihood deterioration could increase displacement, grievance, harmful coping or susceptibility to wider instability.
pathways.uncertainty: Complete climate -> violence chain is not demonstrated. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress can worsen livelihood insecurity, but any FCV effect is mediated by markets, assets, governance and conflict conditions rather than being automatic. (UNFCCC2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, rainfall variability, heat and changing pasture/water availability.
pathways.documented_impact: Pressure on livestock systems and possible altered seasonal movements.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Migration timing, livestock corridors, land access, water points and farmer-herder institutions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Earlier or redirected livestock movement may raise localized conflict risks where crops, routes or water points overlap and governance mechanisms fail.
pathways.uncertainty: Climate-specific contribution relative to these drivers is poorly quantified. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: customary dispute mechanisms and locally designed resource governance
pathways.compact_statement: Climate variability may modify pastoral mobility and resource contact, but governance and political-security conditions determine whether such contact becomes conflictual. (CGSpace9)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat, flood or rainfall failure/variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Potential livelihood loss and climate-sensitive migration.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Movement into areas with constrained land, services and employment.
pathways.possible_consequence: Host-area tension could increase where access and institutions are inadequate.
alternative_explanations: The current displacement crisis is primarily a direct consequence of war and violence
pathways.uncertainty: Very high for any attempt to allocate current displacement quantitatively to climate. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-sensitive livelihood mobility is plausible, but Sudan's current mass displacement must not be attributed to climate without direct evidence. (NUPI8)

pathways.climate_pressure: Background climate variability may affect production, but it is not the initiating pressure in this pathway.
pathways.documented_impact: Siege, blocked roads, destroyed water infrastructure, disrupted planting and markets.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed conflict and humanitarian/commercial access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Households can lose assets, nutrition and coping capacity, leaving them more susceptible to later drought, heat, floods and disease.
alternative_explanations: Macroeconomic collapse and pre-existing poverty interact strongly
pathways.uncertainty: Future climate consequences of depleted coping capacity are inferred. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: In current conflict zones, armed violence and access constraints are demonstrably undermining the production, food and service systems on which climate resilience depends. (IPCinfo5)

pathways.climate_pressure: Multiple existing and future climate hazards.
pathways.documented_impact: Federal implementation capacity is unreliable in current World Bank project arrangements; state/local structures and third-party actors carry delivery functions.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict, institutional fragmentation, security constraints and reduced fiscal resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate adaptation, WASH, agriculture, health and early-warning investments may be delayed, uneven or inaccessible.
alternative_explanations: Pre-war underinvestment and capacity deficiencies already existed
pathways.uncertainty: Project evidence cannot establish equal levels of impairment in every state. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: War compounds pre-existing adaptation-capacity gaps and shifts delivery toward decentralized and humanitarian structures. (UNFCCC2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Future drought, heat and rainfall variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Darfur evidence indicates conflict accelerated environmental degradation and weakened traditional environmental-management arrangements.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed violence, institutional erosion, displacement and contested resource governance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Degraded land and governance could leave livelihoods less able to absorb later climate shocks.
pathways.uncertainty: Foundational source is old; environmental degradation cannot automatically be attributed to climate. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Restored customary/resource institutions and conflict-sensitive ecosystem rehabilitation
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict can undermine the ecological and governance assets needed for later adaptation, but the evidence is Darfur-specific and partly historical. (Humanitarian Practice Network12)

pathways.climate_pressure: Water scarcity/variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Water access is a recurring livelihood and resource-management concern.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Whether infrastructure and access are shared, governed and perceived as legitimate.
pathways.possible_consequence: Jointly managed water systems could reduce friction and support community stabilization.
alternative_explanations: New water infrastructure can itself generate distributional disputes if siting
ownership or recharge is poorly managed
pathways.uncertainty: No identified evaluation demonstrates a peace outcome in the current war context. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Water projects are potentially peace-supporting only when their governance and distribution are conflict-sensitive; infrastructure alone is not evidence of peace impact. (Climate-Diplomacy4)

pathways.climate_pressure: Rainfall variability and drought.
pathways.documented_impact: A pre-war programme delivered climate information, insurance and finance-related adaptation activities and received generally positive terminal-evaluation ratings.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Household capacity to manage shocks without distress asset sales, displacement or severe consumption cuts.
pathways.possible_consequence: Better financial and information capacity could reduce erosive coping and therefore some forms of fragility exposure.
pathways.uncertainty: No peace/conflict outcome was evaluated; programme predates April 2023. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: sustained funding and accessible advisory services
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-information and risk-finance programmes show adaptation potential, but no verified evidence establishes that they reduced conflict or survived current-war disruption. (UNDP IEO Evaluation Resource Center11)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, floods and erratic rainfall described as additional yield pressures in the 2026 agri-food report.
pathways.documented_impact: Agricultural losses coexist with unsafe harvest access and disrupted pastoral livelihoods in conflict-affected areas.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Insecurity, displacement, restricted routes/water points and weakened customary institutions narrow access to land, water and inputs.
pathways.possible_consequence: These constraints can reduce the ability of farmers and pastoralists to absorb weather-related livelihood shocks and can aggravate existing resource tensions.
alternative_explanations: Input prices, finance, markets, land governance and conflict itself can reduce production and intensify tensions independently of weather.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional reverse interaction from a consultation-based 2026 report; separate effects and named climate-adaptation delivery impacts are not measured. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Customary management capacities are described as eroded, not absent everywhere; proposed water/community measures are not evaluated results.
pathways.compact_statement: In Darfur/Kordofan, insecurity and restricted land/water access narrow weather-shock coping options and can aggravate resource tensions.

pathways.climate_pressure: Participants in selected Basse-Casamance communities described irregular rainfall and environmental degradation.
pathways.documented_impact: The same participatory study reports food-access difficulties and disrupted agricultural livelihoods.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Landmines, fear and displacement restrict access to farmland and production, narrowing livelihood options under environmental stress.
pathways.possible_consequence: These constraints can leave climate-sensitive food systems less able to absorb further shocks; the interaction is conditional, not a measured joint causal effect.
alternative_explanations: Poverty, markets, salinization, deforestation and labor constraints can affect food access independently of conflict-climate interaction.
pathways.uncertainty: One purposive cross-sectional study combines respondent perceptions with historical context. It does not estimate a climate-conflict interaction, current mine prevalence or a national effect. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Participants propose reforestation, sustainable farming and stronger environmental governance; their effects were not evaluated.
pathways.compact_statement: In selected Casamance communities, mines and displacement restrict farming under environmental stress; a conditional reverse-FCV vulnerability mechanism, not climate-caused violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Coastal erosion, flooding and other climate-related environmental pressures.
pathways.documented_impact: Community research describes threatened land/livelihoods and movement away from exposed settlements.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Limited relocation land, unequal access, customary tenure and community identity shape mobility options.
pathways.possible_consequence: Relocation can generate land disputes or social tensions when access and participation are not resolved.
alternative_explanations: Education, employment and family connections also drive mobility.
Land exclusion, external project design and existing governance disputes can cause tension independently of climate.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional synthesis of selected-site research and contextual peacebuilding analysis, not a nationwide causal estimate. Source-specific examples do not establish that each mechanism occurs in every named site. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Kinship networks, local leadership and traditional knowledge.
Inclusive customary-land decisions and participation by women, young people and persons with disabilities.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate pressures can interact with relocation land constraints and exclusion to create tensions; kinship networks and inclusive local decisions can support adaptation.

pathways.climate_pressure: April 2014 flooding described in the article's Honiara case.
pathways.documented_impact: People were displaced and faced disaster-related losses.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Perceived inadequacy of government rehabilitation support generated recovery grievances.
pathways.possible_consequence: The article codes a16May 2014 protest-turned-riot; this is one historical case, not a general causal relationship.
alternative_explanations: Disaster-recovery governance and existing political grievances may shape protest independently of the flood. The aggregate study reports a null association.
pathways.uncertainty: Media-coded historical example, not an event-attribution study or quantified mechanism. Do not generalize across settlements, provinces or future disasters. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Adequate and inclusive recovery assistance is an implied governance consideration, not an evaluated intervention effect.
pathways.compact_statement: One Honiara 2014 case links flood displacement, perceived inadequate rehabilitation and a protest-turned-riot; aggregate study findings do not establish a general disaster-conflict effect.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and erratic rainfall.
pathways.documented_impact: Changed grazing movements.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Farm encroachment and resource competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: Potential violent disputes.
alternative_explanations: Tenure arrangements and pre-existing disputes also shape risk.
pathways.uncertainty: NDC prospective risk framing, not observed countrywide attribution. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: NDC-proposed land rights, corridors and inclusive mediation.
pathways.compact_statement: Changed pastoral movement may increase farm-resource disputes.

pathways.climate_pressure: Historical severe drought affecting staple production in Dry Corridor communities.
pathways.documented_impact: Smallholder harvest and livelihood losses in the programme context examined in 2019.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Low cohesion, gang-related social control and negotiated programme access can narrow collective coping and participation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Combined livelihood stress and access restrictions may undermine resilience; no causal claim that drought created gangs or a quantified increase in violence.
alternative_explanations: Civil-war legacies, land inequality, economic exclusion, gang governance and wider political dynamics independently affect insecurity.
pathways.uncertainty: Qualitative programme research from March 2019, not current territorial-control evidence or an estimated climate effect. Fieldwork sites are not a uniform risk ranking. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: The study observed communication between workers, smallholders, landowners and authorities; these reported contributions to cohesion are not an independently identified peace impact.
pathways.compact_statement: In historical Dry Corridor programme settings, drought-related harvest loss overlapped with low cohesion and gang restrictions that constrained coping and programme access; climate causation of gang violence is not established.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and rainfall failure.
pathways.documented_impact: Water/pasture depletion, livestock stress and earlier/farther pastoral mobility.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Access rules for water, grazing land and migration routes; land/resource governance; pre-existing grievances.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where governance and dispute-resolution institutions are weak or contested, increased concentrations of livestock and altered mobility may intensify local resource disputes or pre-existing tensions.
geographies: Current pastoral evidence is strongest in central/northern Somalia
conflict-pathway evidence is specifically documented in Hirshabelle/Galmudug NLA
affected_groups: farmers and communities along migration routes
pathways.uncertainty: No national evidence establishes a fixed drought -> conflict relationship; the best direct pathway study is geographically restricted. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: clear access arrangements and credible local dispute-resolution mechanisms
pathways.compact_statement: Drought-driven livelihood and mobility changes can raise local resource pressures, but whether these become conflict depends on governance, historical relations and institutions.

pathways.climate_pressure: Failed Deyr rains and continuing drought.
pathways.documented_impact: Severely reduced Deyr crop output and livestock productivity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Food markets, purchasing power, conflict disruption, currency conditions and humanitarian assistance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Combined production and market shocks may deepen food insecurity, distress coping and displacement, increasing vulnerability in already fragile communities.
geographies: with particularly severe conditions in specified livelihood zones and districts
pathways.uncertainty: IPC classifications integrate multiple drivers and do not assign an independent causal percentage to climate. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: 2026 food insecurity reflects climate-linked production stress interacting with conflict, markets, disease, services and humanitarian financing.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, with episodic flood exposure.
pathways.documented_impact: Livelihood deterioration and displacement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Settlement access, urban service capacity, land/property access, livelihoods and host-IDP relations.
pathways.possible_consequence: Large displacement flows may increase demand for water, housing, livelihoods and municipal services and can aggravate vulnerability or grievances where delivery and land governance are weak.
geographies: urban implications should be assessed city by city
alternative_explanations: poverty and established patterns of urbanization
pathways.uncertainty: UNHCR reports conflict and drought jointly; it does not allocate the “nearly 90%” figure between them or establish the downstream grievance pathway. (UNHCR Data Portal) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought and conflict jointly drive displacement; resulting FCV effects depend on urban/service and land-governance capacity.

pathways.climate_pressure: Multiple recurrent hazards requiring adaptation.
pathways.documented_impact: Need for climate planning and local delivery.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Insecurity, territorial access, institutional fragility and operating costs.
pathways.possible_consequence: Insecure or inaccessible areas may receive less consistent adaptation programming, monitoring and service delivery, producing geographically unequal resilience.
geographies: national relevance plausible but magnitude unquantified
affected_groups: Communities in insecure or hard-to-access areas
pathways.uncertainty: The observed UNDP programme-design choice cannot quantify all adaptation excluded by insecurity. (UNDP Climate Change Adaptation) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
pathways.compact_statement: Insecurity can directly narrow where adaptation programmes operate, making FCV an obstacle to climate resilience.

pathways.climate_pressure: Repeated drought/flood shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: Recurring demand for water, social protection, food-security and recovery services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Limited fiscal space, contested federal arrangements, institutional capacity and absorptive constraints.
pathways.possible_consequence: Rapidly expanding crisis/resilience portfolios may overload systems or become fiscally unsustainable even when individual projects deliver useful outputs.
pathways.uncertainty: IEG evidence is specific to the World Bank portfolio rather than all adaptation financing. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: stronger coordination and realistic absorptive-capacity assessment
pathways.compact_statement: Institutional and fiscal fragility can make climate-resilience gains difficult to sustain even where projects work.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and emerging flood risk.
pathways.documented_impact: Water, pasture and food-security deterioration.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Information flows, anticipatory financing, government/humanitarian coordination and community resource management.
pathways.possible_consequence: Earlier and better-coordinated response could protect livelihoods and services and thereby reduce some pressures that otherwise feed displacement or grievance; conflict-prevention effects are not independently demonstrated.
pathways.uncertainty: Early-warning use and preparedness activation are documented more strongly than avoided losses or conflict effects. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: scalable safety nets and coordinated crisis governance
pathways.compact_statement: Somalia has meaningful anticipatory and community resilience capacities, but their effect on FCV outcomes remains under-evaluated.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought losses described in Afgoye programme communities at 2026 endline.
pathways.documented_impact: Residents described agricultural losses and disrupted livelihoods.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Recurring armed conflict blocked access to farms and roads to markets in Jambaluul and Buula Madino.
pathways.possible_consequence: Insecurity compounds drought losses and restricts households' ability to sustain food and income access.
alternative_explanations: Input and food prices, aid changes, market demand and other livelihood constraints may also influence losses.
pathways.uncertainty: Named-community qualitative account in a non-counterfactual programme evaluation; no separate climate/conflict effect size or national extrapolation. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Water-supported gardening examples elsewhere in the programme are not assumed effective in these two conflict-affected communities.
pathways.compact_statement: In Jambaluul/Buula Madino, conflict blocked farms and market routes and compounded drought-related livelihood losses.

pathways.climate_pressure: May 2014 flooding; the study does not attribute this event to climate change.
pathways.documented_impact: Evacuated people depended on collective/reception centres during displacement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Isolated locations, inadequate lighting and a lack of continuous organized support could weaken women's protection.
pathways.possible_consequence: Potential trafficking, sexual-assault and harassment risks identified by the author; no observed incidence increase is established.
alternative_explanations: Centre design, support quality and pre-existing exclusion independently affect risk.
Historical study is not nationally representative or a current shelter assessment.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional protection mechanism from a dated event-specific study, not verified violence occurrence or anthropogenic climate attribution. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
